.claude/commands/wire-harness.md for the authoritative spec.\n- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: \"chart\", \"graph\", \"plot\", \"data viz\", \"visualization\", \"dashboard\", \"analytics\", \"visualize data\", \"categorical colors\", \"sequential / diverging palette\", \"stat tile\", \"sparkline\", \"heatmap\", \"legend\", \"axis\", \"tooltip\", \"chart colors\", \"color by series\".\n- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one - Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.\n- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.\n- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, or handing the viewer a file to save. Load it whenever any such runtime behavior would make an artifact more useful, before writing the page.\n- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors (\"from now on when X\", \"each time X\", \"whenever X\", \"before/after X\") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions (\"allow X\", \"add permission\", \"move permission to\"), env vars (\"set X=Y\"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. 1	# Cash Register
2	
3	## The Problem
4	Creative Cash Draw Solutions is a client who wants to provide something different for the cashiers who use their system. The function of the application is to tell the cashier how much change is owed, and what denominations should be used. In most cases the app should return the minimum amount of physical change, but the client would like to add a twist. If the "owed" amount is divisible by 3, the app should randomly generate the change denominations (but the math still needs to be right :))
5	
6	Please write a program which accomplishes the clients goals. The program should:
7	
8	1. Accept a flat file as input
9		1. Each line will contain the amount owed and the amount paid separated by a comma (for example: 2.13,3.00)
10		2. Expect that there will be multiple lines
11	2. Output the change the cashier should return to the customer
12		1. The return string should look like: 1 dollar,2 quarters,1 nickel, etc ...
13		2. Each new line in the input file should be a new line in the output file
14	
15	## Sample Input
16	2.12,3.00
17	
18	1.97,2.00
19	
20	3.33,5.00
21	
22	## Sample Output
23	3 quarters,1 dime,3 pennies
24	
25	3 pennies
26	
27	1 dollar,1 quarter,6 nickels,12 pennies
28	
29	*Remember the last one is random
30	
31	## The Fine Print
32	Please use whatever technology and techniques you feel are applicable to solve the problem. We suggest that you approach this exercise as if this code was part of a larger system. The end result should be representative of your abilities and style.
33	
34	Please fork this repository. When you have completed your solution, please issue a pull request to notify us that you are ready.
35	
36	Have fun.
37	
38	## Things To Consider
39	Here are a couple of thoughts about the domain that could influence your response:
40	
41	* What might happen if the client needs to change the random divisor?
42	* What might happen if the client needs to add another special case (like the random twist)?
43	* What might happen if sales closes a new client in France?
```

The exception is content that could mislead or cause harm if shared further: anything that imitates a real organization, person or record, and anything the person presented as sensitive. Claude builds those as files and lets the person decide whether they get a URL.\n\nWhen a finished piece of work is meant for other people or agents, such as a report for a team or the case for a decision the team has yet to make, Claude does not treat it as finished while it exists only in terminal scrollback or in a local file. Claude publishes it even when the request is phrased as a question, such as \"can you write up the plan?\". When the request says who else will read or use the work, such as a team, a manager or a reviewer, or where it will be posted or presented, such as a channel or a meeting, Claude publishes it. A write-up that will be posted in a channel or a thread is still published, so the post can carry the link; when it is short, Claude also gives the text in its reply, ready to paste. When it might be passed along but nothing says so, Claude offers the page in one line instead of saying nothing. When the person asks only for Claude's own verdict, such as \"should we ship this?\", and names no one else who will read it, Claude gives the answer in the terminal and offers the page in one line instead of publishing it. absent on inline-only reviews","type":"string","enum":["CONFIRMED","PLAUSIBLE"]},"outcome":{"description":"Set ONLY when re-reporting after applying fixes: what happened to this finding","type":"string","enum":["fixed","skipped","no_change_needed"]}},"required":["file","summary","failure_scenario"],"additionalProperties":false}}},"required":["findings"],"additionalProperties":false},"eager_input_streaming":true}},{"name":"ScheduleWakeup","description":"Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.\n\nDo NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.\n\nPass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.\n\nSet `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report (\"no change\", \"still waiting\", \"quiet hold\"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).\n\n## Picking delaySeconds\n\nThis session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)\n\nMatch the delay to what you're actually waiting for:\n\n- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes.   "content": "# Cash Register — .NET 10 API + React/TypeScript\n\n## Context\nRepo contains only README.md (the problem statement). Build a system that takes a flat file of `owed,paid` lines and returns one line of change per input line, e.g. `3 quarters,1 dime,3 pennies`. Minimum-coin change by default; if owed (in cents) is divisible by 3, use random denominations that still add up correctly. The design must allow a configurable divisor, new special-case rules, and other currencies (France/EUR).\n\nInterpretation: \"owed\" means the amount owed (3.33 → 333 cents, which is divisible by 3; matches the sample). All money is held as integer cents (`long`), never floating point.\n\n## Layout\n```\nCashRegister.sln\nglobal.json, Directory.Build.props, Directory.Packages.props, .editorconfig\nsrc/\n  CashRegister.Domain/      money, currencies, change strategies (no framework deps)\n  CashRegister.Application/ file parsing, processing pipeline, output formatting\n  CashRegister.Api/         ASP.NET Core 10 Minimal API\ntests/\n  CashRegister.Domain.Tests/  CashRegister.Application.Tests/  CashRegister.Api.Tests/ (WebApplicationFactory)\nweb/                        Vite + React 19 + TypeScript (strict)\n```\nUsing Vite, not Next.js: this is a single-page client with no server rendering.\n\n## Domain (extensibility points)\n- `Money` (cents + currency code), `Denomination` (value in cents, singular name, plural name).\n- `ICurrency` / `CurrencyDefinition`: loaded from config. Ships USD (dollar, quarter, dime, nickel, penny) and EUR (500€…1 cent, with the names). Adding France only needs config.\n- `IChangeStrategy`: `Minimal` (greedy, which is correct for canonical coin sets like USD and EUR) and `Random` (picks random denominations ≤ remaining until 0; the random source is injected so tests are deterministic).\n- `IChangeRule`: a list of rules, each with `bool Applies(Money owed, Money paid)` and a `StrategyKey`, checked in order; if none match, use the default. `DivisibleByRule(divisor)` takes its divisor from `appsettings` (`ChangeRules:RandomDivisor: 3`). A new special case = a new rule class plus a registration.\n- `ChangeCalculator` picks the strategy via the rules and returns `IReadOnlyList<(Denomination, count)>`.\n\n## Application\n- `TransactionLineParser`: strict decimal parsing with InvariantCulture; ignores blank lines (the sample has them); reports errors per line (bad format, paid < owed, negative) without failing the whole file.\n- `ChangeFormatter`: `1 dollar,2 quarters,1 penny` with correct singular/plural. Exact payment outputs `No change` (documented choice).\n- `ProcessFileHandler`: stream → list of line results, and a text output with one line per input line.\n\n## API (Minimal API, ProblemDetails, OpenAPI)\n- `POST /api/change/file` (multipart upload, size limit) → JSON `[{lineNumber, input, output, error}]`\n- `POST /api/change/file/download` → `text/plain` output file\n- `POST /api/change` (single `{owed, paid, currency}`) for the UI's quick entry\n- `GET /api/currencies`\n- The `currency` query parameter defaults to USD. ## Approved Plan:
# Cash Register — .NET 10 API + React/TypeScript

## Context
Repo contains only README.md (the problem statement). Build a system that takes a flat file of `owed,paid` lines and returns one line of change per input line, e.g. `3 quarters,1 dime,3 pennies`. Minimum-coin change by default; if owed (in cents) is divisible by 3, use random denominations that still add up correctly. The design must allow a configurable divisor, new special-case rules, and other currencies (France/EUR).

Interpretation: "owed" means the amount owed (3.33 → 333 cents, which is divisible by 3; matches the sample). All money is held as integer cents (`long`), never floating point.

## Layout
```
CashRegister.sln
global.json, Directory.Build.props, Directory.Packages.props, .editorconfig
src/
  CashRegister.Domain/      money, currencies, change strategies (no framework deps)
  CashRegister.Application/ file parsing, processing pipeline, output formatting
  CashRegister.Api/         ASP.NET Core 10 Minimal API
tests/
  CashRegister.Domain.Tests/  CashRegister.Application.Tests/  CashRegister.Api.Tests/ (WebApplicationFactory)
web/                        Vite + React 19 + TypeScript (strict)
```
Using Vite, not Next.js: this is a single-page client with no server rendering.

## Domain (extensibility points)
- `Money` (cents + currency code), `Denomination` (value in cents, singular name, plural name).
- `ICurrency` / `CurrencyDefinition`: loaded from config. Ships USD (dollar, quarter, dime, nickel, penny) and EUR (500€…1 cent, with the names). Adding France only needs config.
- `IChangeStrategy`: `Minimal` (greedy, which is correct for canonical coin sets like USD and EUR) and `Random` (picks random denominations ≤ remaining until 0; the random source is injected so tests are deterministic).
- `IChangeRule`: a list of rules, each with `bool Applies(Money owed, Money paid)` and a `StrategyKey`, checked in order; if none match, use the default. `DivisibleByRule(divisor)` takes its divisor from `appsettings` (`ChangeRules:RandomDivisor: 3`). A new special case = a new rule class plus a registration.
- `ChangeCalculator` picks the strategy via the rules and returns `IReadOnlyList<(Denomination, count)>`.

## Application
- `TransactionLineParser`: strict decimal parsing with InvariantCulture; ignores blank lines (the sample has them); reports errors per line (bad format, paid < owed, negative) without failing the whole file.
- `ChangeFormatter`: `1 dollar,2 quarters,1 penny` with correct singular/plural. Exact payment outputs `No change` (documented choice).
- `ProcessFileHandler`: stream → list of line results, and a text output with one line per input line.

## API (Minimal API, ProblemDetails, OpenAPI)
- `POST /api/change/file` (multipart upload, size limit) → JSON `[{lineNumber, input, output, error}]`
- `POST /api/change/file/download` → `text/plain` output file
- `POST /api/change` (single `{owed, paid, currency}`) for the UI's quick entry
- `GET /api/currencies`
- The `currency` query parameter defaults to USD. CORS allows only the Vite dev origin. Health check at `/health`.

## Web (React + TS)
- Upload a file (drag/drop) and pick a currency → a results table (input, change, errors highlighted) → download output.txt.
- Manual single-transaction form.
- Typed API client in `web/src/api/`; Vite proxy `/api` → the API.
- Tests: Vitest + React Testing Library + MSW.

## Tests (xUnit v3, Shouldly)
- Minimal strategy: the README samples (2.12/3.00 → `3 quarters,1 dime,3 pennies`; 1.97/2.00 → `3 pennies`).
- Random strategy: the sum always equals the change (property-style over many seeds).
- Rule selection: divisor config respected (e.g. divisor 5), rule ordering.
- Parser edge cases; formatter pluralization; EUR output.
- API integration: upload the sample file → 3 result lines.

## Verification
1. `dotnet build` and `dotnet test` all pass.
2. `dotnet run --project src/CashRegister.Api`, then `cd web && npm i && npm run dev`; upload a file with the README sample input → lines 1–2 match exactly, line 3 is random and sums to 1.67.
3. `npm run test`, `npm run lint`, `npm run build` all pass.
4. Add a `README` section with run instructions and design notes that answer the three "Things to Consider".

  "content": "namespace CashRegister.Domain.Currencies;\n\n/// <summary>A currency and the denominations a cashier can hand back.</summary>\npublic sealed class Currency\n{\n    public Currency(string code, string displayName, int minorUnitDigits, IEnumerable<Denomination> denominations)\n    {\n        ArgumentException.ThrowIfNullOrWhiteSpace(code);\n        ArgumentException.ThrowIfNullOrWhiteSpace(displayName);\n        ArgumentOutOfRangeException.ThrowIfNegative(minorUnitDigits);\n        ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(denominations);\n\n        var ordered = denominations.OrderByDescending(d => d.ValueInMinorUnits).ToList();\n        if (ordered.Count == 0)\n        {\n            throw new ArgumentException(\"A currency needs at least one denomination.\", nameof(denominations));\n        }\n\n        if (ordered.Select(d => d.ValueInMinorUnits).Distinct().Count() != ordered.Count)\n        {\n            throw new ArgumentException(\"Denomination values must be unique.\", nameof(denominations));\n        }\n\n        // Every amount must be payable exactly, so the smallest unit has to be present.\n        if (ordered[^1].ValueInMinorUnits != 1)\n        {\n            throw new ArgumentException(\"A currency must include a denomination worth one minor unit.\", nameof(denominations));\n        }\n\n        Code = code.ToUpperInvariant();\n        DisplayName = displayName;\n        MinorUnitDigits = minorUnitDigits;\n        Denominations = ordered.AsReadOnly();\n    }\n\n    public string Code { get; }\n\n    public string DisplayName { get; }\n\n    /// <summary>Number of decimal places in a major-unit amount (2 for USD and EUR).</summary>\n    public int MinorUnitDigits { get; }\n\n    /// <summary>Denominations ordered from largest to smallest value.</summary>\n    public IReadOnlyList<Denomination> Denominations { get; }\n}\n"
}

{
  "file_path": "C:\\dev\\CashRegister\\src\\CashRegister.Domain\\Change\\MinimalChangeStrategy.cs",
  "content": "using CashRegister.Domain.Currencies;\n\nnamespace CashRegister.Domain.Change;\n\n/// <summary>\n/// Fewest pieces, using the greedy algorithm. Greedy gives the optimal result for canonical\n/// coin systems such as USD and EUR; a non-canonical currency would need its own strategy.\n/// </summary>\npublic sealed class MinimalChangeStrategy : IChangeStrategy\n{\n    public string Key => ChangeStrategyKeys.Minimal;\n\n    public IReadOnlyList<ChangeLine> MakeChange(long amount, Currency currency)\n    {\n        ArgumentOutOfRangeException.ThrowIfNegative(amount);\n        ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(currency);\n\n        var lines = new List<ChangeLine>();\n        var remaining = amount;\n        foreach (var denomination in currency.Denominations)\n        {\n            var count = remaining / denomination.ValueInMinorUnits;\n            if (count > 0)\n            {\n                lines.Add(new ChangeLine(denomination, count));\n                remaining -= count * denomination.ValueInMinorUnits;\n            }\n        }\n\n        return lines;\n    }\n}\n"
}

{
  "file_path": "C:\\dev\\CashRegister\\src\\CashRegister.Domain\\Change\\RandomChangeStrategy.cs",
  "content": "using CashRegister.Domain.Currencies;\n\nnamespace CashRegister.Domain.Change;\n\n/// <summary>\n/// Takes a random count of each denomination, largest first. The smallest unit makes up\n/// whatever is left, so the total is always exact.\n/// </summary>\npublic sealed class RandomChangeStrategy : IChangeStrategy\n{\n    private readonly Random _random;\n\n    public RandomChangeStrategy(Random random)\n    {\n        ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(random);\n        _random = random;\n    }\n\n    public string Key => ChangeStrategyKeys.Random;\n\n    public IReadOnlyList<ChangeLine> MakeChange(long amount, Currency currency)\n    {\n        ArgumentOutOfRangeException.ThrowIfNegative(amount);\n        ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(currency);\n\n        var lines = new List<ChangeLine>();\n        var remaining = amount;\n        var denominations = currency.Denominations;\n        for (var i = 0; i < denominations.Count; i++)\n        {\n            var denomination = denominations[i];\n            var maxCount = remaining / denomination.ValueInMinorUnits;\n            var isSmallest = i == denominations.Count - 1;\n            var count = isSmallest ? maxCount : _random.NextInt64(0, maxCount + 1);\n            if (count > 0)\n            {\n                lines.Add(new ChangeLine(denomination, count));\n                remaining -= count * denomination.ValueInMinorUnits;\n            }\n        }\n\n        return lines;\n    }\n}\n"
}
```

  "content": "using CashRegister.Domain.Change;\n\nnamespace CashRegister.Domain.Rules;\n\n/// <summary>Applies when the amount owed, in minor units, is divisible by the configured divisor.</summary>\npublic sealed class OwedDivisibleByRule : IChangeRule\n{\n    private readonly int _divisor;\n\n    public OwedDivisibleByRule(int divisor, string strategyKey)\n    {\n        ArgumentOutOfRangeException.ThrowIfNegativeOrZero(divisor);\n        ArgumentException.ThrowIfNullOrWhiteSpace(strategyKey);\n        _divisor = divisor;\n        StrategyKey = strategyKey;\n    }\n\n    public string StrategyKey { get; }\n\n    public bool AppliesTo(Transaction transaction)\n    {\n        ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(transaction);\n        return transaction.Owed % _divisor == 0;\n    }\n}\n"

{
  "file_path": "C:\\dev\\CashRegister\\src\\CashRegister.Domain\\Change\\ChangeCalculator.cs",
  "content": "using CashRegister.Domain.Rules;\n\nnamespace CashRegister.Domain.Change;\n\npublic interface IChangeCalculator\n{\n    IReadOnlyList<ChangeLine> Calculate(Transaction transaction);\n}\n\n/// <summary>Picks a strategy through the ordered rules and falls back to the default strategy.</summary>\npublic sealed class ChangeCalculator : IChangeCalculator\n{\n    private readonly List<IChangeRule> _rules;\n    private readonly Dictionary<string, IChangeStrategy> _strategies;\n    private readonly IChangeStrategy _defaultStrategy;\n\n    public ChangeCalculator(\n        IEnumerable<IChangeRule> rules,\n        IEnumerable<IChangeStrategy> strategies,\n        string defaultStrategyKey = ChangeStrategyKeys.Minimal)\n    {\n        ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(rules);\n        ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(strategies);\n\n        _rules = rules.ToList();\n        _strategies = strategies.ToDictionary(s => s.Key, StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase);\n        _defaultStrategy = Resolve(defaultStrategyKey);\n\n        // Fail at startup, not on the first matching transaction.\n        foreach (var rule in _rules)\n        {\n            Resolve(rule.StrategyKey);\n        }\n    }\n\n    public IReadOnlyList<ChangeLine> Calculate(Transaction transaction)\n    {\n        ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(transaction);\n\n        var rule = _rules.FirstOrDefault(r => r.AppliesTo(transaction));\n        var strategy = rule is null ? _defaultStrategy : Resolve(rule.StrategyKey);\n        return strategy.MakeChange(transaction.ChangeDue, transaction.Currency);\n    }\n\n    private IChangeStrategy Resolve(string key) =>\n        _strategies.TryGetValue(key, out var strategy)\n            ? strategy\n            : throw new InvalidOperationException($\"No change strategy is registered with key '{key}'.\");\n}\n"
}

# /net-spec

**Phase:** 1 — specify
**Owning agent:** `.claude/agents/dotnet-spec-author.md`
**Skills used:** `ears-spec-authoring`, `issue-tracker-ingestion`, `requirements-traceability`

## Purpose
Turn raw intent (a sentence, a paragraph, or a ticket URL) into a complete EARS-style specification at `.specs/<feature-id>/01-spec.md` for a .NET 10 modular-monolith codebase.

## Inputs
Either:
- Free text describing the feature, OR
- A ticket reference (`JIRA-123`, GitHub issue URL, Linear ID, Azure work item URL).

Required. If a ticket is supplied, fetch it via the configured MCP server (see `.claude/skills/issue-tracker-ingestion/SKILL.md`) and treat its body as the source.

## Reads
- The supplied text or ticket.
- `.specs/_onboarding.md` (for stack context: solution layout, modules, target framework).
- `.specs/_stack.json` (module list, configured harness layers).
- `.claude/templates/spec.template.md`.
- `.claude/checklists/spec-review.md` (so the spec is born review-ready).

## Writes
- `.specs/<feature-id>/01-spec.md` (feature-id = kebab-case slug derived from the title, prefixed with date `YYYY-MM-DD-`).

## Process
1. Derive `<feature-id>`. Refuse if a folder with that id already exists unless the user passes `--continue`.
2. Extract: business goal, primary actor, in-scope, explicitly-out-of-scope. Name the owning module (`src/<Module>/`) and the intended vertical slice (`Features/<Slice>/`) when the source makes it unambiguous; otherwise raise a `Q-NNN`.
3. Write acceptance criteria as `AC-001`, `AC-002`, ... using strict EARS forms (Ubiquitous, Event-driven, State-driven, Unwanted-behavior, Optional). Every AC must be testable by a single xUnit test tagged `[Trait("AC", "AC-NNN")]`.
4. List non-functional requirements (latency, throughput, security posture, observability signals) with concrete numbers. If unknown, file an `Open Question` instead of guessing.
5. Record the error-shape expectation explicitly: every failure path returns `ProblemDetails`. If the source implies another error shape, raise a `Q-NNN` rather than inventing one.
6. Capture `Open Questions` as `Q-001`, `Q-002`. **Never invent answers.** Stop and surface the questions to the user.
7. Render the file using `.claude/templates/spec.template.md`.

## Refuse if
- The input has fewer than 3 distinct nouns/verbs (likely too vague — ask the user to expand).
- Any acceptance criterion would require unstated assumptions.
- An AC is compound (two behaviors in one criterion) — split it instead.

## Done when
- `01-spec.md` exists with at least one AC and zero invented answers.
- All ambiguities are listed under `## Open Questions` with `Q-NNN` IDs.
- The user has been told the next command is `/net-spec-review` (after they answer any `Q-NNN`).

# Spec Review Checklist

Used by `spring-spec-author` to gate exit from Phase 2.

## Source & framing

- [ ] Source recorded (tracker, ID, URL, snapshot date) OR explicitly marked `ad-hoc`.
- [ ] Goal is one paragraph and describes a user-visible outcome.
- [ ] Non-goals are present and explicit.
- [ ] Glossary covers every domain term used in AC.
- [ ] `## Domain Entities and Relationships` is present.
- [ ] Entities are described in business terms (no class/table/library leakage).
- [ ] Relationships include clear cardinality and business meaning.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every AC has a stable ID `AC-NNN` (zero-padded, monotonically increasing).
- [ ] Every AC follows an EARS-lite shape (ubiquitous / event / state / optional / unwanted).
- [ ] Every AC is atomic (one condition, one outcome).
- [ ] Every AC is testable (the agent can describe a Given/When/Then test for it).
- [ ] No AC contains implementation choices (class names, libraries, columns, defaults).
- [ ] Vague NFRs ("fast", "secure", "scalable") have been replaced with measurable conditions OR demoted to `Q-NNN`.

## No-invention

- [ ] Assumptions list contains only user/source-stated items.
- [ ] No silent defaults (DB engine, auth scheme, pagination, error envelope, …).
- [ ] All `Q-NNN` items are resolved or explicitly deferred-with-rationale.

## Completeness

- [ ] Source ticket's stated AC are all reflected (or explicitly excluded as non-goals).
- [ ] Out-of-band inputs (chat clarifications, screenshots) recorded under `## Out-of-Band Inputs`.

## Cutover safety

- [ ] Any user-visible cutover (migration, behavior swap, UI change) either has a feature flag with a documented rollback procedure OR carries an explicit waiver with user sign-off.

## Sign-off

- [ ] Reviewed by user.
- [ ] Verdict recorded in `02-spec-review.md` (`approve` or `request-changes`).

# EARS-lite spec authoring

## The five shapes

Every AC is one of:

| Shape | Skeleton | Use when |
|---|---|---|
| **Ubiquitous** | The system shall `<response>`. | Always-true invariant. |
| **Event-driven** | When `<trigger>`, the system shall `<response>`. | An external event causes a behavior. |
| **State-driven** | While `<state>`, the system shall `<response>`. | Behavior holds throughout a state. |
| **Optional feature** | Where `<feature included>`, the system shall `<response>`. | Conditional on configuration. |
| **Unwanted behavior** | If `<unwanted condition>`, then the system shall `<mitigation>`. | Error / failure handling. |

## Rules (enforced by `spec-review.md`)

1. **One AC = one condition + one outcome.** Split anything with "and".
2. **Stable IDs.** Format `AC-NNN`. Never renumber. Insertions get the next number, even if it breaks reading order.
3. **No implementation.** No class names, no DB columns, no library names, no defaults.
4. **No vague NFRs.** "Fast" → `< 200 ms p95 under 50 RPS` OR demote to `Q-NNN`.
5. **No silent defaults.** If the user did not say which behavior to pick, write a `Q-NNN`.
6. **Feature-flag the risky cutovers.** For any cutover, migration, or behavior swap that is user-visible, raise a `Q-NNN` asking whether a feature flag with rollback procedure is required. Default to "yes, use a feature flag" unless the user explicitly waives it.

## The Q-NNN escape hatch

When you would otherwise invent something, write:

```markdown
## Open Questions
- **Q-001** — Source ticket says "users get a discount" but does not specify whether unauthenticated users qualify. Need decision before AC-005 can be written.
```

Resolve via direct user answer, then move it to `## Resolved Questions` with the answer and date.

## Worked example

Source ticket:
> *Users should be able to apply a gift card during checkout. It should reduce the order total. If the card has been used, show an error.*

Bad (what to avoid):

> AC-001: The system uses a `GiftCard` entity with a `usedAt` timestamp and returns 400 when `usedAt != null`.

Why bad: invents a class name, invents a column, invents an HTTP status.

Good:

```markdown
## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC-001** — When an authenticated buyer submits a gift card code with their order, the system shall reduce the order total by the card's remaining balance, capped at the order subtotal.
- **AC-002** — When an authenticated buyer submits a gift card code that has already been fully redeemed, the system shall reject the request and inform the buyer that the card has no remaining balance.
- **AC-003** — When an authenticated buyer submits a gift card code that does not exist, the system shall reject the request and inform the buyer that the code is unknown.
- **AC-004** — While a gift card has remaining balance, the system shall allow it to be applied to multiple orders until the balance reaches zero.

## Open Questions
- **Q-001** — Should unauthenticated/guest checkouts be allowed to use gift cards? Source ticket only mentions "users".
- **Q-002** — Maximum number of gift cards per order? Default? (No source guidance.)
- **Q-003** — What user-facing error format does the buyer see? Banner? Inline field? (UI not specified.)
```

## Self-check before handing off to review

- [ ] Could a junior tester write a Given/When/Then for every AC without asking me a clarifying question?
- [ ] If I removed the AC, would something user-visible change?
- [ ] Does any AC contain "and" / "or" that should be two ACs?
- [ ] Are all invented details (defaults, error formats, limits) demoted to `Q-NNN`?
````

# /net-spec

**Phase:** 1 — specify
**Owning agent:** `.claude/agents/dotnet-spec-author.md`
**Skills used:** `ears-spec-authoring`, `issue-tracker-ingestion`, `requirements-traceability`

## Purpose
Turn raw intent (a sentence, a paragraph, or a ticket URL) into a complete EARS-style specification at `.specs/<feature-id>/01-spec.md` for a .NET 10 modular-monolith codebase.

## Inputs
Either:
- Free text describing the feature, OR
- A ticket reference (`JIRA-123`, GitHub issue URL, Linear ID, Azure work item URL).

Required. If a ticket is supplied, fetch it via the configured MCP server (see `.claude/skills/issue-tracker-ingestion/SKILL.md`) and treat its body as the source.

## Reads
- The supplied text or ticket.
- `.specs/_onboarding.md` (for stack context: solution layout, modules, target framework).
- `.specs/_stack.json` (module list, configured harness layers).
- `.claude/templates/spec.template.md`.
- `.claude/checklists/spec-review.md` (so the spec is born review-ready).

## Writes
- `.specs/<feature-id>/01-spec.md` (feature-id = kebab-case slug derived from the title, prefixed with date `YYYY-MM-DD-`).

## Process
1. Derive `<feature-id>`. Refuse if a folder with that id already exists unless the user passes `--continue`.
2. Extract: business goal, primary actor, in-scope, explicitly-out-of-scope. Name the owning module (`src/<Module>/`) and the intended vertical slice (`Features/<Slice>/`) when the source makes it unambiguous; otherwise raise a `Q-NNN`.
3. Write acceptance criteria as `AC-001`, `AC-002`, ... using strict EARS forms (Ubiquitous, Event-driven, State-driven, Unwanted-behavior, Optional). Every AC must be testable by a single xUnit test tagged `[Trait("AC", "AC-NNN")]`.
4. List non-functional requirements (latency, throughput, security posture, observability signals) with concrete numbers. If unknown, file an `Open Question` instead of guessing.
5. Record the error-shape expectation explicitly: every failure path returns `ProblemDetails`. If the source implies another error shape, raise a `Q-NNN` rather than inventing one.
6. Capture `Open Questions` as `Q-001`, `Q-002`. **Never invent answers.** Stop and surface the questions to the user.
7. Render the file using `.claude/templates/spec.template.md`.

## Refuse if
- The input has fewer than 3 distinct nouns/verbs (likely too vague — ask the user to expand).
- Any acceptance criterion would require unstated assumptions.
- An AC is compound (two behaviors in one criterion) — split it instead.

## Done when
- `01-spec.md` exists with at least one AC and zero invented answers.
- All ambiguities are listed under `## Open Questions` with `Q-NNN` IDs.
- The user has been told the next command is `/net-spec-review` (after they answer any `Q-NNN`).

# /net-spec-review

**Phase:** 2 — review
**Owning agent:** `.claude/agents/dotnet-spec-author.md` (review hat)
**Skills used:** `ears-spec-authoring`, `requirements-traceability`

## Purpose
Audit `01-spec.md` against the spec checklist and produce `02-spec-review.md` with a pass/fail verdict and a numbered list of required edits.

## Inputs
- `<feature-id>` (positional). (optional; if omitted, use the most recently modified `.specs/<id>/`.)

## Reads
- `.specs/<feature-id>/01-spec.md`
- `.claude/checklists/spec-review.md`
- `.claude/templates/spec-review.template.md`

## Writes
- `.specs/<feature-id>/02-spec-review.md`

## Process
1. Walk every checklist item; for each, record `pass | fail | n/a` plus a one-line rationale.
2. For each `fail`, write a concrete edit (line + replacement) the spec author must apply.
3. Verify EARS form compliance for every AC.
4. Verify each AC is independently testable (no compound criteria) and could be proved by one test carrying `[Trait("AC", "AC-NNN")]`.
5. Verify the non-functional requirements are numeric, and that every failure path is specified as `ProblemDetails`.
6. Verify `## Open Questions` is empty before declaring overall verdict `PASS`.
7. Emit summary: `verdict`, `acs_total`, `acs_failed`, `open_questions`, `next_command`.

## Refuse if
- `01-spec.md` does not exist.
- Any `Q-NNN` is unresolved — verdict must be `FAIL` with the open question list quoted verbatim (the `block-progress-on-open-questions.sh` hook enforces the same rule downstream).

## Done when
- `02-spec-review.md` exists with a verdict and a numbered edit list.
- If verdict is `PASS`, the user is pointed to `/net-plan`. If `FAIL`, they are pointed back to editing `01-spec.md`.

In most cases it returns the minimum amount of physical change, but if the \"owed\" amount is divisible by 3 the denominations are randomly generated (the math must still be right). The program accepts a flat file in which each line holds the amount owed and the amount paid, separated by a comma (e.g. `2.13,3.00`), with multiple lines expected. It outputs the change per line, formatted like `1 dollar,2 quarters,1 nickel`, with each input line producing a new output line. Sample: `2.12,3.00` → `3 quarters,1 dime,3 pennies`; `1.97,2.00` → `3 pennies`; `3.33,5.00` → `1 dollar,1 quarter,6 nickels,12 pennies` (random). Things to consider: changing the random divisor, adding another special case, and a new client in France.\n15\t\n16\t## Goal\n17\t\n18\tA cashier supplies a flat file of transactions (amount owed, amount paid) and gets back, for each transaction, the change to hand the customer, expressed as counts of named denominations. Change uses the fewest physical pieces, except when the amount owed meets the client's special-case condition (divisible by 3), in which case the denominations are chosen at random but still total the correct change.\n19\t\n20\t## Acceptance Criteria\n21\t\n22\t- AC-001: When the cashier submits a flat file of transaction lines, the system shall produce exactly one output line for each input owed.\n27\t- AC-006: The system shall format each output line as comma-separated `<count> <denomination name>` entries.\n28\t- AC-007: The system shall list denominations on an output line from - Q-007: Must random change ever differ from the minimal result, and are there constraints on it (e.g. must not always be all pennies)?
  - random change should not care about it being minimal result but the random change must be equal to the `Change` 

- Q-008: When several special-case rules match one transaction, which wins?
  -> have a Integer prirotity that is tied to the rules and Lowest Value wins.

- Q-009: How is the divisor or rule set changed: app configuration (redeploy/restart), or at runtime per client?
  -> I want the divisor to be able to change from the UI in V1. In V2 we can have app configuration 

- Q-010: How is the result delivered: a downloadable output file, results shown in the React UI, or both? Is single-transaction entry in the UI wanted?
  -> a downloadable output file that could be downloaded through a download button on a single entry of the file uploaded. 

- Q-011: What are the input limits and performance targets (maximum file size or line count, latency)?
  -> input file limit be 1000 lines, p95<500 ms

- Q-012: Is authentication required for the API or UI?
  -> None required in v1. In v2 we could have login page setup for the and jwt based authentication of the user with api.

- Q-013: What input number format is accepted (always `.` as the decimal separator even for France; thousands separators; currency symbols)?
  - have separator tied with currency. Only supported currency for v1 is us dollar.

- Q-014: Which module and slice own this feature (e.g. `src/CashRegister/Features/CalculateChange/`)?
  - a single `CashRegister` module; separate `Change` and `Currencies` modules.

- Q-015: What observability is required (logs, metrics, health endpoint)?
  -> structured logs + a health check only; add OpenTelemetry metrics.

(Q-004)\n  - AC-017: If a transaction line cannot be parsed, then the system shall output an error message on that line. (Q-005)\n  - AC-018: If a transaction line has a negative amount, then the system shall output an error message on that line. (Q-005)\n  - AC-019: If a transaction line has an amount paid less than the amount owed, then the system shall output an error message on that line. (Q-005)\n  - AC-020: If a transaction line has an amount with more decimal places than the currency allows, then the system shall output an error message on that line. (Q-005, Q-013)\n  - AC-021: If a transaction line is invalid, then the system shall continue processing the remaining lines. (Q-005)\n  - AC-022: When the input file contains blank lines, the system shall ignore them. (Q-006) Also amend AC-001 to \"…for each non-blank input line\".\n  - AC-023: If an uploaded file has more than 1000 non-blank lines, then the system shall reject the file with a ProblemDetails response. (Q-011; see NQ-003)\n  - AC-024: When more than one special-case rule matches a transaction, the system shall apply the rule with the lowest priority value. (Q-008)\n  - AC-025: When a user changes the special-case divisor in the UI, the system shall apply the new divisor to files processed afterwards. (Q-009; see NQ-001)\n  - AC-026: If a user submits a divisor that is not a positive integer, then the system shall reject it with a ProblemDetails response. (Q-009; see NQ-002)\n  - AC-027: When a file has been processed, the system shall show it as an entry in the UI's uploaded-files list. (Q-010)\n  - AC-028: When a user selects download on an uploaded-file entry, the system shall return that file's output as a plain-text file. (Q-010)\n  - AC-029: The system shall parse amounts using the decimal separator defined by the transaction's currency. (Q-013)\n- **F-002 (blocker)** — AC-015 conflicts with Q-005. Per-line errors are written to the output file, not returned as ProblemDetails. Replace with: \"AC-004: When the amount owed in cents is divisible by the active special-case divisor, the system shall select denominations using the random change behaviour.\" Add to the glossary: \"Random change behaviour — denominations chosen at random, with no requirement to differ from minimal change (Q-007).\" It is then tested through AC-005 (the total is correct) plus a deterministic random source.\n- **F-004 (major)** — Rewrite AC-003 as: \"AC-003: When no special-case rule matches a transaction, the system shall express the change using the minimum number of physical pieces.\"\n- **F-005 (major)** — AC-013 and AC-014 use the \"Where configured\" form, but the divisor is set from the UI (Q-009). Add the answer date to each resolved question.\n\n## New Questions Raised\n\n- **NQ-001** — Where does a divisor changed in the UI persist, and what is its scope? Does it survive an API restart? Is it global for all users? (Q-009 says \"change from UI\" but not where it is stored.) Options: in-memory until restart; persisted to a file or database.\n- **NQ-002** — Which divisor values are valid? Options: any integer ≥ 1 (note that 1 makes every transaction random); ≥ 2; an upper bound.\n- **NQ-003** — How long is the uploaded-files list kept? Does it survive restart? Is it visible to all users? This implies storing uploaded and processed files, which contradicts the current non-goal. Options: in-memory session only; persisted until deleted; kept for N days.\n- **NQ-004** — Q-014's answer lists both options (\"a single `CashRegister` module; separate `Change` and `Currencies` modules\"). Which one? Options: one `CashRegister` module with `Change` and `Currencies` as slices/folders; two separate modules.\n- **NQ-005** — Q-015's answer lists both options (\"structured logs + a health check only; add OpenTelemetry metrics\"). | Next step | Edit `01-spec.md`, then run `/net-spec-review` again |

**Main problems**
- **Answers not turned into criteria:** the review proposes 14 new ones (AC-016 to AC-029). They cover `No change`, error messages on bad lines, skipping blank lines, the 1000-line limit, the lowest priority winning, changing the divisor from the UI, the uploaded-files list with a download button, and decimal separators per currency.
- **AC-015 contradicts your Q-005 answer:** it says every failure is returned as ProblemDetails, but you said bad lines get an error message in the output file. Only whole-request failures should be ProblemDetails.
- **AC-004 hard-codes the divisor as 3,** which clashes with changing it from the UI.
- **Missing non-functional requirements:** the p95 < 500 ms target for a 1000-line file, logging and monitoring, and no authentication in v1.
- **Contradictory non-goal:** "no persistence or history" conflicts with keeping a list of uploaded files to download from.

**New questions (NQ-001 to NQ-005)**
1. Where is a divisor changed in the UI saved? Is it kept only until restart, or permanently? Does it apply to all users?
2. Which divisor values are allowed? A divisor of 1 would make every transaction random.
3. How long is the uploaded-files list kept? Does it survive a restart, and can every user see it?
4. Your Q-014 answer names both options. Should `Change` and `Currencies` be folders inside one `CashRegister` module, or separate modules?
5. Your Q-015 answer also names both options. Are OpenTelemetry metrics in v1 or not?

Answer these five and I'll apply the ten fixes (F-001 to F-010) to `01-spec.md` and run the review again.

# /net-spec-review

**Phase:** 2 — review
**Owning agent:** `.claude/agents/dotnet-spec-author.md` (review hat)
**Skills used:** `ears-spec-authoring`, `requirements-traceability`

## Purpose
Audit `01-spec.md` against the spec checklist and produce `02-spec-review.md` with a pass/fail verdict and a numbered list of required edits.

## Inputs
- `<feature-id>` (positional). (optional; if omitted, use the most recently modified `.specs/<id>/`.)

## Reads
- `.specs/<feature-id>/01-spec.md`
- `.claude/checklists/spec-review.md`
- `.claude/templates/spec-review.template.md`

## Writes
- `.specs/<feature-id>/02-spec-review.md`

## Process
1. Walk every checklist item; for each, record `pass | fail | n/a` plus a one-line rationale.
2. For each `fail`, write a concrete edit (line + replacement) the spec author must apply.
3. Verify EARS form compliance for every AC.
4. Verify each AC is independently testable (no compound criteria) and could be proved by one test carrying `[Trait("AC", "AC-NNN")]`.
5. Verify the non-functional requirements are numeric, and that every failure path is specified as `ProblemDetails`.
6. Verify `## Open Questions` is empty before declaring overall verdict `PASS`.
7. Emit summary: `verdict`, `acs_total`, `acs_failed`, `open_questions`, `next_command`.

## Refuse if
- `01-spec.md` does not exist.
- Any `Q-NNN` is unresolved — verdict must be `FAIL` with the open question list quoted verbatim (the `block-progress-on-open-questions.sh` hook enforces the same rule downstream).

## Done when
- `02-spec-review.md` exists with a verdict and a numbered edit list.
- If verdict is `PASS`, the user is pointed to `/net-plan`. If `FAIL`, they are pointed back to editing `01-spec.md`.

# Spec: 2026-09-21-cash-register-change-calculation — Cash register change calculation

> Owner: `dotnet-spec-author` · Phase 1 · Template: `.claude/templates/spec.template.md`
>
> **No invention.** If something is not in the source, the conversation, or the codebase, it is logged as a `Q-NNN`.

## Source

- Tracker: ad-hoc
- ID: README.md (repository root)
- URL: `README.md`, commit `9b945d3`
- Snapshot date: 2026-09-21
- Snapshot summary:
  > Creative Cash Draw Solutions wants an app that tells the cashier how much change is owed and which denominations to use. In most cases it returns the minimum amount of physical change, but if the "owed" amount is divisible by 3 the denominations are randomly generated (the math must still be right). The program accepts a flat file in which each line holds the amount owed and the amount paid, separated by a comma (e.g. `2.13,3.00`), with multiple lines expected. It outputs the change per line, formatted like `1 dollar,2 quarters,1 nickel`, with each input line producing a new output line. Sample: `2.12,3.00` → `3 quarters,1 dime,3 pennies`; `1.97,2.00` → `3 pennies`; `3.33,5.00` → `1 dollar,1 quarter,6 nickels,12 pennies` (random). Things to consider: changing the random divisor, adding another special case, and a new client in France.

## Goal

A cashier supplies a flat file of transactions (amount owed, amount paid) and gets back, for each transaction, the change to hand the customer, expressed as counts of named denominations. Change uses the fewest physical pieces, except when the amount owed meets the client's special-case condition (divisible by 3), in which case the denominations are chosen at random but still total the correct change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC-001: When the cashier submits a flat file of transaction lines, the system shall produce exactly one output line for each input transaction line.
- AC-002: The system shall preserve the order of the input transaction lines in the output lines.
- AC-003: When a transaction line has a change amount whose owed amount does not meet any special-case condition, the system shall express the change using the minimum number of physical pieces.
- AC-004: When the amount owed on a transaction line is divisible by 3, the system shall express the change using randomly chosen denominations.
- AC-005: The system shall make the denominations on every output line sum exactly to the amount paid minus the amount owed.
- AC-006: The system shall format each output line as comma-separated `<count> <denomination name>` entries.
- AC-007: The system shall list denominations on an output line from largest value to smallest value.
- AC-008: The system shall omit denominations with a count of zero from an output line.
- AC-009: The system shall use the singular denomination name when the count is 1.
- AC-010: The system shall use the plural denomination name when the count is greater than 1.
- AC-011: When the transaction line `2.12,3.00` is processed, the system shall output `3 quarters,1 dime,3 pennies`.
- AC-012: When the transaction line `1.97,2.00` is processed, the system shall output `3 pennies`.
- AC-013: Where the special-case divisor is configured to a value other than 3, the system shall apply random change to amounts owed divisible by the configured value.
- AC-014: Where an additional special-case rule is configured, the system shall apply that rule's change behavior to transactions matching it.
- AC-015: The system shall return every failure response as ProblemDetails.

## Domain Entities and Relationships

### Entities

- **Transaction** — purpose: one sale as recorded on one input line; key business attributes: amount owed, amount paid, currency.
- **Change** — purpose: what the cashier returns for a transaction; key business attributes: total amount, list of change entries.
- **Change entry** — purpose: a quantity of one denomination; key business attributes: denomination, count.
- **Denomination** — purpose: a physical note or coin; key business attributes: value, singular name, plural name.
- **Currency** — purpose: the monetary system of a client; key business attributes: code, set of denominations.
- **Change rule** — purpose: a special case that changes how denominations are chosen; key business attributes: matching condition (e.g. owed amount divisible by N), behavior (e.g. random).
- **Transaction file** — purpose: the flat file the cashier submits; key business attributes: ordered lines.

### Relationships

- **Transaction file 1..* Transaction** — one line per transaction, in order.
- **Transaction 1..1 Change** — every valid transaction yields exactly one change result.
- **Change 0..* Change entry** — zero entries when no change is due (see Q-004).
- **Change entry *..1 Denomination** — each entry counts one denomination.
- **Currency 1..* Denomination** — a currency defines its available denominations.
- **Change rule 0..* Transaction** — a rule may match any number of transactions; the first match applies (see Q-008).

## Non-Goals

- Recording or persisting sales, cash-drawer balances, or history (not in source).
- Authentication and user management (not in source; see Q-012).
- Tracking the physical stock of coins and notes in the drawer (not in source).

## Glossary

- **Amount owed** — the price of the sale, the first value on an input line.
- **Amount paid** — what the customer tendered, the second value on an input line.
- **Change** — amount paid minus amount owed.
- **Denomination** — a physical note or coin (dollar, quarter, dime, nickel, penny).
- **Minimum physical change** — the combination with the fewest pieces.
- **Random change** — denominations chosen at random whose values still total the change.
- **Special-case divisor** — the number (3 by default) that triggers random change.
- **Flat file** — a plain-text file with one transaction per line.

## Assumptions

- The initial currency is US dollars, with the denominations dollar, quarter, dime, nickel and penny (source: sample output).
- The system is a .NET 10 API with a React + TypeScript front end (user, in chat).

## Out-of-Band Inputs

- User (2026-09-21): "i want to .net core 10 API + react + Typescript system".
- User (2026-09-21): asked for the spec to be written from the README before any implementation.

## Open Questions

## Resolved Questions

- Q-001: Does "divisible by 3" apply to the owed amount in cents (3.33 → 333) or to whole dollars?
  ->  It applies to the cents.

- Q-002: Which currencies must be supported now for the "new client in France"? Does the currency apply per file, per client, or per line?
  -> US dollar needs to be supported. we need to have the solution architected in a way that adding a new currency follows open/close principle.

- Q-003: For EUR, what denomination names and output language (English or French) are expected, and are notes included?
  -> output text be english for now irrespective of the currencies. geospecific/Currencies specific output language be done in v2.

- Q-004: What should the output line be when paid equals owed (no change)?
  -> output line should have - `No change`.

- Q-005: How are invalid lines handled (malformed, negative amounts, paid < owed, more than 2 decimals)?
  -> emit the error message on that output line and continue.

- Q-006: Are blank lines in the input (as in the README sample formatting) ignored, or echoed as blank output lines?
  -> ignore for now. In V2 we can think of a status call on the file id that returns the detail of the files that processed i.e - noOfRows,emptyRow,noOfRowError,noOfRowSuccessful.

- Q-007: Must random change ever differ from the minimal result, and are there constraints on it (e.g. must not always be all pennies)?
  - random change should not care about it being minimal result but the random change must be equal to the `Change` 

- Q-008: When several special-case rules match one transaction, which wins?
  -> have a Integer prirotity that is tied to the rules and Lowest Value wins.

- Q-009: How is the divisor or rule set changed: app configuration (redeploy/restart), or at runtime per client?
  -> I want the divisor to be able to change from the UI in V1. In V2 we can have app configuration 

- Q-010: How is the result delivered: a downloadable output file, results shown in the React UI, or both? Is single-transaction entry in the UI wanted?
  -> a downloadable output file that could be downloaded through a download button on a single entry of the file uploaded. 

- Q-011: What are the input limits and performance targets (maximum file size or line count, latency)?
  -> input file limit be 1000 lines, p95<500 ms

- Q-012: Is authentication required for the API or UI?
  -> None required in v1. In v2 we could have login page setup for the and jwt based authentication of the user with api.

- Q-013: What input number format is accepted (always `.` as the decimal separator even for France; thousands separators; currency symbols)?
  - have separator tied with currency. Only supported currency for v1 is us dollar.

- Q-014: Which module and slice own this feature (e.g. `src/CashRegister/Features/CalculateChange/`)?
  - a single `CashRegister` module; separate `Change` and `Currencies` modules.

- Q-015: What observability is required (logs, metrics, health endpoint)?
  -> structured logs + a health check only; add OpenTelemetry metrics.

- (none yet)

- [x ] All `Q-NNN` are resolved or explicitly deferred-with-rationale.

  "content": "# Spec: 2026-09-21-cash-register-change-calculation — Cash register change calculation\n\n> Owner: `dotnet-spec-author` · Phase 1 · Template: `.claude/templates/spec.template.md`\n>\n> **No invention.** If something is not in the source, the conversation, or the codebase, it is logged as a `Q-NNN`.\n\n## Source\n\n- Tracker: ad-hoc\n- ID: README.md (repository root)\n- URL: `README.md`, commit `9b945d3`\n- Snapshot date: 2026-09-21\n- Snapshot summary:\n  > Creative Cash Draw Solutions wants an app that tells the cashier how much change is owed and which denominations to use. In most cases it returns the minimum amount of physical change, but if the \"owed\" amount is divisible by 3 the denominations are randomly generated (the math must still be right). The program accepts a flat file in which each line holds the amount owed and the amount paid, separated by a comma (e.g. `2.13,3.00`), with multiple lines expected. It outputs the change per line, formatted like `1 dollar,2 quarters,1 nickel`, with each input line producing a new output line. Sample: `2.12,3.00` → `3 quarters,1 dime,3 pennies`; `1.97,2.00` → `3 pennies`; `3.33,5.00` → `1 dollar,1 quarter,6 nickels,12 pennies` (random). Things to consider: changing the random divisor, adding another special case, and a new client in France.\n\n## Goal\n\nA cashier uploads a flat file of transactions (amount owed, amount paid) through a web UI. The system works out, for each transaction, the change to hand the customer as counts of named denominations, and makes the result available as a downloadable output file from the uploaded file's entry in the UI. Change uses the fewest physical pieces, except when the amount owed in cents is divisible by the special-case divisor (3 by default, changeable in the UI); then the denominations are chosen at random but still total the correct change.\n\n## Acceptance Criteria\n\n### File processing\n- AC-001: When the cashier submits a flat file of transaction lines, the system shall produce exactly one output line for each non-blank input line.\n- AC-002: The system shall preserve the order of the non-blank input lines in the output lines.\n- AC-022: When the input file contains blank lines, the system shall ignore them.\n- AC-023: If an uploaded file has more than 1000 non-blank lines, then the system shall reject the file with a ProblemDetails response.\n\n### Change calculation\n- AC-003: When no special-case rule matches a transaction, the system shall express the change using the minimum number of physical pieces.\n- AC-004: When the amount owed in cents is divisible by the active special-case divisor, the system shall select denominations using the random change behaviour.\n- AC-005: The system shall make the denominations on every output line sum exactly to the amount paid minus the amount owed.\n- AC-013: While the active special-case divisor is N, the system shall apply random change to transactions whose owed amount in cents is divisible by N.\n- AC-024: When more than one special-case rule matches a transaction, the system shall apply the rule with the lowest priority value.\n- AC-016: When the amount paid equals the amount owed, the system shall output `No change` on that line.\n\n### Output format\n- AC-006: The system shall format each change line as comma-separated `<count> <denomination name>` entries.\n- AC-007: The system shall list denominations on an output line from largest value to smallest value.\n- AC-008: The system shall omit denominations with a count of zero from an output line.\n- AC-009: The system shall use the singular denomination name when the count is 1.\n- AC-010: The system shall use the plural denomination name when the count is greater than 1.\n- AC-011: When the transaction line `2.12,3.00` is processed, the system shall output `3 quarters,1 dime,3 pennies`.\n- AC-012: When the transaction line `1.97,2.00` is processed, the system shall output `3 pennies`.\n\n### Invalid lines\n- AC-017: If a transaction line cannot be parsed, then the system shall output an error message on that line.\n- AC-018: If a transaction line has a negative amount, then the system shall output an error message on that line.\n- AC-019: If a transaction line has an amount paid less than the amount owed, then the system shall output an error message on that line.\n- AC-020: If a transaction line has an amount with more decimal places than the currency allows, then the system shall output an error message on that line.\n- AC-021: If a transaction line is invalid, then the system shall continue processing the remaining lines.\n- AC-029: The system shall parse amounts using the decimal separator defined by the transaction's currency.\n\n### Divisor setting\n- AC-025: When a user changes the special-case divisor in the UI, the system shall apply the new divisor to files processed afterwards.\n- AC-026: If a user submits a divisor that is not an integer greater than or equal to 1, then the system shall reject it with a ProblemDetails response.\n\n### Uploaded files and download\n- AC-027: When a file has been processed, the system shall show it as an entry in the UI's uploaded-files list.\n- AC-028: When a user selects download on an uploaded-file entry, the system shall return that file's output as a plain-text file.\n\n### Errors\n- AC-015: If a request fails as a whole (invalid file, over the line limit, invalid divisor), then the system shall return a ProblemDetails response.\n\n> AC-014 was withdrawn on 2026-09-21 (review finding F-005). Its intent is kept as DC-001. The ID is not reused.\n\n## Design Constraints\n\n- DC-001: Adding a new special-case rule shall not require modifying existing rules or the calculation flow (open/closed). Verified in design and code review. (Source \"Things to consider\"; Q-008)\n- DC-002: Adding a new currency shall not require modifying existing currency handling (open/closed). (Q-002)\n- DC-003: Code is organised as a single `CashRegister` module with `Change` and `Currencies` as slices/folders. (Q-014, NQ-004)\n\n## Non-Functional Requirements\n\n- NFR-001: Processing a 1000-line file completes with p95 latency < 500 ms. (Q-011)\n- NFR-002: The system writes a structured log entry for every processed file. (Q-015)\n- NFR-003: The system exposes a health endpoint that reports liveness. (Q-015)\n- NFR-004: No authentication in v1. (Q-012)\n- NFR-005: The divisor setting and the uploaded-files list are held in memory and are lost on restart. (NQ-001, NQ-003)\n\n## Domain Entities and Relationships\n\n### Entities\n\n- **Transaction** — purpose: one sale as recorded on one input line; key business attributes: amount owed, amount paid, currency.\n- **Change** — purpose: what the cashier returns for a transaction; key business attributes: total amount, list of change entries.\n- **Change entry** — purpose: a quantity of one denomination; key business attributes: denomination, count.\n- **Denomination** — purpose: a physical note or coin; key business attributes: value, singular name, plural name.\n- **Currency** — purpose: the monetary system of a client; key business attributes: code, decimal separator, allowed decimal places, set of denominations.\n- **Change rule** — purpose: a special case that changes how denominations are chosen; key business attributes: priority, matching condition (e.g. owed amount divisible by N), behaviour (e.g. random).\n- **Divisor setting** — purpose: the currently active special-case divisor; key business attributes: value (integer ≥ 1).\n- **Transaction file** — purpose: the flat file the cashier submits; key business attributes: ordered lines.\n- **Uploaded file entry** — purpose: a processed file as listed in the UI; key business attributes: file name, upload time, output file.\n\n### Relationships\n\n- **Transaction file 1..* Transaction** — one non-blank line per transaction, in order.\n- **Transaction 0..1 Change** — a valid transaction yields exactly one change; an invalid line yields a line error message instead.\n- **Change 0..* Change entry** — zero entries when no change is due, which is output as `No change`.\n- **Change entry *..1 Denomination** — each entry counts one denomination.\n- **Currency 1..* Denomination** — a currency defines its available denominations.\n- **Change rule 0..* Transaction** — a rule may match any number of transactions; when several match, the lowest priority value wins.\n- **Divisor setting 1..1 Change rule** — the divisor setting drives the divisible-by rule.\n- **Uploaded file entry 1..1 Transaction file** and **Uploaded file entry 1..1 Output file** — each entry keeps its input and its downloadable output.\n\n## Non-Goals\n\n- Persisting sales, cash-drawer balances, the divisor, or uploaded files beyond process memory (v1 is in-memory; persistence for N days is v2 — NQ-001, NQ-003).\n- Authentication and user management (v2: login page + JWT — Q-012).\n- Tracking the physical stock of coins and notes in the drawer (not in source).\n- Currencies other than USD (v2; the design must be open/closed for them — Q-002).\n- Output language other than English (v2 — Q-003).\n- A file status/summary endpoint with row counts (v2 — Q-006).\n- Setting the divisor through app configuration (v2 — Q-009).\n- OpenTelemetry metrics (v2 — NQ-005).\n- Single-transaction entry in the UI (not requested — Q-010).\n\n## Glossary\n\n- **Amount owed** — the price of the sale, the first value on an input line.\n- **Amount paid** — what the customer tendered, the second value on an input line.\n- **Change** — amount paid minus amount owed.\n- **Denomination** — a physical note or coin (dollar, quarter, dime, nickel, penny).\n- **Minimum physical change** — the combination with the fewest pieces.\n- **Random change behaviour** — denominations chosen at random whose values total the change, with no requirement to differ from minimum change (Q-007).\n- **Special-case divisor** — the integer (≥ 1, default 3) that triggers random change when it divides the owed amount in cents.\n- **Rule priority** — an integer attached to each change rule; the lowest value wins when several rules match.\n- **No change** — the output text when the amount paid equals the amount owed.\n- **Line error message** — the text written to an output line in place of change when that input line is invalid.\n- **Uploaded file entry** — a processed file listed in the UI, with a download button for its output.\n- **Flat file** — a plain-text file with one transaction per line.\n\n## Assumptions\n\n- The initial currency is US dollars, with the denominations dollar, quarter, dime, nickel and penny (source: sample output).\n- The system is a .NET 10 API with a React + TypeScript front end (user, in chat).\n\n## Out-of-Band Inputs\n\n- User (2026-09-21): \"i want to .net core 10 API + react + Typescript system\".\n- User (2026-09-21): asked for the spec to be written from the README before any implementation.\n- User (2026-09-21): answered NQ-001 to NQ-005 in `02-spec-review.md`.\n\n## Open Questions\n\n- (none)\n\n## Resolved Questions\n\nAll answered by the user on 2026-09-21; answers quoted verbatim.\n\n- Q-001: Does \"divisible by 3\" apply to the owed amount in cents (3.33 → 333) or to whole dollars?\n  -> \"It applies to the cents.\"\n- Q-002: Which currencies must be supported now for the \"new client in France\"? Does the currency apply per file, per client, or per line?\n  -> \"US dollar needs to be supported. we need to have the solution architected in a way that adding a new currency follows open/close principle.\"\n- Q-003: For EUR, what denomination names and output language (English or French) are expected, and are notes included?\n  -> \"output text be english for now irrespective of the currencies. geospecific/Currencies specific output language be done in v2.\"\n- Q-004: What should the output line be when paid equals owed (no change)?\n  -> \"output line should have - `No change`.\"\n- Q-005: How are invalid lines handled (malformed, negative amounts, paid < owed, more than 2 decimals)?\n  -> \"emit the error message on that output line and continue.\"\n- Q-006: Are blank lines in the input ignored, or echoed as blank output lines?\n  -> \"ignore for now. In V2 we can think of a status call on the file id that returns the detail of the files that processed i.e - noOfRows,emptyRow,noOfRowError,noOfRowSuccessful.\"\n- Q-007: Must random change ever differ from the minimal result, and are there constraints on it?\n  -> \"random change should not care about it being minimal result but the random change must be equal to the `Change`\"\n- Q-008: When several special-case rules match one transaction, which wins?\n  -> \"have a Integer prirotity that is tied to the rules and Lowest Value wins.\"\n- Q-009: How is the divisor or rule set changed?\n  -> \"I want the divisor to be able to change from the UI in V1. In V2 we can have app configuration\"\n- Q-010: How is the result delivered?\n  -> \"a downloadable output file that could be downloaded through a download button on a single entry of the file uploaded.\"\n- Q-011: What are the input limits and performance targets?\n  -> \"input file limit be 1000 lines, p95<500 ms\"\n- Q-012: Is authentication required for the API or UI?\n  -> \"None required in v1. In v2 we could have login page setup for the and jwt based authentication of the user with api.\"\n- Q-013: What input number format is accepted?\n  -> \"have separator tied with currency. Only supported currency for v1 is us dollar.\"\n- Q-014: Which module and slice own this feature?\n  -> See NQ-004.\n- Q-015: What observability is required?\n  -> See NQ-005: \"structured logs + a health check\"; OpenTelemetry deferred to v2.\n- NQ-001: Where does a UI-changed divisor persist, and what is its scope?\n  -> \"In memory is fine for v1.for V2 we can persist in db.\"\n- NQ-002: Which divisor values are valid?\n  -> \"any integer ≥ 1\"\n- NQ-003: How long is the uploaded-files list kept?\n  -> \"in memory for v1. we can do persisted for N number of days in V2.\"\n- NQ-004: Single module or separate modules?\n  -> \"module with `Change` and `Currencies` as slices/folders.\"\n- NQ-005: OpenTelemetry metrics in v1?\n  -> \"OpenTelementy in v2\"\n\n## Sign-off\n\n- [x] All AC are atomic and testable.\n- [x] All `Q-NNN` are resolved or explicitly deferred-with-rationale.\n- [x] Source recorded.\n- [ ] Reviewed by user on <YYYY-MM-DD> (pending re-confirmation of the revised ACs).\n"
}
