  "file_path": "C:\\dev\\CashRegister\\.specs\\2026-09-21-cash-register-change-calculation\\01-spec.md",
  "content": "# Spec: 2026-09-21-cash-register-change-calculation — Cash register change calculation\n\n> Owner: `dotnet-spec-author` · Phase 1 · Template: `.claude/templates/spec.template.md`\n>\n> **No invention.** If something is not in the source, the conversation, or the codebase, it is logged as a `Q-NNN`.\n\n## Source\n\n- Tracker: ad-hoc\n- ID: README.md (repository root)\n- URL: `README.md`, commit `9b945d3`\n- Snapshot date: 2026-09-21\n- Snapshot summary:\n  > Creative Cash Draw Solutions wants an app that tells the cashier how much change is owed and which denominations to use. In most cases it returns the minimum amount of physical change, but if the \"owed\" amount is divisible by 3 the denominations are randomly generated (the math must still be right). The program accepts a flat file in which each line holds the amount owed and the amount paid, separated by a comma (e.g. `2.13,3.00`), with multiple lines expected. It outputs the change per line, formatted like `1 dollar,2 quarters,1 nickel`, with each input line producing a new output line. Sample: `2.12,3.00` → `3 quarters,1 dime,3 pennies`; `1.97,2.00` → `3 pennies`; `3.33,5.00` → `1 dollar,1 quarter,6 nickels,12 pennies` (random). Things to consider: changing the random divisor, adding another special case, and a new client in France.\n\n## Goal\n\nA cashier uploads a flat file of transactions (amount owed, amount paid) through a web UI. The system works out, for each transaction, the change to hand the customer as counts of named denominations, and makes the result available as a downloadable output file from the uploaded file's entry in the UI. Change uses the fewest physical pieces, except when the amount owed in cents is divisible by the special-case divisor (3 by default, changeable in the UI); then the denominations are chosen at random but still total the correct change.\n\n## Acceptance Criteria\n\n### File processing\n- AC-001: When the cashier submits a flat file of transaction lines, the system shall produce exactly one output line for each non-blank input line.\n- AC-002: The system shall preserve the order of the non-blank input lines in the output lines.\n- AC-022: When the input file contains blank lines, the system shall ignore them.\n- AC-023: If an uploaded file has more than 1000 non-blank lines, then the system shall reject the file with a ProblemDetails response.\n\n### Change calculation\n- AC-003: When no special-case rule matches a transaction, the system shall express the change using the minimum number of physical pieces.\n- AC-004: When the amount owed in cents is divisible by the active special-case divisor, the system shall select denominations using the random change behaviour.\n- AC-005: The system shall make the denominations on every output line sum exactly to the amount paid minus the amount owed.\n- AC-013: While the active special-case divisor is N, the system shall apply random change to transactions whose owed amount in cents is divisible by N.\n- AC-024: When more than one special-case rule matches a transaction, the system shall apply the rule with the lowest priority value.\n- AC-016: When the amount paid equals the amount owed, the system shall output `No change` on that line.\n\n### Output format\n- AC-006: The system shall format each change line as comma-separated `<count> <denomination name>` entries.\n- AC-007: The system shall list denominations on an output line from largest value to smallest value.\n- AC-008: The system shall omit denominations with a count of zero from an output line.\n- AC-009: The system shall use the singular denomination name when the count is 1.\n- AC-010: The system shall use the plural denomination name when the count is greater than 1.\n- AC-011: When the transaction line `2.12,3.00` is processed, the system shall output `3 quarters,1 dime,3 pennies`.\n- AC-012: When the transaction line `1.97,2.00` is processed, the system shall output `3 pennies`.\n\n### Invalid lines\n- AC-017: If a transaction line cannot be parsed, then the system shall output an error message on that line.\n- AC-018: If a transaction line has a negative amount, then the system shall output an error message on that line.\n- AC-019: If a transaction line has an amount paid less than the amount owed, then the system shall output an error message on that line.\n- AC-020: If a transaction line has an amount with more decimal places than the currency allows, then the system shall output an error message on that line.\n- AC-021: If a transaction line is invalid, then the system shall continue processing the remaining lines.\n- AC-029: The system shall parse amounts using the decimal separator defined by the transaction's currency.\n\n### Divisor setting\n- AC-025: When a user changes the special-case divisor in the UI, the system shall apply the new divisor to files processed afterwards.\n- AC-026: If a user submits a divisor that is not an integer greater than or equal to 1, then the system shall reject it with a ProblemDetails response.\n\n### Uploaded files and download\n- AC-027: When a file has been processed, the system shall show it as an entry in the UI's uploaded-files list.\n- AC-028: When a user selects download on an uploaded-file entry, the system shall return that file's output as a plain-text file.\n\n### Errors\n- AC-015: If a request fails as a whole (invalid file, over the line limit, invalid divisor), then the system shall return a ProblemDetails response.\n\n> AC-014 was withdrawn on 2026-09-21 (review finding F-005). Its intent is kept as DC-001. The ID is not reused.\n\n## Design Constraints\n\n- DC-001: Adding a new special-case rule shall not require modifying existing rules or the calculation flow (open/closed). Verified in design and code review. (Source \"Things to consider\"; Q-008)\n- DC-002: Adding a new currency shall not require modifying existing currency handling (open/closed). (Q-002)\n- DC-003: Code is organised as a single `CashRegister` module with `Change` and `Currencies` as slices/folders. (Q-014, NQ-004)\n\n## Non-Functional Requirements\n\n- NFR-001: Processing a 1000-line file completes with p95 latency < 500 ms. (Q-011)\n- NFR-002: The system writes a structured log entry for every processed file. (Q-015)\n- NFR-003: The system exposes a health endpoint that reports liveness. (Q-015)\n- NFR-004: No authentication in v1. (Q-012)\n- NFR-005: The divisor setting and the uploaded-files list are held in memory and are lost on restart. (NQ-001, NQ-003)\n\n## Domain Entities and Relationships\n\n### Entities\n\n- **Transaction** — purpose: one sale as recorded on one input line; key business attributes: amount owed, amount paid, currency.\n- **Change** — purpose: what the cashier returns for a transaction; key business attributes: total amount, list of change entries.\n- **Change entry** — purpose: a quantity of one denomination; key business attributes: denomination, count.\n- **Denomination** — purpose: a physical note or coin; key business attributes: value, singular name, plural name.\n- **Currency** — purpose: the monetary system of a client; key business attributes: code, decimal separator, allowed decimal places, set of denominations.\n- **Change rule** — purpose: a special case that changes how denominations are chosen; key business attributes: priority, matching condition (e.g. owed amount divisible by N), behaviour (e.g. random).\n- **Divisor setting** — purpose: the currently active special-case divisor; key business attributes: value (integer ≥ 1).\n- **Transaction file** — purpose: the flat file the cashier submits; key business attributes: ordered lines.\n- **Uploaded file entry** — purpose: a processed file as listed in the UI; key business attributes: file name, upload time, output file.\n\n### Relationships\n\n- **Transaction file 1..* Transaction** — one non-blank line per transaction, in order.\n- **Transaction 0..1 Change** — a valid transaction yields exactly one change; an invalid line yields a line error message instead.\n- **Change 0..* Change entry** — zero entries when no change is due, which is output as `No change`.\n- **Change entry *..1 Denomination** — each entry counts one denomination.\n- **Currency 1..* Denomination** — a currency defines its available denominations.\n- **Change rule 0..* Transaction** — a rule may match any number of transactions; when several match, the lowest priority value wins.\n- **Divisor setting 1..1 Change rule** — the divisor setting drives the divisible-by rule.\n- **Uploaded file entry 1..1 Transaction file** and **Uploaded file entry 1..1 Output file** — each entry keeps its input and its downloadable output.\n\n## Non-Goals\n\n- Persisting sales, cash-drawer balances, the divisor, or uploaded files beyond process memory (v1 is in-memory; persistence for N days is v2 — NQ-001, NQ-003).\n- Authentication and user management (v2: login page + JWT — Q-012).\n- Tracking the physical stock of coins and notes in the drawer (not in source).\n- Currencies other than USD (v2; the design must be open/closed for them — Q-002).\n- Output language other than English (v2 — Q-003).\n- A file status/summary endpoint with row counts (v2 — Q-006).\n- Setting the divisor through app configuration (v2 — Q-009).\n- OpenTelemetry metrics (v2 — NQ-005).\n- Single-transaction entry in the UI (not requested — Q-010).\n\n## Glossary\n\n- **Amount owed** — the price of the sale, the first value on an input line.\n- **Amount paid** — what the customer tendered, the second value on an input line.\n- **Change** — amount paid minus amount owed.\n- **Denomination** — a physical note or coin (dollar, quarter, dime, nickel, penny).\n- **Minimum physical change** — the combination with the fewest pieces.\n- **Random change behaviour** — denominations chosen at random whose values total the change, with no requirement to differ from minimum change (Q-007).\n- **Special-case divisor** — the integer (≥ 1, default 3) that triggers random change when it divides the owed amount in cents.\n- **Rule priority** — an integer attached to each change rule; the lowest value wins when several rules match.\n- **No change** — the output text when the amount paid equals the amount owed.\n- **Line error message** — the text written to an output line in place of change when that input line is invalid.\n- **Uploaded file entry** — a processed file listed in the UI, with a download button for its output.\n- **Flat file** — a plain-text file with one transaction per line.\n\n## Assumptions\n\n- The initial currency is US dollars, with the denominations dollar, quarter, dime, nickel and penny (source: sample output).\n- The system is a .NET 10 API with a React + TypeScript front end (user, in chat).\n\n## Out-of-Band Inputs\n\n- User (2026-09-21): \"i want to .net core 10 API + react + Typescript system\".\n- User (2026-09-21): asked for the spec to be written from the README before any implementation.\n- User (2026-09-21): answered NQ-001 to NQ-005 in `02-spec-review.md`.\n\n## Open Questions\n\n- (none)\n\n## Resolved Questions\n\nAll answered by the user on 2026-09-21; answers quoted verbatim.\n\n- Q-001: Does \"divisible by 3\" apply to the owed amount in cents (3.33 → 333) or to whole dollars?\n  -> \"It applies to the cents.\"\n- Q-002: Which currencies must be supported now for the \"new client in France\"? Does the currency apply per file, per client, or per line?\n  -> \"US dollar needs to be supported. we need to have the solution architected in a way that adding a new currency follows open/close principle.\"\n- Q-003: For EUR, what denomination names and output language (English or French) are expected, and are notes included?\n  -> \"output text be english for now irrespective of the currencies. geospecific/Currencies specific output language be done in v2.\"\n- Q-004: What should the output line be when paid equals owed (no change)?\n  -> \"output line should have - `No change`.\"\n- Q-005: How are invalid lines handled (malformed, negative amounts, paid < owed, more than 2 decimals)?\n  -> \"emit the error message on that output line and continue.\"\n- Q-006: Are blank lines in the input ignored, or echoed as blank output lines?\n  -> \"ignore for now. In V2 we can think of a status call on the file id that returns the detail of the files that processed i.e - noOfRows,emptyRow,noOfRowError,noOfRowSuccessful.\"\n- Q-007: Must random change ever differ from the minimal result, and are there constraints on it?\n  -> \"random change should not care about it being minimal result but the random change must be equal to the `Change`\"\n- Q-008: When several special-case rules match one transaction, which wins?\n  -> \"have a Integer prirotity that is tied to the rules and Lowest Value wins.\"\n- Q-009: How is the divisor or rule set changed?\n  -> \"I want the divisor to be able to change from the UI in V1. In V2 we can have app configuration\"\n- Q-010: How is the result delivered?\n  -> \"a downloadable output file that could be downloaded through a download button on a single entry of the file uploaded.\"\n- Q-011: What are the input limits and performance targets?\n  -> \"input file limit be 1000 lines, p95<500 ms\"\n- Q-012: Is authentication required for the API or UI?\n  -> \"None required in v1. In v2 we could have login page setup for the and jwt based authentication of the user with api.\"\n- Q-013: What input number format is accepted?\n  -> \"have separator tied with currency. Only supported currency for v1 is us dollar.\"\n- Q-014: Which module and slice own this feature?\n  -> See NQ-004.\n- Q-015: What observability is required?\n  -> See NQ-005: \"structured logs + a health check\"; OpenTelemetry deferred to v2.\n- NQ-001: Where does a UI-changed divisor persist, and what is its scope?\n  -> \"In memory is fine for v1.for V2 we can persist in db.\"\n- NQ-002: Which divisor values are valid?\n  -> \"any integer ≥ 1\"\n- NQ-003: How long is the uploaded-files list kept?\n  -> \"in memory for v1. we can do persisted for N number of days in V2.\"\n- NQ-004: Single module or separate modules?\n  -> \"module with `Change` and `Currencies` as slices/folders.\"\n- NQ-005: OpenTelemetry metrics in v1?\n  -> \"OpenTelementy in v2\"\n\n## Sign-off\n\n- [x] All AC are atomic and testable.\n- [x] All `Q-NNN` are resolved or explicitly deferred-with-rationale.\n- [x] Source recorded.\n- [ ] Reviewed by user on <YYYY-MM-DD> (pending re-confirmation of the revised ACs).\n"
}

You'd answered the five new questions in the review file but the spec hadn't been updated, so I applied all ten fixes and your answers to [01-spec.md](.specs/2026-09-21-cash-register-change-calculation/01-spec.md), then reviewed it again.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Verdict | **PASS** |
| Acceptance criteria | 28 active, 0 failing |
| Open questions | 0 |
| Next step | `/net-plan` |

**What changed in the spec**
- **New criteria AC-016 to AC-029:**
  - `No change` when paid equals owed;
  - an error message on each bad line, with processing continuing;
  - blank lines skipped, and files over 1000 lines rejected;
  - the lowest rule priority wins;
  - the divisor changeable in the UI, with any integer of 1 or more accepted;
  - a list of uploaded files, each with a download button;
  - decimal separators tied to the currency.
- **Rewritten criteria:**
  - AC-015 now uses ProblemDetails only when a whole request fails;
  - AC-004 and AC-013 use whatever divisor is active instead of a fixed 3;
  - AC-003 was reworded.
- **AC-014 withdrawn** and turned into three design rules: adding a special-case rule or a new currency must not require changing existing code, and there is one `CashRegister` module with `Change` and `Currencies` as folders. The ID won't be reused.
- **New non-functional requirements:**
  - p95 under 500 ms for a 1000-line file;
  - a structured log entry per file;
  - a health endpoint;
  - no login in v1;
  - the divisor and uploaded-files list kept in memory only.
- **Non-goals** now list the v2 items: persistence, login with JWT, other currencies, non-English output, the file status endpoint, setting the divisor in app config, and OpenTelemetry.
- **Resolved questions:** all 20 answers are quoted word for word and dated.

**Notes for design (not blocking)**
- A divisor of 1 makes every transaction random, so the UI might warn about it.
- The wording of per-line error messages isn't specified yet; the design will define it.
- Keeping state in memory assumes a single API instance.

I've unticked the "Reviewed by user" box in the spec because the criteria changed. Please check the revised criteria, tick it, and then run `/net-plan`.

# /net-plan

**Phase:** 3 — plan
**Owning agent:** `.claude/agents/dotnet-architect.md`
**Skills used:** `epic-slicing-planning`, `dotnet-task-decomposition`, `dotnet-10-conventions`, `openapi-contract-first`, `efcore-10-data-access`, `dotnet-architecture-rules`, `dotnet-security-baseline`, `dotnet-observability-ops`, `adr-authoring`

## Purpose
Translate a `PASS`-verdict spec into planning artifacts:

- Non-Epic mode: `03-design.md` + `04-tasks.md`
- Epic mode: `03-epic-design.md` + `03a-epic-roadmap.md`, then slice-level `03-design.md` + `04-tasks.md`

Then initialize `.tdd-state.json`.

## Inputs
- `<feature-id>`. Required.
- `--epic` (optional; forces Epic mode).

## Reads
- `.specs/<feature-id>/01-spec.md`, `.specs/<feature-id>/02-spec-review.md` (verdict must be `PASS`).
- `.specs/_stack.json`
- `.specs/_onboarding.md`
- `.claude/templates/design.template.md`, `.claude/templates/tasks.template.md`, `.claude/templates/adr.template.md`
- Epic mode: `.claude/templates/epic-design.template.md`, `.claude/templates/epic-roadmap.template.md`
- All design/architecture skills above.

## Writes
- `.specs/<feature-id>/03-epic-design.md` (Epic mode)
- `.specs/<feature-id>/03a-epic-roadmap.md` (Epic mode)
- `.specs/<feature-id>/03-design.md`
- `.specs/<feature-id>/04-tasks.md`
- `.specs/<feature-id>/.tdd-state.json` (initial: no `active_task`, every task `phase: "pending"`)
- `.specs/<feature-id>/adr/ADR-NNN-*.md` for any architecturally significant decision.

## Process
1. Refuse if `02-spec-review.md` is missing or its verdict is not `PASS`.
2. Refuse if `01-spec.md` still has any `Q-NNN`.
3. Detect planning mode. Use Epic mode if `--epic` is present or the feature spans multiple vertical slices / shared cross-cutting decisions.
4. In Epic mode, write `03-epic-design.md` and `03a-epic-roadmap.md` first. Refuse to continue if either Epic artifact has unresolved `Q-NNN`.
5. Produce `03-design.md`: module map (`src/<Module>/`) and slice layout (`Features/<Slice>/`), public surface (the module's `Contracts` types — cross-module access goes nowhere else), Minimal API endpoint sketch with `TypedResults` shapes (or the full OpenAPI delta per `openapi-contract-first`), EF Core model and entity configurations, the EF Core migration plan (`dotnet ef migrations add`, reviewed as an explicit pipeline step — never applied at startup), the `ProblemDetails` error model, observability (`ILogger<T>` LoggerMessage events, `ActivitySource` spans, `Meter` counters, health checks), security touch points (authn/authz policy, CORS, rate limit, secrets), and the ArchUnitNET rule additions the slice needs.
6. For each architecturally-significant choice, write an ADR. Every overridden default and every deferred layer gets one.
7. Decompose into tasks `T-001`, `T-002`, ... per `dotnet-task-decomposition`. Each task must list:
   - `id`, `title`, `acs_covered: [AC-NNN, ...]`, `files_in_scope: [paths]`, `depends_on`, `estimated_phases: [red, green, refactor, simplify]`.
   - Tasks that touch `src/<Module>/**` MUST list at least one file under `tests/<Module>.Tests/**` or `tests/<Module>.IntegrationTests/**` in `files_in_scope`.
   - Per-task gates: `unit` always; `it` when the task needs a container or the full host; `coverage` on every task that adds production lines.
8. Validate AC coverage: every AC from `01-spec.md` must appear in at least one task. If not, FAIL the plan and surface the gap.
9. Initialize `.tdd-state.json` — `tasks` is a map keyed by task id, with a top-level `active_task`. An array shape is rejected by the hooks.
   ```json
   { "active_task": null, "tasks": { "T-001": { "phase": "pending", "files_in_scope": [...], "acs_covered": [...] } } }
   ```

## Refuse if
- Spec review verdict is not `PASS`.
- Epic mode is active and either Epic artifact is missing.
- Any AC has no covering task.
- Any task touches `src/<Module>/**` without a corresponding `tests/<Module>.Tests/**` or `tests/<Module>.IntegrationTests/**` file in scope.
- A task's `files_in_scope` would be so broad that `enforce-files-in-scope.sh` stops being a meaningful boundary (e.g. a whole module directory).
- A design decision was made without an ADR where a default is overridden.

## Done when
- `03-design.md`, `04-tasks.md`, any ADRs, and `.tdd-state.json` are written.
- `.tdd-state.json` uses the keyed-map shape with `active_task: null`.
- The user is pointed to `/net-build T-001`.

# .NET Task Decomposition

## Sizing rule

Each task is **1–4 hours** for a competent engineer. If larger, split. If smaller than 30 minutes,
fold into the previous task.

## Shape

A good task has all of:

1. **Stable ID** `T-NNN`. Never renumber.
2. **Linked AC-IDs** — what user-visible criteria this task moves forward.
3. **Test-IDs** — at least one (`T-NNN-T1`, `T-NNN-T2`).
4. **Files in scope** — every path the task is allowed to edit, **production and tests**.
5. **Dependencies** — `T-NNN` IDs that must be `done` first.
6. **Gates** — which gates from `artifacts/harness-summary.json` run for this task.
7. **Rollback** — one sentence on how to revert if validation fails.

## Files in scope: the test path is mandatory

`files_in_scope` lists paths in .NET shapes:

```
src/Ordering/Features/Orders/CreateOrderEndpoint.cs
src/Ordering/Features/Orders/CreateOrderHandler.cs
tests/Ordering.Tests/Features/Orders/CreateOrderTests.cs
tests/Ordering.IntegrationTests/Features/Orders/CreateOrderEndpointTests.cs
```

**Every task must include the test path.** This is not a style preference.
`.claude/hooks/enforce-files-in-scope.sh` now blocks an edit to any file the active task has not
declared — **including test files**. A task whose `files_in_scope` names only production paths
cannot be built at all: the red step is the first thing `/build` does, and the hook rejects the
test file before a single line is written. The task is dead on arrival and must be re-planned.

So, for every task:

- At least one `tests/<Module>.Tests/...` path, or a `tests/<Module>.IntegrationTests/...` path
  when the task's proof is an integration test.
- Concrete paths, never globs. `tests/Ordering.Tests/**` will not satisfy the hook.
- The path as it will exist, including the mirrored `Features/<Slice>/` folder.
- A refactor-only task still declares the test files it will touch, even if it only re-runs them.

## Migrations are always their own task

EF Core migration work never rides along inside a feature task.

- One task per migration, ordered **before** any task that depends on the new schema.
- `files_in_scope` includes the generated migration files —
  `src/Ordering/Migrations/20260920120000_AddOrderLineTotals.cs`, its `.Designer.cs`, and
  `src/Ordering/Migrations/ShopDbContextModelSnapshot.cs` — plus the changed entity/configuration
  and the migration's own test.
- Gates: `unit` and `it` (the integration gate is what actually applies the migration against a
  Testcontainers Postgres).
- Rollback: `dotnet ef migrations remove`, plus reverting the entity change.
- Never `EnsureCreated()`. Never edit a migration that has already been released.

## Greenfield: the scaffold task comes first and carries no AC

The first task of a greenfield feature is the project/solution scaffold. It is the one task with
an empty `AC-IDs` list, because it delivers no user-visible behavior.

`files_in_scope` for the scaffold:

auto-format-touched.sh
block-impl-without-failing-test.sh
block-progress-on-open-questions.sh
enforce-files-in-scope.sh
forbid-skip-flags.sh
lib
log-tdd-state-transition.sh
route-natural-language-aliases.sh
````

Its proof is a smoke test that the solution builds and the test host runs — so it still has a
test path, and its gate is `unit` only. Refactor-only tasks are the other exception to the
AC rule; **every other task maps to at least one AC.**

## Gates per task

Name the gates exactly as they appear in `artifacts/harness-summary.json`:

| Gate | Runs | Put it on a task when |
|---|---|---|
| `unit` | xUnit v3 tests without `[Trait("Category","Integration")]` | Always. Every task. |
| `it` | tests with `[Trait("Category","Integration")]` — `WebApplicationFactory`, Testcontainers, Respawn | The task adds a migration, an endpoint, or anything crossing a process boundary. |
| `coverage` | Cobertura at `artifacts/coverage/cobertura.xml`; 0.90 floor, 0.95 on new code | Every task that adds production code. |
| `mutation` | Stryker.NET, 0.75 kill rate — `skipped` unless `stryker-config.json` exists | Only when the repo has opted in. Otherwise omit it; a `skipped` gate is not a task concern. |

## Ordering rules

Dependencies flow inward. In order:

1. **Scaffold** (greenfield only).
2. **Contract and migration** — request/response DTOs, validators, domain types; EF Core
   migration as its own task.
3. **Handler** — the business logic, unit-tested in isolation with NSubstitute doubles.
4. **Endpoint** — the Minimal API mapping, `TypedResults`, the validation filter wiring.
5. **Integration test** — `WebApplicationFactory` + Testcontainers through the real endpoint.
6. **Cross-cutting** — ArchUnitNET rules, observability, ProblemDetails shape.

Contract and migration before handler. Handler before endpoint. Endpoint before integration test.
Two tasks never edit the same file in parallel — serialize them with a dependency.
**One task touches one slice.** A change spanning `Features/Orders` and `Features/Payments` is
two tasks plus a contract task, not one.

## Worked example — "Create order with line totals"

```markdown
### T-001 — Scaffold the Ordering module and test projects
- **AC-IDs:** none (scaffold)
- **Test-IDs:** T-001-T1 (solution builds; test host discovers zero-failure suite)
- **Files in scope:**
  - `global.json`
  - `Directory.Build.props`
  - `Directory.Packages.props`
  - `Shop.sln`
  - `src/Ordering/Ordering.csproj`
  - `tests/Ordering.Tests/Ordering.Tests.csproj`
  - `tests/Ordering.IntegrationTests/Ordering.IntegrationTests.csproj`
  - `tests/Ordering.Tests/ScaffoldSmokeTests.cs`
- **Dependencies:** none
- **Gates:** unit
- **Rollback:** delete the solution and both project folders.

### T-002 — `CreateOrderRequest` DTO + FluentValidation rules
- **AC-IDs:** AC-001, AC-004
- **Test-IDs:** T-002-T1 (rejects blank reference), T-002-T2 (rejects >100 lines), T-002-T3 (caps reference at 32 chars)
- **Files in scope:**
  - `src/Ordering/Features/Orders/CreateOrderRequest.cs`
  - `src/Ordering/Features/Orders/CreateOrderRequestValidator.cs`
  - `tests/Ordering.Tests/Features/Orders/CreateOrderRequestValidatorTests.cs`
- **Dependencies:** T-001
- **Gates:** unit, coverage
- **Rollback:** delete the three files; nothing references them yet.

### T-003 — EF Core migration `AddOrderLineTotals`
- **AC-IDs:** AC-002
- **Test-IDs:** T-003-T1 (migration applies to an empty Postgres container and the snapshot round-trips)
- **Files in scope:**
  - `src/Ordering/Domain/OrderLine.cs`
  - `src/Ordering/Persistence/OrderLineConfiguration.cs`
  - `src/Ordering/Migrations/20260920120000_AddOrderLineTotals.cs`
  - `src/Ordering/Migrations/20260920120000_AddOrderLineTotals.Designer.cs`
  - `src/Ordering/Migrations/ShopDbContextModelSnapshot.cs`
  - `tests/Ordering.IntegrationTests/Persistence/MigrationTests.cs`
- **Dependencies:** T-001
- **Gates:** unit, it
- **Rollback:** `dotnet ef migrations remove`, revert the entity and configuration.

### T-004 — `CreateOrderHandler` computes line totals and order total
- **AC-IDs:** AC-002, AC-003
- **Test-IDs:** T-004-T1 (sums line totals), T-004-T2 (applies member discount at the £100 boundary), T-004-T3 (returns NotFound result for an unknown customer)
- **Files in scope:**
  - `src/Ordering/Features/Orders/CreateOrderHandler.cs`
  - `src/Ordering/Features/Orders/CreateOrderResult.cs`
  - `tests/Ordering.Tests/Features/Orders/CreateOrderHandlerTests.cs`
- **Dependencies:** T-002, T-003
- **Gates:** unit, coverage
- **Rollback:** delete the handler and result type; T-005 is not yet written.

### T-005 — `POST /api/orders` endpoint with TypedResults and ProblemDetails
- **AC-IDs:** AC-001, AC-005
- **Test-IDs:** T-005-T1 (201 + Location on success), T-005-T2 (400 ProblemDetails on validation failure), T-005-T3 (404 ProblemDetails for unknown customer)
- **Files in scope:**
  - `src/Ordering/Features/Orders/CreateOrderEndpoint.cs`
  - `src/Ordering/OrderingEndpoints.cs`
  - `tests/Ordering.Tests/Features/Orders/CreateOrderEndpointTests.cs`
- **Dependencies:** T-004
- **Gates:** unit, coverage
- **Rollback:** remove the map call from `OrderingEndpoints`; delete the endpoint file.

### T-006 — Integration test: create order end to end
- **AC-IDs:** AC-001, AC-002, AC-003, AC-005
- **Test-IDs:** T-006-T1 (persists order and lines), T-006-T2 (409 on duplicate reference), T-006-T3 (401 when unauthenticated)
- **Files in scope:**
  - `tests/Ordering.IntegrationTests/Features/Orders/CreateOrderEndpointTests.cs`
  - `tests/Ordering.IntegrationTests/OrderingApiFixture.cs`
- **Dependencies:** T-005
- **Gates:** unit, it, coverage
- **Rollback:** delete both test files.

### T-007 — Authorization policy and rate limit for the orders group

Everything else is `internal` (with `InternalsVisibleTo` for the test projects).\n- `Features/Currencies` depends on nothing in `Features/Change`.\n- `Features/Change` depends on `Features/Currencies` only through `Currency`, `Denomination` and `ICurrencyRegistry`.\n- `CashRegister.Api` references only `CashRegister` and calls only `AddCashRegister` / `MapCashRegister`.\n\nArchUnitNET rules added in T-012:\n1. `Features.Currencies` must not depend on `Features.Change`.\n2. `CashRegister` (module) must not depend on `CashRegister.Api`.\n3. Every class implementing `IChangeRule` must be `sealed` and live in `Features.Change.Rules` (DC-001).\n4. No type in the module calls `DateTime.Now`/`UtcNow`; use `TimeProvider`.\n5. Types in `Features/*` must not reference `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http` except types whose name ends in `Endpoints`.\n\n## Entity Relationship Model\n\n| Entity | Purpose | Key attributes | Relationships | Persistence notes |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| Transaction | one parsed line | owed, paid (long minor units), currency | 0..1 Change | transient |\n| ChangeLine | count of one denomination | denomination, count | *..1 Denomination | transient |\n| Denomination | coin or note | value, singular, plural | *..1 Currency | static per currency class |\n| Currency | monetary system | code, decimal separator, minor digits | 1..* Denomination | DI singleton |\n| Change rule | special case | priority, strategy, condition | 0..* Transaction | DI singleton |\n| Divisor setting | active divisor | value ≥ 1, default 3 | drives OwedDivisibleByRule | in-memory singleton (ADR-002) |\n| Uploaded file | processed file | id (Guid), file name, uploaded at, line count, error count, output text | 1..1 output | in-memory `ConcurrentDictionary` (ADR-002) |\n\n## API Sketch (Minimal API, OpenAPI via `Microsoft.AspNetCore.OpenApi` at `/openapi/v1.json`)\n\n```yaml\npaths:\n  /api/files:\n    post:   # multipart/form-data, field \"file\"\n      responses:\n        '201': { UploadedFileSummary, Location: /api/files/{id} }       # AC-027\n        '400': { ProblemDetails }  # no file / empty name / > 1000 non-blank lines (AC-015, AC-023)\n    get:\n      responses:\n        '200': { UploadedFileSummary[] (newest first) }                  # AC-027\n  /api/files/{id}/output:\n    get:\n      responses:\n        '200': { text/plain; Content-Disposition: attachment; filename=\"<name>-change.txt\" }  # AC-028\n        '404': { ProblemDetails }\n  /api/settings/divisor:\n    get:  { '200': { divisor: int } }\n    put:  # body { divisor: int }\n      responses:\n        '200': { divisor: int }                                         # AC-025\n        '400': { ProblemDetails / HttpValidationProblemDetails }        # AC-026, AC-015\n  /health:  { '200': Healthy }                                          # NFR-003\n```\n\n`UploadedFileSummary = { id, fileName, uploadedAt, lineCount, errorLineCount }`.\n\nReturns are declared as `Results<Created<UploadedFileSummary>, ProblemHttpResult>`, `Results<FileContentHttpResult, NotFound<ProblemDetails>>` and so on. Divisor validation uses .NET 10 built-in Minimal API validation (`AddValidation()` + `[Range(1, int.MaxValue)]`). A non-integer JSON body fails binding, which yields a 400 ProblemDetails through `AddProblemDetails()`.\n\n## Processing Flow\n\n1. The endpoint reads the `IFormFile` stream.\n2. `ChangeFileProcessor.Process(stream, currency)` reads line by line and skips whitespace-only lines (AC-022). Once more than 1000 non-blank lines are seen, it returns `LineLimitExceeded` and stops reading (AC-023).\n3. For each line, `TransactionLineParser`:\n   - returns a `Transaction`, or `Error: …` text (AC-017–AC-020) and processing continues (AC-021);\n   - otherwise `ChangeCalculator` produces the lines and `ChangeFormatter` renders them (`No change` when due is 0, AC-016).\n4. The output joins lines with `\\n` in input order (AC-001, AC-002; ADR-007), is stored in `IUploadedFileStore` with `TimeProvider.GetUtcNow()`, a log event is written (NFR-002), and the endpoint returns 201.\n\nParsing (USD, ADR-004): the field separator is `,`; exactly 2 fields after trimming; the decimal separator comes from the currency (`.` for USD); at most `MinorUnitDigits` decimal places (2); no thousands separators or currency symbols; `-` gives the negative-amount error (AC-018).\n\n## Line Error Messages (ADR-007)\n\n| Condition | Output line |\n|---|---|\n| not exactly two fields / not a number | `Error: invalid line, expected '<owed>,<paid>'` |\n| negative amount | `Error: amounts must not be negative` |\n| paid < owed | `Error: amount paid is less than amount owed` |\n| too many decimals | `Error: amounts must have at most 2 decimal places` |\n\n## Data Model + Migrations\n\n- No database in v1 (ADR-002): no EF Core, no `DbContext`, no migrations. The persistence layer is deferred to v2 (\"persist in db\", \"N days\"). The store interfaces are the seam.\n\n## ProblemDetails Error Model\n\n- `builder.Services.AddProblemDetails()`, `app.UseExceptionHandler()`, `app.UseStatusCodePages()`. Unhandled exceptions return 500 ProblemDetails with no stack trace outside Development.\n- Endpoint failures use `TypedResults.Problem(title, detail, statusCode)` with stable titles: `Invalid file`, `Too many lines`, `File not found`, `Invalid divisor`.\n- Per-line errors are data in the output, not ProblemDetails (spec AC-015 vs Q-005).\n\n## Security Posture (ADR-005)\n\n- AuthN/AuthZ: none in v1 (NFR-004); endpoints are anonymous. JWT arrives in v2.\n- CORS: a named policy allowing only the origins in `Cors:AllowedOrigins` (Development: `http://localhost:5173`). Production serves the SPA behind the same origin.\n- Request limits: `FormOptions.MultipartBodyLengthLimit` and the upload endpoint's `RequestSizeLimit` are 1 MB. 1000 lines × a generous 64 bytes ≈ 64 KB, so 1 MB guards memory without rejecting valid files.\n- Input: file content is treated as data only; the file name is sanitised for `Content-Disposition` (path chars stripped, max 100 chars).\n- PII: none. Secrets: none.\n\n## Observability (ADR-008)\n\n- `CashRegisterLog` (LoggerMessage source-generated):\n  - `FileProcessed(Guid fileId, string fileName, int lineCount, int errorLineCount, long elapsedMs)`, Information (NFR-002)\n  - `FileRejected(string fileName, string reason)`, Warning\n  - `DivisorChanged(int oldValue, int newValue)`, Information\n- `builder.Services.AddHealthChecks()` → `app.MapHealthChecks(\"/health\")` (NFR-003).\n- JSON console logging in non-Development environments.\n\n## Front End (ADR-006)\n\n`web/src/`:\n- `api/client.ts`: typed `fetch` wrappers `uploadFile`, `listFiles`, `outputUrl(id)`, `getDivisor`, `setDivisor`; ProblemDetails is parsed into a `ApiError`.\n- `features/divisor/DivisorSettings.tsx`: number input with a \"Save\" button; shows server ProblemDetails errors and warns when the value is 1 (AC-025, AC-026).\n- `features/files/FileUpload.tsx`: file input and upload; shows the ProblemDetails error (AC-023).\n- `features/files/UploadedFilesList.tsx`: table (name, uploaded at, lines, errors) with a Download button per entry that opens `outputUrl(id)` (AC-027, AC-028).\n- `App.tsx` composes them; `vite.config.ts` proxies `/api` and `/health` to the API.\n\n## Risks + Rollback\n\n| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation | Rollback |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| The in-memory file store grows without bound | medium | memory | 1 MB request cap, 1000 lines; restart clears it (NFR-005); v2 adds retention | restart the process |\n| Multiple API instances diverge on divisor/files | low (v1 single instance) | inconsistent UX | document single-instance deployment in ADR-002 | n/a |\n| A future currency uses `,` as its decimal separator, which clashes with the `,` field separator | medium (v2 EUR) | parse ambiguity | ADR-004: the field separator becomes per-currency (e.g. `;`) when such a currency is added | n/a for v1 |\n| Divisor = 1 makes every line random | low | surprise | UI warning (spec review note) | set the divisor back to 3 |\n| p95 regression | low | NFR-001 | integration perf test (T-012) | revert the offending commit |\n\n## Non-Functional Requirements\n\n- NFR-001: p95 < 500 ms for a 1000-line upload. Verified by `FileUploadPerformanceTests` (50 sequential uploads in-process after warm-up; the 95th percentile is asserted).\n- NFR-002: `FileProcessed` log event. Verified with `FakeLogger` in a unit test.\n- NFR-003: `/health` returns 200. Integration test.\n- NFR-004: no auth. Integration tests call without credentials.\n- NFR-005: in-memory state. By construction (ADR-002).\n\n## Open Questions\n\n- (none)\n\n## Resolved Questions\n\n- (none; all design choices beyond the spec are recorded as ADRs for user review)\n\n## Sign-off\n\n- [x] Every AC from `01-spec.md` is addressed by at least one component or task (see the coverage table in `04-tasks.md`).\n- [x] All `Q-NNN` resolved or deferred-with-rationale.\n- [ ] Reviewed by user on <YYYY-MM-DD>.\n"
}

The module takes a `FrameworkReference` to `Microsoft.AspNetCore.App` in order to map its endpoints.\n\n## Links\n\n- Source: `01-spec.md` DC-003, NQ-004\n"

  "content": "# ADR-003: Change rules + strategies pipeline, integer minor units, random algorithm\n\n- **Status:** accepted\n- **Date:** 2026-09-21\n- **Deciders:** user, `dotnet-architect`\n\n## Context and problem statement\n\nThe client wants a configurable random divisor, more special cases later, and a lowest-priority-wins resolution (Q-008). Adding a rule must not change existing code (DC-001). The money arithmetic must be exact (AC-005).\n\n## Decision drivers\n\n- DC-001 (open/closed), AC-024, AC-005.\n- Deterministic tests for random behaviour.\n\n## Considered options\n\n1. An `if/else` inside one calculator.\n2. `IChangeRule { int Priority; Type StrategyType; bool Matches(Transaction) }` together with `IChangeStrategy` implementations. Both are registered in DI; `ChangeCalculator` picks the lowest-priority matching rule, or the minimal strategy when none matches.\n3. A rules engine library.\n\n## Decision outcome\n\nChosen option: **Option 2**.\n\n- Amounts are held as `long` minor units (cents); `decimal` is used only while parsing. There is no floating point.\n- If two rules have the same priority, registration order breaks the tie. A startup check rejects a rule whose strategy is not registered.\n- The random strategy walks the denominations from largest to smallest. For each denomination except the smallest it takes `Random.NextInt64(0, remaining / value + 1)`; the smallest unit takes the remainder. The total is therefore always exact. The result may coincide with the minimal result, which is allowed (Q-007). `Random` is injected (`Random.Shared` in production, a seeded instance in tests).\n\n### Consequences\n\n- Positive: a new special case is one new sealed class plus one DI registration.\n- Negative: the random distribution is biased toward small coins at the end. This is acceptable because the spec only requires the total to be correct.\n\n## Links\n\n- Source: `01-spec.md` AC-003, AC-004, AC-005, AC-013, AC-024, DC-001, Q-007, Q-008\n"
}
```

}

  "content": "# ADR-007: Output file format and line error wording\n\n- **Status:** accepted\n- **Date:** 2026-09-21\n- **Deciders:** user, `dotnet-architect`\n\n## Context and problem statement\n\nThe spec says invalid lines \"emit the error message on that output line\" (Q-005) but does not fix the wording. The line terminator and download file name are also unspecified.\n\n## Decision outcome\n\n- Output lines are joined with `\\n` (LF), with no trailing newline. It is UTF-8 without a BOM, `text/plain; charset=utf-8`.\n- The download file name is `<original name without extension>-change.txt`.\n- Every line error starts with `Error: ` so the cashier and any tooling can spot it:\n  - `Error: invalid line, expected '<owed>,<paid>'`\n  - `Error: amounts must not be negative`\n  - `Error: amount paid is less than amount owed`\n  - `Error: amounts must have at most 2 decimal places` (the digit count comes from the currency)\n- When no change is due, the line is `No change` (AC-016).\n- Checks run in this order: format, then negative, then decimals, then paid < owed. The first failing check wins.\n\n### Consequences\n\n- The user may change the wording at design review. The tests assert these exact strings.\n\n## Links\n\n- Source: `01-spec.md` AC-016 to AC-020, Q-004, Q-005\n"
}

## Assistant · 2026-09-21T16:57:24.886Z

I've written the plan. All 28 active acceptance criteria map to at least one task, and every task that touches `src/CashRegister/` lists a test file too. Everything is in [.specs/2026-09-21-cash-register-change-calculation/](.specs/2026-09-21-cash-register-change-calculation/):

- **Design:** [03-design.md](.specs/2026-09-21-cash-register-change-calculation/03-design.md)
- **Tasks:** [04-tasks.md](.specs/2026-09-21-cash-register-change-calculation/04-tasks.md)
- **Decisions:** 8 ADRs in [adr/](.specs/2026-09-21-cash-register-change-calculation/adr/)
- **Build state:** `.tdd-state.json`, generated from `04-tasks.md` so the two can't drift apart. No task is active yet and all 16 are pending.

**Design in short**
- **Layout:** one `CashRegister` module with `Features/Currencies` and `Features/Change` folders, a thin `CashRegister.Api` host, unit and integration test projects, and a Vite React front end in `web/`.
- **Money:** held as whole cents throughout, never floating point.
- **Special cases:** each rule has an integer priority and the lowest wins. When no rule matches, the fewest-coins method is used. A new rule or currency is one new class plus one registration.
- **Endpoints:**
  - `POST /api/files` and `GET /api/files` to upload and list files;
  - `GET /api/files/{id}/output` to download the result;
  - `GET` and `PUT /api/settings/divisor` to read and change the divisor;
  - `/health`.
- **Storage:** everything is in memory, so there is no database or EF Core in v1.

**Choices I made that you should check.** These go beyond the spec and are recorded as ADRs.

| ADR | Decision |
|---|---|
| 001 | Deletes the first-pass projects I scaffolded earlier (`Domain`, `Application`, and three test projects), which don't fit the single-module layout you chose. |
| 004 | Files are processed in USD, set in app config. There is no currency picker on upload, because the spec doesn't ask for one. |
| 005 | CORS allows only the dev front end, and uploads are capped at 1 MB. Rate limiting is deferred to v2 alongside login. |
| 006 | The front end uses Vite instead of the toolkit's default, Next.js, because there's no server-side rendering need. |
| 007 | Exact error wording on bad lines, e.g. `Error: amount paid is less than amount owed`. Output lines end in `\n`, and the download is named `<name>-change.txt`. |

**Build order**

| Tasks | What they build |
|---|---|
| T-001 | Project scaffold |
| T-002 to T-004 | Currencies, then the fewest-coins and random change methods |
| T-005 | Rules and the divisor setting |
| T-006 and T-007 | Output formatting and line parsing |
| T-008 | File processing |
| T-009 to T-011 | API host and endpoints |
| T-012 | Architecture rules and the p95 < 500 ms test |
| T-013 to T-015 | Front end |
| T-016 | README |

If you're happy with the ADRs, tick the sign-off boxes in `03-design.md` and `04-tasks.md`, then run `/net-build T-001`.

## User · 2026-09-21T16:58:45.282Z

# /net-build

**Phase:** 4 — build (TDD)
**Owning agent:** `.claude/agents/dotnet-implementer.md` (collaborates with `dotnet-test-engineer`)
**Skills used:** `tdd-red-green-refactor`, `dotnet-10-conventions`, `clarity-over-cleverness`, `dotnet-testing-patterns`, `dotnet-task-decomposition`

## Purpose
Execute one task end-to-end through the four TDD phases (red → green → refactor → simplify), updating `.tdd-state.json` and appending a block to `05-implementation-log.md` after each phase.

## Inputs
- `<task-id>` (e.g. `T-001`). Required.

## Reads
- `.specs/<feature-id>/04-tasks.md`
- `.specs/<feature-id>/03-design.md`
- `.specs/<feature-id>/.tdd-state.json`
- `.claude/skills/tdd-red-green-refactor/SKILL.md` (authoritative)
- `.claude/skills/dotnet-testing-patterns/SKILL.md` (scope selection and the `[Trait("AC", ...)]` contract)

## Writes
- `tests/<Module>.Tests/**`, `tests/<Module>.IntegrationTests/**` and `src/<Module>/Features/<Slice>/**` files listed in `tasks[<task-id>].files_in_scope`.
- `.specs/<feature-id>/.tdd-state.json` (phase transitions; `tasks` is a map keyed by task id with a top-level `active_task`).
- `.specs/<feature-id>/05-implementation-log.md` (one `### <task-id> — <phase>` block per phase).

## Process
For the supplied `<task-id>`:

0. **Pre-flight commit check.** Run `git status`. If there are uncommitted changes from any prior task, refuse to start. List the changed files and remind: `git commit → /net-build <task-id>`.
1. **Activate.** Set `.tdd-state.json` `active_task = <task-id>`. Refuse if any other task is `phase: red|green|refactor|simplify` (one task in flight at a time).
2. **Red** (`dotnet-test-engineer`). Write the smallest test that captures the next AC slice, with the attribute block in order: `[Fact]`/`[Theory]` → `[Trait("AC", "AC-NNN")]` → `[Trait("Category", "Integration")]` when it needs a container or the full host. Run it with `dotnet test --filter "FullyQualifiedName~ClassName.MethodName"`. Confirm it fails on an assertion, not a compile error. Capture the failure message into `tasks[<task-id>].red_failure_excerpt`. Set `phase: "red"`. Append log block.
3. **Green** (`dotnet-implementer`). Write the minimum production code under `files_in_scope` to pass the test. Re-run the single test, then `dotnet test --filter "Category!=Integration"` for the unit suite (plus `dotnet test --filter "Category=Integration"` when integration files were touched). Set `phase: "green"`. Append log block.
4. **Refactor.** Improve structure without changing behavior or public signatures. Re-run the suite after every edit. Set `phase: "refactor"`. Append log block.
5. **Simplify.** Apply `clarity-over-cleverness` (untangle ternaries, inline once-used helpers, kill dead options, name domain concepts from the `01-spec.md` glossary, extract every literal that appears 2+ times in a file). Run `dotnet format --verify-no-changes` and `dotnet build -c Release` (warning-free) plus the suite. Set `phase: "simplify"`. Append log block.
6. **Done.** Set `phase: "done"`, clear `active_task`. If more ACs in this task remain uncovered, immediately re-run from step 2 with the next slice (do not declare done early).
7. **STOP — commit reminder.** Surface: files changed (`git status`), tests passing, suggested commit message. Recommend: `git status → git commit → /net-build <next-task-id>`. Do not auto-start the next task unless the user explicitly requests chaining.

## Refuse if
- `<task-id>` is not in `.tdd-state.json`, or `.tdd-state.json` has an array-shaped `tasks` value (the hooks reject it — re-run `/net-plan`).
- Another task is mid-flight (not `pending` or `done`).
- A `src/**/*.cs` edit is attempted while `phase != "red"` and `red_failure_excerpt` is empty (also enforced by the Claude hook `block-impl-without-failing-test.sh`).
- Any edit lands outside `tasks[<task-id>].files_in_scope` (enforced by `enforce-files-in-scope.sh`).
- A skip or gate-weakening flag would be needed — `dotnet test --no-build`, `-p:SkipTests`, `-p:RunAnalyzers=false`, `-p:TreatWarningsAsErrors=false` (enforced by `forbid-skip-flags.sh`).
- The spec or design leaves the edge case undefined — halt and open a `Q-NNN` instead of choosing a silent default (`block-progress-on-open-questions.sh`).
- A new NuGet package would be needed and the user has not confirmed it (version goes in `Directory.Packages.props`, never inline on the `PackageReference`).

## Done when
- Every AC listed under `tasks[<task-id>].acs_covered` has at least one test carrying `[Trait("AC", "AC-NNN")]`.
- All four phase blocks are present in `05-implementation-log.md` for this task.
- `.tdd-state.json` shows `phase: "done"` for `<task-id>` and `active_task` is cleared.
- `dotnet format --verify-no-changes` is clean and `dotnet build -c Release` produces no warnings.
- Commit reminder surfaced (Step 7); user commits before starting the next task. After all tasks done, run `/net-test` then `/net-validate`.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# enforce-files-in-scope.sh
# Claude PreToolUse Edit|Write hook.
# Blocks edits outside the active task's files_in_scope, EXCEPT:
#   - .specs/** and build/config files are always allowed (artifacts).
#   - test code is allowed for the test-engineer agents (red step).
#
# This is a defense-in-depth alongside block-impl-without-failing-test.sh which
# already covers production code. This script extends the same check to test
# files. Path classification is shared — see lib/classify-path.sh.

set -euo pipefail

HOOK_LIB="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/lib" && pwd)"
# shellcheck source=lib/preflight.sh
. "$HOOK_LIB/preflight.sh"
# shellcheck source=lib/classify-path.sh
. "$HOOK_LIB/classify-path.sh"

require_jq

input="$(cat)"
file_path="$(echo "$input" | jq -r '.tool_input.file_path // .tool_input.path // empty')"
[ -z "$file_path" ] && exit 0

# Artifacts always pass; production code is the sibling hook's job; only test
# code is enforced here.
case "$(classify_path "$file_path")" in
  test) ;;
  *) exit 0 ;;
esac

state_file="$(ls -t .specs/*/.tdd-state.json 2>/dev/null | head -n 1 || true)"
[ -z "$state_file" ] && exit 0  # no active feature; let it through (e.g. test-plan author)

# A legacy array-shaped `tasks` cannot be queried by key; stay out of the way
# rather than blocking every test edit (the sibling hook reports the problem).
jq -e '.tasks | type == "object"' "$state_file" >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 0

active_task="$(jq -r '.active_task // empty' "$state_file")"
[ -z "$active_task" ] && exit 0

# Each declared path is bound to $s before comparing: inside `endswith(.)` the
# `.` would rebind to $f, making the test always true.
in_scope="$(jq -r --arg t "$active_task" --arg f "$file_path" '
  .tasks[$t].files_in_scope // []
  | map(. as $s | select($f == $s or ($f | endswith($s))))
  | length
' "$state_file")"

if [ "$in_scope" = "0" ]; then
  echo "BLOCKED: $file_path is not in task $active_task files_in_scope. Edit only the declared test paths, or update 04-tasks.md and re-plan." >&2
  exit 2
fi

exit 0

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# block-impl-without-failing-test.sh
# Claude Code PreToolUse hook for Edit|Write.
# Refuses to edit production code unless .specs/<active>/.tdd-state.json shows
# phase=red with a non-empty red_failure_excerpt and the file is in files_in_scope.
#
# "Production code" is whatever lib/classify-path.sh calls `prod`: src/main/** on
# the JVM stack, src/**/*.cs on the .NET stack.
#
# Input: JSON on stdin (Claude Code hook protocol). We read tool_input.file_path.
# Output: exit 0 to allow, exit 2 + stderr message to block.

set -euo pipefail

HOOK_LIB="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/lib" && pwd)"
# shellcheck source=lib/preflight.sh
. "$HOOK_LIB/preflight.sh"
# shellcheck source=lib/classify-path.sh
. "$HOOK_LIB/classify-path.sh"

require_jq

input="$(cat)"

file_path="$(echo "$input" | jq -r '.tool_input.file_path // .tool_input.path // empty')"
[ -z "$file_path" ] && exit 0

# Only enforce on production code (JVM src/main/**, .NET src/**/*.cs).
[ "$(classify_path "$file_path")" = "prod" ] || exit 0

# Find the active feature: the most recent .specs/<id>/.tdd-state.json by mtime.
state_file="$(ls -t .specs/*/.tdd-state.json 2>/dev/null | head -n 1 || true)"
if [ -z "$state_file" ] || [ ! -f "$state_file" ]; then
  echo "BLOCKED: no .specs/<feature>/.tdd-state.json found. Run /build <task-id> so the test-engineer writes the failing test first." >&2
  exit 2
fi

# The canonical shape has `tasks` as a map keyed by task id. A legacy array
# shape makes every .tasks[$t] lookup abort under `set -e`, so report it plainly.
if ! jq -e '.tasks | type == "object"' "$state_file" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "BLOCKED: $state_file has a legacy array-shaped \"tasks\" field. Re-run /plan (or /net-plan) to migrate it to the keyed-map shape: {\"tasks\": {\"T-001\": {...}}}." >&2
  exit 2
fi

active_task="$(jq -r '.active_task // empty' "$state_file")"
if [ -z "$active_task" ]; then
  echo "BLOCKED: no active_task in $state_file. Run /build <task-id>." >&2
  exit 2
fi

phase="$(jq -r --arg t "$active_task" '.tasks[$t].phase // empty' "$state_file" 2>/dev/null || echo '')"
red_excerpt="$(jq -r --arg t "$active_task" '.tasks[$t].red_failure_excerpt // empty' "$state_file" 2>/dev/null || echo '')"

if [ "$phase" != "red" ] && [ "$phase" != "green" ] && [ "$phase" != "refactor" ] && [ "$phase" != "simplify" ]; then
  echo "BLOCKED: task $active_task phase is '$phase'. Cannot edit src/main/** without a failing test (phase=red)." >&2
  exit 2
fi

if [ "$phase" = "red" ] && [ -z "$red_excerpt" ]; then
  echo "BLOCKED: task $active_task phase=red but red_failure_excerpt is empty. The failing test was not actually run, or it passed." >&2
classify-path.sh
preflight.sh

## Assistant · 2026-09-21T17:02:56.359Z

I've stopped here: the scope hook has a bug on Windows that blocks the red step.

**The problem.** `enforce-files-in-scope.sh` checks whether the edited path ends with one of the task's declared paths. Claude Code passes Windows paths with backslashes (`C:\dev\CashRegister\tests\CashRegister.Tests\ScaffoldSmokeTests.cs`), but the task declares `tests/CashRegister.Tests/ScaffoldSmokeTests.cs`. They never match, so any test file is blocked even though it is in scope. Passing a forward-slash path doesn't help, because the tool normalises it back to backslashes.

The sibling hook `block-impl-without-failing-test.sh` probably has the reverse problem. If `lib/classify-path.sh` doesn't recognise `src\...\*.cs` as production code, production edits would be let through without a failing test. That would explain why the `.csproj` writes went through without any check.

I haven't bypassed the hook by writing the files through Bash, since that would defeat the TDD guard.

**Proposed fix.** Normalise the path in both hooks right after `file_path` is read. Collapsing `\` to `/` and stripping the repo root makes the path relative, so exact and suffix matching both work:

```bash
file_path="${file_path//\\//}"                      # backslashes → forward slashes
file_path="${file_path#"$(pwd -W 2>/dev/null || pwd)/"}"  # make relative to repo root
```

I'd also check `lib/classify-path.sh` for the same assumption.

**T-001 state so far**
- `active_task` is set to `T-001`; the phase is still `pending`.
- Written: `global.json`, `Directory.Build.props`, `Directory.Packages.props` (latest stable versions: xUnit v3 4.0.1, ASP.NET 10.0.12, NSubstitute 6.2.0, ArchUnitNET 0.13.4 and others), `.editorconfig`, `.gitignore`, and both test `.csproj` files.
- Blocked: the two `ScaffoldSmokeTests.cs` red tests.
- The four new NuGet packages in `Directory.Packages.props` (NSubstitute, `Microsoft.Extensions.Diagnostics.Testing`, ArchUnitNET, `Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.CodeCoverage`) were named in the approved plan. `/net-build` asks for confirmation before adding packages, so please confirm them too.

Should I apply this fix to the two hooks (and `classify-path.sh` if it needs it), then carry on with T-001?

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# classify-path.sh
# Shared path classifier for the PreToolUse/PostToolUse hooks.
#
# Sourced, not executed. Defines one pure function:
#
#   classify_path <file_path>   ->  prints exactly one of:
#                                     artifact  spec/build/config file, never gated
#                                     prod      production code, TDD gate applies
#                                     test      test code, files_in_scope applies
#                                     other     unrecognised, hooks ignore it
#
# Classification is by PATH SHAPE only. It deliberately does not read
# .specs/_stack.json: that file does not exist until /onboard or /net-onboard
# runs, and a hook must not fail closed on a missing file.
#
# Rule order matters. The Java rules (src/main, src/test) are evaluated before
# the C# rules so existing JVM behavior is byte-for-byte unchanged.

classify_path() {
  local p="$1"

  # Normalise so a repo-relative path ("src/main/java/App.java") matches the
  # same */prefixed patterns as an absolute one. Claude Code passes absolute
  # paths today, but the hooks are also driven by hand and from tests.
  case "$p" in
    /* | ./*) ;;        # already absolute or explicitly relative
    *) p="./$p" ;;      # bare or repo-relative: give it a leading ./
  esac

  # 1. Spec artifacts are never gated.
  case "$p" in
    *.specs/*) echo artifact; return 0 ;;
  esac

  # 2. Build and configuration files are never gated.
  case "$p" in
    */pom.xml|pom.xml) echo artifact; return 0 ;;
    */checkstyle.xml|*/dependency-check-suppressions.xml) echo artifact; return 0 ;;
    */global.json|global.json) echo artifact; return 0 ;;
    */Directory.Build.props|Directory.Build.props) echo artifact; return 0 ;;
    */Directory.Packages.props|Directory.Packages.props) echo artifact; return 0 ;;
    *.sln|*.slnx|*.csproj|*.props|*.targets) echo artifact; return 0 ;;
    */.editorconfig|.editorconfig) echo artifact; return 0 ;;
    */appsettings*.json|appsettings*.json) echo artifact; return 0 ;;
    */stryker-config.json|stryker-config.json) echo artifact; return 0 ;;
  esac

  # 3-4. Java / Maven layout, unchanged from the original hooks.
  case "$p" in
    */src/test/*) echo test; return 0 ;;
    */src/main/*) echo prod; return 0 ;;
  esac

  # 5. C# test code. Checked before C# production code so a test project
  #    living under src/ (e.g. src/Orders.Tests/) still classifies as test.
  case "$p" in
    *.cs)
      case "$p" in
        */tests/*|tests/*) echo test; return 0 ;;
        *.Tests/*|*.Tests.*/*|*.IntegrationTests/*) echo test; return 0 ;;
        *Tests.cs|*Test.cs|*Fixture.cs|*Fixtures.cs) echo test; return 0 ;;
      esac
      ;;
  esac

  # 6. C# production code.
  case "$p" in
    *.cs)
      case "$p" in
        */src/*|src/*) echo prod; return 0 ;;
      esac
      ;;
  esac

  # 7. Everything else is outside the gates.
  echo other
  return 0
}
  echo "BLOCKED: task $active_task phase=red but red_failure_excerpt is empty. The failing test was not actually run, or it passed." >&2
  exit 2
fi

# Files in scope check. Each declared path is bound to $s before comparing:
# inside `endswith(.)` the `.` would rebind to $f, making the test always true.
in_scope="$(jq -r --arg t "$active_task" --arg f "$file_path" '
  .tasks[$t].files_in_scope // []
  | map(. as $s | select($f == $s or ($f | endswith($s))))
  | length
' "$state_file")"

if [ "$in_scope" = "0" ]; then
  echo "BLOCKED: $file_path is not in task $active_task files_in_scope. Edit only the declared paths, or update the task entry first (and re-run /plan)." >&2
  exit 2
fi

exit 0

## Assistant · 2026-09-21T17:16:20.330Z

T-001 is done: the new solution builds and both smoke tests pass, one in each test project.

**What's in place**
- **Solution:** `CashRegister.slnx` with four projects: the `CashRegister` module, the `CashRegister.Api` host, `CashRegister.Tests` and `CashRegister.IntegrationTests`.
- **Shared settings:** `global.json` pins the .NET 10 SDK and uses the Microsoft.Testing.Platform test runner. `Directory.Build.props` turns on nullable checks and treats warnings as errors. Package versions are managed centrally.
- **Host:** a minimal API that listens on `http://localhost:5080`. The integration tests can start it.
- **Gates:**
  - `dotnet format --verify-no-changes` passes;
  - the Release build has 0 warnings;
  - unit tests 1/1 and integration tests 1/1 pass.
- **Records:** `.tdd-state.json` marks T-001 done with no active task, and all four phases are logged in `05-implementation-log.md`.

**Things you should know**
- **Hook fix:** as you approved, five scripts in `.claude/hooks/` now convert Windows backslash paths to forward slashes. I tested all three hook cases: an in-scope test file is allowed, an out-of-scope test file is blocked, and production code before a failing test is blocked.
- **Red-step test changed:** the first unit smoke test could never pass. The compiler drops a reference to an assembly whose types are never used, and the module has no types until T-009. I changed it to load the assembly by name and confirmed it failed before adding the project. The log records this.
- **Packages:** NSubstitute, ArchUnitNET, FakeLogger and the code-coverage extension are added at their latest stable versions, as named in the approved plan.

Everything is still untracked, and the project settings block me from running `git commit`, so please commit it yourself. Suggested message:

```

- .NET 10 slnx with CashRegister module + thin API host (ADR-001)
- xUnit v3 on Microsoft.Testing.Platform, central package management
- fix Windows backslash paths in .claude hooks

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
```

## User · 2026-09-21T17:19:41.690Z

# /net-build

**Phase:** 4 — build (TDD)
**Owning agent:** `.claude/agents/dotnet-implementer.md` (collaborates with `dotnet-test-engineer`)
**Skills used:** `tdd-red-green-refactor`, `dotnet-10-conventions`, `clarity-over-cleverness`, `dotnet-testing-patterns`, `dotnet-task-decomposition`

## Purpose
Execute one task end-to-end through the four TDD phases (red → green → refactor → simplify), updating `.tdd-state.json` and appending a block to `05-implementation-log.md` after each phase.

## Inputs
- `<task-id>` (e.g. `T-001`). Required.

## Reads
- `.specs/<feature-id>/04-tasks.md`
- `.specs/<feature-id>/03-design.md`
- `.specs/<feature-id>/.tdd-state.json`
- `.claude/skills/tdd-red-green-refactor/SKILL.md` (authoritative)
- `.claude/skills/dotnet-testing-patterns/SKILL.md` (scope selection and the `[Trait("AC", ...)]` contract)

## Writes
- `tests/<Module>.Tests/**`, `tests/<Module>.IntegrationTests/**` and `src/<Module>/Features/<Slice>/**` files listed in `tasks[<task-id>].files_in_scope`.
- `.specs/<feature-id>/.tdd-state.json` (phase transitions; `tasks` is a map keyed by task id with a top-level `active_task`).
- `.specs/<feature-id>/05-implementation-log.md` (one `### <task-id> — <phase>` block per phase).

## Process
For the supplied `<task-id>`:

0. **Pre-flight commit check.** Run `git status`. If there are uncommitted changes from any prior task, refuse to start. List the changed files and remind: `git commit → /net-build <task-id>`.
1. **Activate.** Set `.tdd-state.json` `active_task = <task-id>`. Refuse if any other task is `phase: red|green|refactor|simplify` (one task in flight at a time).
2. **Red** (`dotnet-test-engineer`). Write the smallest test that captures the next AC slice, with the attribute block in order: `[Fact]`/`[Theory]` → `[Trait("AC", "AC-NNN")]` → `[Trait("Category", "Integration")]` when it needs a container or the full host. Run it with `dotnet test --filter "FullyQualifiedName~ClassName.MethodName"`. Confirm it fails on an assertion, not a compile error. Capture the failure message into `tasks[<task-id>].red_failure_excerpt`. Set `phase: "red"`. Append log block.
3. **Green** (`dotnet-implementer`). Write the minimum production code under `files_in_scope` to pass the test. Re-run the single test, then `dotnet test --filter "Category!=Integration"` for the unit suite (plus `dotnet test --filter "Category=Integration"` when integration files were touched). Set `phase: "green"`. Append log block.
4. **Refactor.** Improve structure without changing behavior or public signatures. Re-run the suite after every edit. Set `phase: "refactor"`. Append log block.
5. **Simplify.** Apply `clarity-over-cleverness` (untangle ternaries, inline once-used helpers, kill dead options, name domain concepts from the `01-spec.md` glossary, extract every literal that appears 2+ times in a file). Run `dotnet format --verify-no-changes` and `dotnet build -c Release` (warning-free) plus the suite. Set `phase: "simplify"`. Append log block.
6. **Done.** Set `phase: "done"`, clear `active_task`. If more ACs in this task remain uncovered, immediately re-run from step 2 with the next slice (do not declare done early).
7. **STOP — commit reminder.** Surface: files changed (`git status`), tests passing, suggested commit message. Recommend: `git status → git commit → /net-build <next-task-id>`. Do not auto-start the next task unless the user explicitly requests chaining.

## Refuse if
- `<task-id>` is not in `.tdd-state.json`, or `.tdd-state.json` has an array-shaped `tasks` value (the hooks reject it — re-run `/net-plan`).
- Another task is mid-flight (not `pending` or `done`).
- A `src/**/*.cs` edit is attempted while `phase != "red"` and `red_failure_excerpt` is empty (also enforced by the Claude hook `block-impl-without-failing-test.sh`).
- Any edit lands outside `tasks[<task-id>].files_in_scope` (enforced by `enforce-files-in-scope.sh`).
- A skip or gate-weakening flag would be needed — `dotnet test --no-build`, `-p:SkipTests`, `-p:RunAnalyzers=false`, `-p:TreatWarningsAsErrors=false` (enforced by `forbid-skip-flags.sh`).
- The spec or design leaves the edge case undefined — halt and open a `Q-NNN` instead of choosing a silent default (`block-progress-on-open-questions.sh`).
- A new NuGet package would be needed and the user has not confirmed it (version goes in `Directory.Packages.props`, never inline on the `PackageReference`).

## Done when
- Every AC listed under `tasks[<task-id>].acs_covered` has at least one test carrying `[Trait("AC", "AC-NNN")]`.
- All four phase blocks are present in `05-implementation-log.md` for this task.
- `.tdd-state.json` shows `phase: "done"` for `<task-id>` and `active_task` is cleared.
- `dotnet format --verify-no-changes` is clean and `dotnet build -c Release` produces no warnings.
- Commit reminder surfaced (Step 7); user commits before starting the next task. After all tasks done, run `/net-test` then `/net-validate`.

  "content": "namespace CashRegister.Features.Currencies;\n\n/// <summary>\n/// A monetary system and the denominations a cashier can hand back.\n/// A new currency is added by subclassing and registering it (DC-002, ADR-004).\n/// </summary>\npublic abstract class Currency\n{\n    protected Currency(string code, char decimalSeparator, int minorUnitDigits, IEnumerable<Denomination> denominations)\n    {\n        ArgumentException.ThrowIfNullOrWhiteSpace(code);\n        ArgumentOutOfRangeException.ThrowIfNegative(minorUnitDigits);\n        ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(denominations);\n\n        var largestFirst = denominations.OrderByDescending(d => d.ValueInMinorUnits).ToList();\n\n        if (largestFirst.Count == 0)\n        {\n            throw new ArgumentException(\"A currency needs at least one denomination.\", nameof(denominations));\n        }\n\n        if (largestFirst.DistinctBy(d => d.ValueInMinorUnits).Count() != largestFirst.Count)\n        {\n            throw new ArgumentException(\"Denomination values must be unique.\", nameof(denominations));\n        }\n\n        // Any amount must be payable exactly, so the smallest unit has to exist.\n        if (largestFirst[^1].ValueInMinorUnits != 1)\n        {\n            throw new ArgumentException(\"A currency must include a denomination worth one minor unit.\", nameof(denominations));\n        }\n\n        Code = code;\n        DecimalSeparator = decimalSeparator;\n        MinorUnitDigits = minorUnitDigits;\n        Denominations = largestFirst.AsReadOnly();\n    }\n\n    /// <summary>ISO 4217 code, e.g. <c>USD</c>.</summary>\n    public string Code { get; }\n\n    /// <summary>Separator between major and minor units in input amounts (AC-029).</summary>\n    public char DecimalSeparator { get; }\n\n    /// <summary>Maximum decimal places an input amount may have.</summary>\n    public int MinorUnitDigits { get; }\n\n    /// <summary>Denominations ordered from largest to smallest value.</summary>\n    public IReadOnlyList<Denomination> Denominations { get; }\n}\n"

  "content": "using System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis;\n\nnamespace CashRegister.Features.Currencies;\n\n/// <summary>Looks up registered currencies by code, ignoring case.</summary>\npublic sealed class CurrencyRegistry : ICurrencyRegistry\n{\n    private readonly Dictionary<string, Currency> _byCode;\n\n    public CurrencyRegistry(IEnumerable<Currency> currencies)\n    {\n        ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(currencies);\n\n        // ToDictionary throws ArgumentException on a duplicate code.\n        _byCode = currencies.ToDictionary(c => c.Code, StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase);\n    }\n\n    public IReadOnlyCollection<Currency> All => _byCode.Values;\n\n    public bool TryGet(string code, [MaybeNullWhen(false)] out Currency currency)\n    {\n        ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(code);\n        return _byCode.TryGetValue(code, out currency);\n    }\n}\n"
}

## Assistant · 2026-09-21T17:28:39.697Z

T-002 is done. The Currencies slice is in place and all 23 tests pass (22 unit, 1 integration).

**What's in place**
- `Denomination`: rejects blank names or a value of zero or less, and `NameFor(count)` gives the singular name for 1 and the plural otherwise (AC-009, AC-010).
- `Currency`: an abstract base class holding the code, decimal separator, allowed decimal places, and denominations sorted largest first (AC-007, AC-029). It rejects a currency with no denominations, with two denominations of the same value, or without a 1-cent unit. Adding a currency means one new subclass (DC-002).
- `UsdCurrency`: dollar, quarter, dime, nickel and penny, with `.` as the separator and 2 decimal places.
- `CurrencyRegistry`: looks up currencies by code ignoring case, and refuses duplicate codes.

**Gates:** format check clean, Release build with 0 warnings, 100% line and branch coverage on the slice.

**Two deviations**
- **Two-step red:** in C#, a test that references missing types fails to compile rather than on an assertion. I logged the compile failure first, then added stubs that throw `NotImplementedException` and confirmed 21 assertion failures before implementing. This is recorded in the log, and I'll use the same pattern for later tasks.
- **`.editorconfig` change:** the format check wanted `_penny` for a `static readonly` field. I added a rule so private static readonly fields use PascalCase, the usual .NET convention.

Commit message:
```
feat(currencies): add Denomination, Currency base, USD and currency registry (T-002)
```

Then run `/net-build T-003` (Transaction and the fewest-coins strategy).

## User · 2026-09-21T17:29:27.727Z

# /net-build

**Phase:** 4 — build (TDD)
**Owning agent:** `.claude/agents/dotnet-implementer.md` (collaborates with `dotnet-test-engineer`)
**Skills used:** `tdd-red-green-refactor`, `dotnet-10-conventions`, `clarity-over-cleverness`, `dotnet-testing-patterns`, `dotnet-task-decomposition`

## Purpose
Execute one task end-to-end through the four TDD phases (red → green → refactor → simplify), updating `.tdd-state.json` and appending a block to `05-implementation-log.md` after each phase.

## Inputs
- `<task-id>` (e.g. `T-001`). Required.

## Reads
- `.specs/<feature-id>/04-tasks.md`
- `.specs/<feature-id>/03-design.md`
- `.specs/<feature-id>/.tdd-state.json`
- `.claude/skills/tdd-red-green-refactor/SKILL.md` (authoritative)
- `.claude/skills/dotnet-testing-patterns/SKILL.md` (scope selection and the `[Trait("AC", ...)]` contract)

## Writes
- `tests/<Module>.Tests/**`, `tests/<Module>.IntegrationTests/**` and `src/<Module>/Features/<Slice>/**` files listed in `tasks[<task-id>].files_in_scope`.
- `.specs/<feature-id>/.tdd-state.json` (phase transitions; `tasks` is a map keyed by task id with a top-level `active_task`).
- `.specs/<feature-id>/05-implementation-log.md` (one `### <task-id> — <phase>` block per phase).

## Process
For the supplied `<task-id>`:

0. **Pre-flight commit check.** Run `git status`. If there are uncommitted changes from any prior task, refuse to start. List the changed files and remind: `git commit → /net-build <task-id>`.
1. **Activate.** Set `.tdd-state.json` `active_task = <task-id>`. Refuse if any other task is `phase: red|green|refactor|simplify` (one task in flight at a time).
2. **Red** (`dotnet-test-engineer`). Write the smallest test that captures the next AC slice, with the attribute block in order: `[Fact]`/`[Theory]` → `[Trait("AC", "AC-NNN")]` → `[Trait("Category", "Integration")]` when it needs a container or the full host. Run it with `dotnet test --filter "FullyQualifiedName~ClassName.MethodName"`. Confirm it fails on an assertion, not a compile error. Capture the failure message into `tasks[<task-id>].red_failure_excerpt`. Set `phase: "red"`. Append log block.
3. **Green** (`dotnet-implementer`). Write the minimum production code under `files_in_scope` to pass the test. Re-run the single test, then `dotnet test --filter "Category!=Integration"` for the unit suite (plus `dotnet test --filter "Category=Integration"` when integration files were touched). Set `phase: "green"`. Append log block.
4. **Refactor.** Improve structure without changing behavior or public signatures. Re-run the suite after every edit. Set `phase: "refactor"`. Append log block.
5. **Simplify.** Apply `clarity-over-cleverness` (untangle ternaries, inline once-used helpers, kill dead options, name domain concepts from the `01-spec.md` glossary, extract every literal that appears 2+ times in a file). Run `dotnet format --verify-no-changes` and `dotnet build -c Release` (warning-free) plus the suite. Set `phase: "simplify"`. Append log block.
6. **Done.** Set `phase: "done"`, clear `active_task`. If more ACs in this task remain uncovered, immediately re-run from step 2 with the next slice (do not declare done early).
7. **STOP — commit reminder.** Surface: files changed (`git status`), tests passing, suggested commit message. Recommend: `git status → git commit → /net-build <next-task-id>`. Do not auto-start the next task unless the user explicitly requests chaining.

## Refuse if
- `<task-id>` is not in `.tdd-state.json`, or `.tdd-state.json` has an array-shaped `tasks` value (the hooks reject it — re-run `/net-plan`).
- Another task is mid-flight (not `pending` or `done`).
- A `src/**/*.cs` edit is attempted while `phase != "red"` and `red_failure_excerpt` is empty (also enforced by the Claude hook `block-impl-without-failing-test.sh`).
- Any edit lands outside `tasks[<task-id>].files_in_scope` (enforced by `enforce-files-in-scope.sh`).
- A skip or gate-weakening flag would be needed — `dotnet test --no-build`, `-p:SkipTests`, `-p:RunAnalyzers=false`, `-p:TreatWarningsAsErrors=false` (enforced by `forbid-skip-flags.sh`).
- The spec or design leaves the edge case undefined — halt and open a `Q-NNN` instead of choosing a silent default (`block-progress-on-open-questions.sh`).
- A new NuGet package would be needed and the user has not confirmed it (version goes in `Directory.Packages.props`, never inline on the `PackageReference`).

## Done when
- Every AC listed under `tasks[<task-id>].acs_covered` has at least one test carrying `[Trait("AC", "AC-NNN")]`.
- All four phase blocks are present in `05-implementation-log.md` for this task.
- `.tdd-state.json` shows `phase: "done"` for `<task-id>` and `active_task` is cleared.
- `dotnet format --verify-no-changes` is clean and `dotnet build -c Release` produces no warnings.
- Commit reminder surfaced (Step 7); user commits before starting the next task. After all tasks done, run `/net-test` then `/net-validate`.

  "content": "using CashRegister.Features.Change.Money;\nusing CashRegister.Features.Currencies;\n\nnamespace CashRegister.Tests.Features.Change.Money;\n\npublic sealed class TransactionTests\n{\n    private static readonly UsdCurrency Usd = new();\n\n    [Fact]\n    [Trait(\"AC\", \"AC-005\")]\n    public void ChangeDue_IsPaidMinusOwed()\n    {\n        var transaction = new Transaction(owed: 212, paid: 300, Usd);\n\n        transaction.ChangeDue.ShouldBe(88);\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void ChangeDue_ExactPayment_IsZero()\n    {\n        new Transaction(owed: 300, paid: 300, Usd).ChangeDue.ShouldBe(0);\n    }\n\n    [Theory]\n    [InlineData(-1, 100)]\n    [InlineData(100, -1)]\n    public void Constructor_NegativeAmount_Throws(long owed, long paid)\n    {\n        Should.Throw<ArgumentOutOfRangeException>(() => new Transaction(owed, paid, Usd));\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Constructor_PaidLessThanOwed_Throws()\n    {\n        Should.Throw<ArgumentException>(() => new Transaction(owed: 300, paid: 200, Usd));\n    }\n}\n"
}
