{
  "file_path": "C:\\dev\\CashRegister\\.github\\scripts\\lib\\new-code-coverage.mjs",
  "content": "// New-code coverage: of the src/**/*.cs lines added or changed since BASE_REF, how many that\n// the coverage report counts as executable were hit by the unit run.\nimport { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';\nimport fs from 'node:fs';\nimport { readMerged } from './cobertura.mjs';\n\nconst repoRoot = process.cwd();\nconst baseRef = process.env.BASE_REF ?? 'origin/main';\nconst threshold = Number(process.env.NEW_CODE_THRESHOLD ?? '0.95');\nconst report = 'artifacts/coverage/cobertura.xml';\n\nif (!fs.existsSync(report)) {\n  console.error(`missing ${report}; run ./.github/scripts/harness-dotnet.sh first`);\n  process.exit(2);\n}\n\nconst diff = spawnSync('git', ['diff', '--unified=0', `${baseRef}...HEAD`, '--', 'src/**/*.cs', 'src/*.cs'], {\n  encoding: 'utf8',\n  maxBuffer: 64 * 1024 * 1024,\n});\nif (diff.status !== 0) {\n  console.error(diff.stderr);\n  process.exit(2);\n}\n\n// file -> set of changed line numbers (new side of the diff)\nconst changed = new Map();\nlet current = null;\nfor (const line of diff.stdout.split('\\n')) {\n  const file = line.match(/^\\+\\+\\+ b\\/(.+)$/);\n  if (file) {\n    current = file[1];\n    changed.set(current, changed.get(current) ?? new Set());\n    continue;\n  }\n  const hunk = line.match(/^@@ -\\d+(?:,\\d+)? \\+(\\d+)(?:,(\\d+))? @@/);\n  if (hunk && current) {\n    const start = Number(hunk[1]);\n    const count = hunk[2] === undefined ? 1 : Number(hunk[2]);\n    for (let n = start; n < start + count; n++) changed.get(current).add(n);\n  }\n}\n\nconst coverage = readMerged([report], repoRoot);\nlet executable = 0;\nlet covered = 0;\nconst uncovered = [];\nfor (const [file, lines] of changed) {\n  const fileCoverage = coverage.get(file);\n  if (!fileCoverage) continue;\n  for (const n of lines) {\n    const entry = fileCoverage.get(n);\n    if (!entry) continue; // not an executable line\n    executable++;\n    if (entry.hits > 0) covered++;\n    else uncovered.push(`${file}:${n}`);\n  }\n}\n\nconst rate = executable === 0 ? 1 : covered / executable;\nconst result = {\n  base_ref: baseRef,\n  threshold,\n  changed_executable_lines: executable,\n  covered_lines: covered,\n  new_code_line: Number(rate.toFixed(4)),\n  status: rate >= threshold ? 'pass' : 'fail',\n  uncovered: uncovered.slice(0, 200),\n};\nfs.writeFileSync('artifacts/new-code-coverage.json', `${JSON.stringify(result, null, 2)}\\n`);\nconsole.log(`new-code coverage vs ${baseRef}: ${(100 * rate).toFixed(2)}% (${covered}/${executable}) → ${result.status}`);\nprocess.exitCode = result.status === 'pass' ? 0 : 1;\n"
}

  "content": "# ADR-009: Build-harness defaults this repo overrides\n\n- **Status:** accepted\n- **Date:** 2026-09-21\n- **Deciders:** user, `dotnet-architect`\n- **Consulted:** `dotnet-build-harness` skill\n\n## Context and problem statement\n\nThe harness was wired from the `dotnet-build-harness` skill. Four of its defaults conflict with choices already made here, or with the repo's own guard rails. The user decided each one on 2026-09-21.\n\n## Decisions\n\n| # | Harness default | This repo | Why |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 | Coverage is measured on the **unit** run only | **Kept (canonical).** The endpoints are proved only by integration tests today, so unit-only coverage is 73.2% line / 75.4% branch and the gate fails. **T-017** adds endpoint unit tests to reach the 90% floor. Thresholds are not lowered. | User choice: \"unit only, add unit tests\". |\n| 2 | `Meziantou.Analyzer` + `GenerateDocumentationFile` | **Waived.** The .NET analyzers stay at `latest-recommended` with warnings (and analyzer warnings) as errors. | User choice. A trial build showed about 36 findings (28 missing XML docs, 5 one-type-per-file, 3 ConfigureAwait, which the skill's own `.editorconfig` disables). |\n| 3 | Private fields `camelCase`, no underscore | **`_camelCase` private fields**; PascalCase types, members, constants and static readonly fields; `I`-prefixed interfaces; no Hungarian notation. Enforced as errors in `.editorconfig`. | User: \"c# is PascalCase, private fields can use _camelCase no hungarian notation\". Matches the existing code and the .NET runtime style. |\n| 4 | `dotnet test --no-build` after `dotnet build` | **No `--no-build`.** The script builds once, then `dotnet test -c Release` does an incremental no-op rebuild. | The repo guard (`settings.json` deny rule + `forbid-skip-flags.sh`) forbids `--no-build` as a stale-build risk; the user chose to keep the guard. |\n\n## Smaller adaptations (no user decision needed)\n\n- **Test filters:** xUnit v3 on Microsoft.Testing.Platform uses `--filter-trait` / `--filter-not-trait`, not VSTest's `--filter`. The trait `Category=Integration` is unchanged.\n- **Per-project test runs:** the unit gate runs once per test project. A solution-wide run with one `--coverage-output` path lets the last process overwrite the others, which was observed. Each project writes its own Cobertura file, and `lib/cobertura.mjs` merges them (a line is covered if any run hit it) into `artifacts/coverage/cobertura.xml`. `--ignore-exit-code 8` tolerates a project with no tests for that gate; the gate still fails if the total is zero.\n- **Contract gate:** no `Microsoft.Extensions.ApiDescription.Server` package. The script starts the built API in Development, fetches `/openapi/v1.json` into `artifacts/openapi/openapi.json` (committed; see `.gitignore`), and diffs operations (path + method) against `BASE_REF`. Schema-level changes are not diffed.\n- **Not adopted:** `ArtifactsPath` (moves `bin/`/`obj/`, and no report path depends on it), `InvariantGlobalization`, the `Microsoft.Build.Traversal` SDK, `.config/dotnet-tools.json` (no dotnet tools are used; Stryker is not opted in), and `Verify.XUnit` (dropped as Gap-004 because of its licence requirement).\n- **Web gates** (lint, typecheck, Vitest coverage with a 90% floor, production build) and `npm audit` (high/critical blocking) run inside the same harness, because the repo ships a React app.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- Positive: one command (`./.github/scripts/harness-dotnet.sh --report`) produces every report `/net-validate` reads.\n- Negative: until T-017 is done, the `coverage` gate is red and the overall harness verdict is `fail`.\n\n## Links\n\n- Skill: `.claude/skills/dotnet-build-harness/SKILL.md`, `references/props-fragments.md`\n- Related: ADR-005 (security), ADR-008 (observability), `06-test-plan.md` Gap-004 / Gap-007\n"

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| format, compile | pass (the stricter `.editorconfig` produced no findings) |
| unit | pass, 128 tests |
| it | pass, 30 tests |
| **coverage** (unit tests only) | **fail: 73.2% line / 75.4% branch**, floor is 90% |
| mutation | skipped (no Stryker config) |
| contract | pass, 5 operations, nothing breaking |
| security | pass, 0 high/critical in NuGet and npm |
| web | pass: lint, typecheck, coverage (100% line / 90.4% branch), build |

The other scripts also work:
- `check-new-code-coverage-dotnet.sh` passes, because no `src` code has changed since the `origin/main` you pushed.
- `traceability-dotnet.sh` shows all 28 acceptance criteria covered.

**Your decisions (recorded in ADR-009)**
- **Coverage:** measured from unit tests only; thresholds not lowered.
- **Analyzers:** Meziantou.Analyzer and XML docs skipped. The .NET analyzers still treat warnings as errors.
- **Naming:** PascalCase for types and members, `_camelCase` for private fields, `I` prefix for interfaces, no Hungarian notation. All are now build errors if broken.
- **`--no-build`:** not used, so the repo's guard stays intact.

**Changes I made to fit this repo** (also in ADR-009)
- **Test filters:** xUnit v3 uses `--filter-trait` / `--filter-not-trait` rather than `--filter`.
- **One coverage report:** the unit gate runs once per test project and the coverage files are merged. A single solution-wide run let one process overwrite another's report; I saw it happen.
- **Contract check:** the OpenAPI document is fetched from the built API and committed as `artifacts/openapi/openapi.json`, so later changes can be diffed. Only additions and removals of endpoints are compared, not schema details.
- **Skipped from the skill's defaults:** `ArtifactsPath`, the Traversal SDK and `dotnet-tools.json`, none of which this repo needs.

**Other new files:** `tests/Directory.Build.props` (shared test settings), `.specs/_stack.json`, and a `.gitignore` that ignores `artifacts/` except the OpenAPI document.

**T-017** will unit-test the file and divisor endpoint handlers to lift coverage above 90%. It needs a small change in `src`: the handlers go from `private` to `internal` so tests can call them. It's planned in `04-tasks.md` and the state file as pending. It could use `FakeTimeProvider` (from `Microsoft.Extensions.TimeProvider.Testing`), a new test package that needs your OK; otherwise I'll write a small fake clock in the test.

## Purpose
Execute one task end-to-end through the four TDD phases (red → green → refactor → simplify), updating `.tdd-state.json` and appending a block to `05-implementation-log.md` after each phase.

## Inputs
- `<task-id>` (e.g. `T-001`). Required.

## Reads
- `.specs/<feature-id>/04-tasks.md`
- `.specs/<feature-id>/03-design.md`
- `.specs/<feature-id>/.tdd-state.json`
- `.claude/skills/tdd-red-green-refactor/SKILL.md` (authoritative)
- `.claude/skills/dotnet-testing-patterns/SKILL.md` (scope selection and the `[Trait("AC", ...)]` contract)

## Writes
- `tests/<Module>.Tests/**`, `tests/<Module>.IntegrationTests/**` and `src/<Module>/Features/<Slice>/**` files listed in `tasks[<task-id>].files_in_scope`.
- `.specs/<feature-id>/.tdd-state.json` (phase transitions; `tasks` is a map keyed by task id with a top-level `active_task`).
- `.specs/<feature-id>/05-implementation-log.md` (one `### <task-id> — <phase>` block per phase).

## Process
For the supplied `<task-id>`:

0. **Pre-flight commit check.** Run `git status`. If there are uncommitted changes from any prior task, refuse to start. List the changed files and remind: `git commit → /net-build <task-id>`.
1. **Activate.** Set `.tdd-state.json` `active_task = <task-id>`. Refuse if any other task is `phase: red|green|refactor|simplify` (one task in flight at a time).
2. **Red** (`dotnet-test-engineer`). Write the smallest test that captures the next AC slice, with the attribute block in order: `[Fact]`/`[Theory]` → `[Trait("AC", "AC-NNN")]` → `[Trait("Category", "Integration")]` when it needs a container or the full host. Run it with `dotnet test --filter "FullyQualifiedName~ClassName.MethodName"`. Confirm it fails on an assertion, not a compile error. Capture the failure message into `tasks[<task-id>].red_failure_excerpt`. Set `phase: "red"`. Append log block.
3. **Green** (`dotnet-implementer`). Write the minimum production code under `files_in_scope` to pass the test. Re-run the single test, then `dotnet test --filter "Category!=Integration"` for the unit suite (plus `dotnet test --filter "Category=Integration"` when integration files were touched). Set `phase: "green"`. Append log block.
4. **Refactor.** Improve structure without changing behavior or public signatures. Re-run the suite after every edit. Set `phase: "refactor"`. Append log block.
5. **Simplify.** Apply `clarity-over-cleverness` (untangle ternaries, inline once-used helpers, kill dead options, name domain concepts from the `01-spec.md` glossary, extract every literal that appears 2+ times in a file). Run `dotnet format --verify-no-changes` and `dotnet build -c Release` (warning-free) plus the suite. Set `phase: "simplify"`. Append log block.
6. **Done.** Set `phase: "done"`, clear `active_task`. If more ACs in this task remain uncovered, immediately re-run from step 2 with the next slice (do not declare done early).
7. **STOP — commit reminder.** Surface: files changed (`git status`), tests passing, suggested commit message. Recommend: `git status → git commit → /net-build <next-task-id>`. Do not auto-start the next task unless the user explicitly requests chaining.

## Refuse if
- `<task-id>` is not in `.tdd-state.json`, or `.tdd-state.json` has an array-shaped `tasks` value (the hooks reject it — re-run `/net-plan`).
- Another task is mid-flight (not `pending` or `done`).
- A `src/**/*.cs` edit is attempted while `phase != "red"` and `red_failure_excerpt` is empty (also enforced by the Claude hook `block-impl-without-failing-test.sh`).
- Any edit lands outside `tasks[<task-id>].files_in_scope` (enforced by `enforce-files-in-scope.sh`).
- A skip or gate-weakening flag would be needed — `dotnet test --no-build`, `-p:SkipTests`, `-p:RunAnalyzers=false`, `-p:TreatWarningsAsErrors=false` (enforced by `forbid-skip-flags.sh`).
- The spec or design leaves the edge case undefined — halt and open a `Q-NNN` instead of choosing a silent default (`block-progress-on-open-questions.sh`).
- A new NuGet package would be needed and the user has not confirmed it (version goes in `Directory.Packages.props`, never inline on the `PackageReference`).

## Done when
- Every AC listed under `tasks[<task-id>].acs_covered` has at least one test carrying `[Trait("AC", "AC-NNN")]`.
- All four phase blocks are present in `05-implementation-log.md` for this task.
- `.tdd-state.json` shows `phase: "done"` for `<task-id>` and `active_task` is cleared.
- `dotnet format --verify-no-changes` is clean and `dotnet build -c Release` produces no warnings.
- Commit reminder surfaced (Step 7); user commits before starting the next task. After all tasks done, run `/net-test` then `/net-validate`.

# /net-build

**Phase:** 4 — build (TDD)
**Owning agent:** `.claude/agents/dotnet-implementer.md` (collaborates with `dotnet-test-engineer`)
**Skills used:** `tdd-red-green-refactor`, `dotnet-10-conventions`, `clarity-over-cleverness`, `dotnet-testing-patterns`, `dotnet-task-decomposition`

## Purpose
Execute one task end-to-end through the four TDD phases (red → green → refactor → simplify), updating `.tdd-state.json` and appending a block to `05-implementation-log.md` after each phase.

## Inputs
- `<task-id>` (e.g. `T-001`). Required.

## Reads
- `.specs/<feature-id>/04-tasks.md`
- `.specs/<feature-id>/03-design.md`
- `.specs/<feature-id>/.tdd-state.json`
- `.claude/skills/tdd-red-green-refactor/SKILL.md` (authoritative)
- `.claude/skills/dotnet-testing-patterns/SKILL.md` (scope selection and the `[Trait("AC", ...)]` contract)

## Writes
- `tests/<Module>.Tests/**`, `tests/<Module>.IntegrationTests/**` and `src/<Module>/Features/<Slice>/**` files listed in `tasks[<task-id>].files_in_scope`.
- `.specs/<feature-id>/.tdd-state.json` (phase transitions; `tasks` is a map keyed by task id with a top-level `active_task`).
- `.specs/<feature-id>/05-implementation-log.md` (one `### <task-id> — <phase>` block per phase).

## Process
For the supplied `<task-id>`:

0. **Pre-flight commit check.** Run `git status`. If there are uncommitted changes from any prior task, refuse to start. List the changed files and remind: `git commit → /net-build <task-id>`.
1. **Activate.** Set `.tdd-state.json` `active_task = <task-id>`. Refuse if any other task is `phase: red|green|refactor|simplify` (one task in flight at a time).
2. **Red** (`dotnet-test-engineer`). Write the smallest test that captures the next AC slice, with the attribute block in order: `[Fact]`/`[Theory]` → `[Trait("AC", "AC-NNN")]` → `[Trait("Category", "Integration")]` when it needs a container or the full host. Run it with `dotnet test --filter "FullyQualifiedName~ClassName.MethodName"`. Confirm it fails on an assertion, not a compile error. Capture the failure message into `tasks[<task-id>].red_failure_excerpt`. Set `phase: "red"`. Append log block.
3. **Green** (`dotnet-implementer`). Write the minimum production code under `files_in_scope` to pass the test. Re-run the single test, then `dotnet test --filter "Category!=Integration"` for the unit suite (plus `dotnet test --filter "Category=Integration"` when integration files were touched). Set `phase: "green"`. Append log block.
4. **Refactor.** Improve structure without changing behavior or public signatures. Re-run the suite after every edit. Set `phase: "refactor"`. Append log block.
5. **Simplify.** Apply `clarity-over-cleverness` (untangle ternaries, inline once-used helpers, kill dead options, name domain concepts from the `01-spec.md` glossary, extract every literal that appears 2+ times in a file). Run `dotnet format --verify-no-changes` and `dotnet build -c Release` (warning-free) plus the suite. Set `phase: "simplify"`. Append log block.
6. **Done.** Set `phase: "done"`, clear `active_task`. If more ACs in this task remain uncovered, immediately re-run from step 2 with the next slice (do not declare done early).
7. **STOP — commit reminder.** Surface: files changed (`git status`), tests passing, suggested commit message. Recommend: `git status → git commit → /net-build <next-task-id>`. Do not auto-start the next task unless the user explicitly requests chaining.

## Refuse if
- `<task-id>` is not in `.tdd-state.json`, or `.tdd-state.json` has an array-shaped `tasks` value (the hooks reject it — re-run `/net-plan`).
- Another task is mid-flight (not `pending` or `done`).
- A `src/**/*.cs` edit is attempted while `phase != "red"` and `red_failure_excerpt` is empty (also enforced by the Claude hook `block-impl-without-failing-test.sh`).
- Any edit lands outside `tasks[<task-id>].files_in_scope` (enforced by `enforce-files-in-scope.sh`).
- A skip or gate-weakening flag would be needed — `dotnet test --no-build`, `-p:SkipTests`, `-p:RunAnalyzers=false`, `-p:TreatWarningsAsErrors=false` (enforced by `forbid-skip-flags.sh`).
- The spec or design leaves the edge case undefined — halt and open a `Q-NNN` instead of choosing a silent default (`block-progress-on-open-questions.sh`).
- A new NuGet package would be needed and the user has not confirmed it (version goes in `Directory.Packages.props`, never inline on the `PackageReference`).

## Done when
- Every AC listed under `tasks[<task-id>].acs_covered` has at least one test carrying `[Trait("AC", "AC-NNN")]`.
- All four phase blocks are present in `05-implementation-log.md` for this task.
- `.tdd-state.json` shows `phase: "done"` for `<task-id>` and `active_task` is cleared.
- `dotnet format --verify-no-changes` is clean and `dotnet build -c Release` produces no warnings.
- Commit reminder surfaced (Step 7); user commits before starting the next task. After all tasks done, run `/net-test` then `/net-validate`.

  "content": "using System.Net;\nusing System.Text;\nusing Microsoft.AspNetCore.Builder;\nusing Microsoft.AspNetCore.Hosting;\nusing Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http;\nusing Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Testing;\nusing Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection;\n\nnamespace CashRegister.Tests;\n\n/// <summary>\n/// The host's startup code (Program.cs) in both environments, run in the unit gate (user decision\n/// in T-017, ADR-009): error handling, CORS, OpenAPI exposure and health. The same behaviour is\n/// proved end to end by the integration suite; this keeps the composition root inside the unit\n/// coverage measurement.\n/// </summary>\npublic sealed class HostCompositionTests\n{\n    private const string ThrowingPath = \"/test-only/throw\";\n\n    private static CancellationToken Cancellation => TestContext.Current.CancellationToken;\n\n    /// <summary>Adds a route that throws, behind the host's exception handler.</summary>\n    private sealed class ThrowingEndpointFilter : IStartupFilter\n    {\n        public Action<IApplicationBuilder> Configure(Action<IApplicationBuilder> next) => app =>\n        {\n            next(app);\n            app.Map(ThrowingPath, branch => branch.Run(_ => throw new InvalidOperationException(\"boom\")));\n        };\n    }\n\n    private static WebApplicationFactory<Program> HostIn(string environment) =>\n        new WebApplicationFactory<Program>().WithWebHostBuilder(builder =>\n        {\n            builder.UseEnvironment(environment);\n            builder.ConfigureServices(services => services.AddSingleton<IStartupFilter, ThrowingEndpointFilter>());\n        });\n\n    private static async Task<bool> PreflightAllowed(HttpClient client)\n    {\n        using var request = new HttpRequestMessage(HttpMethod.Options, new Uri(\"/api/files\", UriKind.Relative));\n        request.Headers.Add(\"Origin\", \"http://localhost:5173\");\n        request.Headers.Add(\"Access-Control-Request-Method\", \"POST\");\n        var response = await client.SendAsync(request, Cancellation);\n        return response.Headers.Contains(\"Access-Control-Allow-Origin\");\n    }\n\n    [Theory]\n    [Trait(\"AC\", \"AC-015\")]\n    [InlineData(\"Development\", true, HttpStatusCode.OK)]\n    [InlineData(\"Production\", false, HttpStatusCode.NotFound)]\n    public async Task Host_ComposesTheSamePipelineInEachEnvironment(\n        string environment, bool spaOriginAllowed, HttpStatusCode openApiStatus)\n    {\n        await using var factory = HostIn(environment);\n        var client = factory.CreateClient();\n\n        (await client.GetStringAsync(new Uri(\"/health\", UriKind.Relative), Cancellation)).ShouldBe(\"Healthy\");\n\n        var badBody = await client.PutAsync(\n            new Uri(\"/api/settings/divisor\", UriKind.Relative),\n            new StringContent(\"not json\", Encoding.UTF8, \"application/json\"),\n            Cancellation);\n        badBody.StatusCode.ShouldBe(HttpStatusCode.BadRequest);\n        badBody.Content.Headers.ContentType?.MediaType.ShouldBe(\"application/problem+json\");\n\n        var crash = await client.GetAsync(new Uri(ThrowingPath, UriKind.Relative), Cancellation);\n        crash.StatusCode.ShouldBe(HttpStatusCode.InternalServerError);\n        (await crash.Content.ReadAsStringAsync(Cancellation)).ShouldNotContain(\"boom\");\n\n        (await PreflightAllowed(client)).ShouldBe(spaOriginAllowed);\n\n        (await client.GetAsync(new Uri(\"/openapi/v1.json\", UriKind.Relative), Cancellation)).StatusCode\n            .ShouldBe(openApiStatus);\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    [Trait(\"AC\", \"AC-015\")]\n    public async Task Host_WithoutACorsSection_AllowsNoOrigins()\n    {\n        await using var factory = HostIn(\"Production\").WithWebHostBuilder(builder =>\n            builder.UseSetting(\"Cors:AllowedOrigins\", null));\n\n        (await PreflightAllowed(factory.CreateClient())).ShouldBeFalse();\n    }\n}\n"
}

T-017 is done, and the harness now passes overall. Unit-test coverage is **100% line / 99.28% branch** (up from 73.2% / 75.4%), against the 90% floor.

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| format, compile | pass |
| unit | pass, 149 tests |
| it | pass, 30 tests |
| coverage (unit tests only) | **pass, 100% / 99.28%** |
| mutation | skipped (not set up) |
| contract, security, web | pass |

Traceability still shows all 28 acceptance criteria covered, with no orphaned tags.

**What changed**
- **`src`:** the file and divisor endpoint handlers went from `private` to `internal`, so tests can call them directly. Behaviour is unchanged. Because that was the only production change, the red step was a compile failure; the log says so.
- **Handler unit tests (17):**
  - upload, list and download, including every error response and the file-name clean-up;
  - divisor read and change, including the log entry and invalid values;
  - both use a small fake clock in place of the unapproved `FakeTimeProvider` package.
- **Route-table tests (2):** they build the app without starting it and confirm every endpoint path and method is registered. That pins the HTTP contract and covers the mapping code.
- **Host test (your choice):** `HostCompositionTests` runs the API's startup code in Development and in Production. It checks health, bad-JSON handling, 500s that don't leak details, CORS, and whether the OpenAPI document is served. It has no integration tag, so it counts in the unit coverage. For that, the unit test project now references the API host and `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Testing`, which is already in `Directory.Packages.props`, so there's no new package. I widened T-017's scope in the plan and state before adding it.

**Removed one test of mine:** it claimed to test a missing CORS setting, but the shipped `appsettings.json` always supplies it, so the test never reached that path. The Production host test already proves no cross-origin requests are allowed by default.

**Recorded:** ADR-009 now includes both of your coverage decisions, and the implementation log has all four phases.

New-code coverage showed `0/0` because it compares against committed history and T-017 isn't committed yet. `/net-validate` will measure it after the commit.

- `artifacts/harness-summary.json`, `artifacts/new-code-coverage.json`

## Process
1. Run `./.github/scripts/harness-dotnet.sh --report > artifacts/harness-summary.json`. Layers: format (`dotnet format --verify-no-changes`) → build (`dotnet build -c Release` with Roslyn analyzers + Meziantou.Analyzer, warnings are errors) → unit (`dotnet test --filter "Category!=Integration"`) → integration (`dotnet test --filter "Category=Integration"`) → coverage (Cobertura) → mutation (Stryker.NET, opt-in) → contract (OpenAPI diff) → vulnerable dependencies (`dotnet list package --vulnerable --include-transitive`).
2. Run `./.github/scripts/check-new-code-coverage-dotnet.sh` (env `NEW_CODE_THRESHOLD` default `0.95`, `BASE_REF` default `origin/main`). Must be ≥ 95% on changed lines.
3. Run `./.github/scripts/traceability-dotnet.sh <feature-id>`. Any AC with zero tests = FAIL. An AC whose only test lacks `[Trait("AC", ...)]` reads as uncovered — report it as a missing tag, not as missing behavior.
4. Aggregate the gates — `unit`, `it`, `coverage`, `mutation` — plus new-code coverage and traceability. Coverage floor is 0.90 line and branch overall, 0.95 on new code. Verdict is `PASS` only if every gate is `pass` or `skipped`; a `skipped` mutation gate (no `stryker-config.json`) is expected and is **not** a failure. A `Survived` mutant in changed code fails unless ADR-justified.
5. Diff every metric against `.specs/_baseline.json`. Anything that worsened is a finding, severity per `.claude/checklists/validation-gates.md`.
6. Write `07-validation-report.md` with: verdict, gate table, coverage detail (overall, per-project, new code), mutation detail or the reason the gate is `skipped`, OpenAPI contract diff (breaking / non-breaking) against `artifacts/openapi/openapi.json`, vulnerable-dependency advisories and waivers, baseline diff, top failing items, artifact links, recommended next action.

## Refuse if
- `04-tasks.md` shows any task not `done`.
- The harness was bypassed or a cached result was reused — always re-run.
- A skip or threshold-lowering flag would be needed (`forbid-skip-flags.sh` blocks the underlying `dotnet` invocation; `COVERAGE_FLOOR`, `NEW_CODE_THRESHOLD` and `MUTATION_THRESHOLD` are never lowered).
- A report is missing for a layer `_stack.json` says is configured — that is an `error`, not a `pass`.
- Any `Q-NNN` is unresolved in the spec or design (`block-progress-on-open-questions.sh`).
- A waiver has no covering ADR.

## Done when
- `07-validation-report.md` and `07a-traceability.md` exist with a clear verdict.
- Every gate is accounted for, including the reason for any `skipped` layer.
- If `PASS`, the user is pointed to `/net-review`. If `FAIL`, the report lists the smallest set of `/net-build` or `/net-test` actions needed to recover.

# /net-review

**Phase:** 6 — pre-commit code review
**Owning agent:** `.claude/agents/dotnet-code-reviewer.md`
**Skills used:** `dotnet-code-review-rubric`, `clarity-over-cleverness`, `dotnet-10-conventions`, `dotnet-security-baseline`, `efcore-10-data-access`, `dotnet-observability-ops`

## Purpose
Run a structured self-review of the diff before the user commits. Produces `08-code-review.md` with categorized findings.

## Inputs
- `<feature-id>` (optional; defaults to the most recent feature).
- `--base <ref>` (optional; defaults to `origin/main`).

## Reads
- `git diff <base>...HEAD` for changed `*.cs`, test, `*.csproj`, `Directory.Build.props`, `Directory.Packages.props`, `.editorconfig`, EF Core migration and OpenAPI files.
- `.specs/<feature-id>/01-spec.md`, `03-design.md`, `07-validation-report.md`, `07a-traceability.md`
- `.claude/skills/dotnet-code-review-rubric/SKILL.md` (the rubric is authoritative)
- `.claude/templates/code-review.template.md`

## Writes
- `.specs/<feature-id>/08-code-review.md`

## Process
1. Refuse if `07-validation-report.md` verdict is not `PASS`.
2. Walk every changed file. Evaluate each against the rubric categories: traceability, slice and module boundaries, Minimal API idioms (`TypedResults`, endpoint filters, FluentValidation), error handling (`ProblemDetails` only, no `ex.Message` to clients), EF Core data access (no startup migrations, `AsNoTracking` projections, mandatory capped pagination, no N+1), nullable discipline, async correctness (`CancellationToken` threaded, no sync-over-async, no `async void`), security, observability, test quality, clarity, conventions, packaging.
3. Classify findings as `must-fix`, `should-fix`, `nit`, or `praise`. Include file + line range + suggested change for `must-fix` and `should-fix`.
4. Cross-check: every AC in `01-spec.md` is exercised by at least one test carrying `[Trait("AC", "AC-NNN")]` in the diff (or already merged), and every integration test in the diff also carries `[Trait("Category", "Integration")]`.
5. Flag any added `NoWarn` entry, `#pragma warning disable` without a reason comment, `!` null-forgiving operator without justification, or inline `Version` attribute on a `PackageReference` (versions belong in `Directory.Packages.props`).
6. If any `must-fix` exists, recommend `/net-build` or `/net-code-simplify`. Do NOT auto-apply fixes.
7. Emit summary line: counts by severity + recommended next action.

## Refuse if
- `07-validation-report.md` is missing or its verdict is not `PASS`.
- The diff is empty.
- Any `Q-NNN` is unresolved in the spec or design.
- A finding is accepted without fixing it and has no covering ADR.

## Done when
- `08-code-review.md` exists with every rubric category answered and a verdict of `Approve`, `Approve with waivers`, or `Request changes`.
- If zero `must-fix`, the agent prints the suggested commit message and tells the user to run `git commit` themselves (the agent never commits).
- If `must-fix` findings remain, the smallest recovery command is named.

````
## Severity ladder

- **blocker** — must fix before commit. (Security hole, broken behavior, gate-bypass.)
- **major** — must fix before commit OR document as ADR + waiver.
- **minor** — should fix; leave a note if not.
- **nit** — taste; mention once, don't insist.

### 3. Minimal API idioms

Apply `dotnet-10-conventions`. Look for:

- `TypedResults.*` returned, not `Results.*`, and the endpoint's return type is
  `Results<Ok<T>, ProblemHttpResult>` or similar — not bare `IResult`.
- Every error path returns ProblemDetails. No ad-hoc error envelope, no bare string body.
- Validation runs in an endpoint filter (`AddEndpointFilter<ValidationFilter>`), not inside the
  handler and not via `if (!ModelState.IsValid)`.
- **No logic in `Program.cs`** — it composes and maps. Any `if`, loop, or business expression
  there is `major`; extract to an extension method that can be tested.
- Endpoints registered via a per-slice `MapXxx(this IEndpointRouteBuilder)` extension, not a
  hundred inline lambdas in `Program.cs`.
- Handlers are static or take their dependencies as parameters; no service-locator
  `IServiceProvider.GetService` in a handler.
- Mapster mappings configured centrally; no hand-written 40-line mapper next to a generated one.
- No MVC controllers, `[ApiController]`, or `ActionResult<T>` added to a Minimal API codebase.

### 4. Error handling
### 9. Test quality

- Tests fail for the right reason — re-read the red excerpt in `05-implementation-log.md`.
- **One behavior per test.** A test with three unrelated `Should*` blocks and three arrange
  sections is three tests.
- **Shouldly assertions only** (`result.Status.ShouldBe(...)`). No `Assert.Equal`, no FluentAssertions.
- **NSubstitute only. No Moq** — any `Moq` using directive or `new Mock<T>()` is `blocker`.
- **Narrowest scope that proves the behavior**: a plain unit test over a handler beats a
  `WebApplicationFactory` test; a `WebApplicationFactory` test beats a Testcontainers test.
  A container-backed test for logic that has no database in it is `major`.
- Integration tests use `Respawn` between tests for isolation, and Testcontainers for real
  dependencies — no shared mutable static state, no ordering dependence between tests.
- `Verify.XUnit` snapshots reviewed in the diff, not blindly accepted. A `.received.*` file
  committed is `blocker`.
- **No skipped tests** — `Skip = "..."` needs an issue reference and an ADR; `Skip` with no
  reason is `blocker`.
- **Deterministic time.** No `DateTime.Now`/`UtcNow` or `DateTimeOffset.UtcNow` in production
  code under test — inject `TimeProvider` and use `FakeTimeProvider` in tests. No `Thread.Sleep`
  or `Task.Delay` as a synchronisation mechanism.
- No removed or weakened assertion in the diff. Coverage holds; new code ≥ 0.95 line and branch.
- If `stryker-config.json` exists, survived mutants in changed files are all killed or
  ADR-waived. If it does not, the `mutation` gate reporting `skipped` is expected, not a finding.

### 10. Clarity over cleverness
## Findings table format

```markdown
| ID | Severity | Section | File | Line | Finding | Suggested fix |
|----|---------|---------|------|------|---------|---------------|
| F-001 | blocker | security | src/Ordering/Features/Orders/CreateOrderEndpoint.cs | 34 | `.AllowAnonymous()` on a state-changing POST, no comment or ADR | apply `RequireAuthorization("orders:write")` |
| F-002 | major | data-access | src/Ordering/Features/Orders/GetOrdersHandler.cs | 21 | list query has no `Take` and no `AsNoTracking` | add page-size ceiling + `AsNoTracking()` |
| F-003 | minor | clarity | src/Ordering/Features/Orders/Pricing.cs | 58 | `0.10m` repeated in three places | extract `MemberDiscountRate` constant |
```

Every finding carries a `file:line`. A finding without one is not actionable and must not be
written.

## Reviewer conduct

The reviewer **reports; it does not repair.**

- Never commit, never stage, never push.
- Never edit production code, tests, configuration, or a migration. If a fix is obvious, put the
  fix in the *Suggested fix* column as text.
- Never re-run the harness to "see if it passes now" after suggesting a change.
- Never raise a finding without reading the file at the cited line.
- Every waiver requires an ADR under `.specs/<feature-id>/adr/`; a waiver recorded in
  `08-code-review.md` with no ADR is itself a blocker.

## Verdict

End `08-code-review.md` with one of:

- ✅ **Approve** — no blockers; minors noted; safe to commit.
- ⚠️ **Approve with waivers** — blockers/majors waived via the listed ADRs; commit OK.
- ❌ **Request changes** — blockers exist, no waivers; commit blocked.

## Assistant · 2026-09-21T22:02:04.782Z

The review requests changes: one major finding blocks the commit. The report is in [08-code-review.md](.specs/2026-09-21-cash-register-change-calculation/08-code-review.md). I reviewed the **whole feature (`9b945d3...HEAD`)** rather than just since `origin/main`, because you'd pushed T-001 to T-012 without a review and `origin/main` would have skipped most of the backend. I didn't change any code.

**Summary: 1 major, 6 minor, 3 nit, 4 praise, 0 blockers.**

**The blocker, F-001 (major):** [Program.cs](src/CashRegister.Api/Program.cs#L7-L36) contains logic: two Development-only branches, a status-code ternary and a `?? []` fallback. The review rules count any `if` or expression in `Program.cs` as major, because it can only be tested by booting the whole host; that's why `HostCompositionTests` had to exist. The fix is to move this setup into testable methods, `AddCashRegisterHost()` and `UseCashRegisterHost()`, leaving `Program.cs` as just build → use → map → run.

**Minors (recommended, not blocking)**

| ID | Problem | File |
|---|---|---|
| F-002 | An upload over 1 MB returns a generic **400 "Bad Request"** with no detail, so the UI can only say "Bad Request". I confirmed this against the running API. It should be a 413 "File too large", with a test. | `FileEndpoints.cs:29` |
| F-003 | The divisor is validated inside the handler, but the design says built-in validation. | `DivisorEndpoints.cs:35` |
| F-004 | The design doc has drifted from the code: the validation approach and the `FileProcessed` log fields. | `03-design.md:151, 194` |
| F-005 | The harness script splits paths that contain spaces on Windows. | `harness.mjs:27` |
| F-006 | Three web tests wait on a 20 ms timer instead of waiting for what they expect. | three `*.test.tsx` files |
| F-007 | One host test checks five separate behaviours. | `HostCompositionTests.cs:53-76` |

**Nits:** the logged "old divisor" can be stale under concurrent changes; the security gate counts the word "High" anywhere in `dotnet list` output; and owed `0.00` always gets random change, which fits the spec but isn't written down.

**Checks that passed:**
- every acceptance criterion is tagged and every integration test carries its trait;
- no `NoWarn`, `#pragma` or inline package versions;
- the two `!` operators both have a justifying comment;
- no Moq, `Assert.` or `Sleep` in the tests;
- the cancellation token reaches every async call;
- every error path returns ProblemDetails;
- waivers rely on ADR-002, ADR-005 and ADR-009.

**To unblock, pick one:**
- **Fix it:** add task T-018 "Extract host composition from Program.cs" and run `/net-build T-018`. F-002 and F-003 could go in the same task.
- **Waive it:** record an ADR accepting the environment switches in `Program.cs`. The verdict then becomes "Approve with waivers".

Let me know which, and whether T-018 should include any of the minors.

  "content": "using CashRegister.Api;\nusing Microsoft.AspNetCore.Builder;\nusing Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http;\nusing Microsoft.AspNetCore.Routing;\nusing Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration;\nusing Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection;\nusing Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Console;\nusing Microsoft.Extensions.Options;\n\nnamespace CashRegister.Tests;\n\n/// <summary>Host composition as plain, testable functions (review finding F-001, T-018).</summary>\npublic sealed class HostSetupTests\n{\n    private static WebApplication BuildApp(string environment)\n    {\n        var builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(new WebApplicationOptions { EnvironmentName = environment });\n        builder.AddCashRegisterHost();\n        var app = builder.Build();\n        app.UseCashRegisterHost();\n        return app;\n    }\n\n    private static List<string> RoutePatterns(WebApplication app) =>\n    [\n        .. ((IEndpointRouteBuilder)app).DataSources\n            .SelectMany(source => source.Endpoints)\n            .OfType<RouteEndpoint>()\n            .Select(endpoint => endpoint.RoutePattern.RawText ?? string.Empty),\n    ];\n\n    [Theory]\n    [Trait(\"AC\", \"AC-015\")]\n    [InlineData(StatusCodes.Status400BadRequest)]\n    [InlineData(StatusCodes.Status413PayloadTooLarge)]\n    public void StatusCodeFor_BadRequestException_KeepsItsOwnStatus(int status)\n    {\n        HostSetup.StatusCodeFor(new BadHttpRequestException(\"bad request\", status)).ShouldBe(status);\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    [Trait(\"AC\", \"AC-015\")]\n    public void StatusCodeFor_AnyOtherException_Is500()\n    {\n        HostSetup.StatusCodeFor(new InvalidOperationException(\"boom\")).ShouldBe(StatusCodes.Status500InternalServerError);\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    [Trait(\"AC\", \"AC-015\")]\n    public void AllowedOrigins_ConfiguredList_IsReturned()\n    {\n        var configuration = new ConfigurationBuilder()\n            .AddInMemoryCollection(new Dictionary<string, string?> { [\"Cors:AllowedOrigins:0\"] = \"http://localhost:5173\" })\n            .Build();\n\n        HostSetup.AllowedOrigins(configuration).ShouldBe([\"http://localhost:5173\"]);\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    [Trait(\"AC\", \"AC-015\")]\n    public void AllowedOrigins_MissingSection_IsEmpty()\n    {\n        HostSetup.AllowedOrigins(new ConfigurationBuilder().Build()).ShouldBeEmpty();\n    }\n\n    [Theory]\n    [Trait(\"AC\", \"AC-015\")]\n    [InlineData(\"Production\", ConsoleFormatterNames.Json)]\n    [InlineData(\"Development\", ConsoleFormatterNames.Simple)]\n    public async Task AddCashRegisterHost_UsesJsonConsoleLogsOutsideDevelopmentOnly(string environment, string formatter)\n    {\n        await using var app = BuildApp(environment);\n\n        var options = app.Services.GetRequiredService<IOptions<ConsoleLoggerOptions>>().Value;\n\n        (options.FormatterName ?? ConsoleFormatterNames.Simple).ShouldBe(formatter);\n    }\n\n    [Theory]\n    [Trait(\"AC\", \"AC-015\")]\n    [InlineData(\"Development\", true)]\n    [InlineData(\"Production\", false)]\n    public async Task UseCashRegisterHost_MapsOpenApiInDevelopmentOnly(string environment, bool openApiMapped)\n    {\n        await using var app = BuildApp(environment);\n\n        RoutePatterns(app).Any(pattern => pattern.Contains(\"openapi\", StringComparison.Ordinal)).ShouldBe(openApiMapped);\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    [Trait(\"AC\", \"AC-015\")]\n    public async Task UseCashRegisterHost_MapsHealthAndTheModuleEndpoints()\n    {\n        await using var app = BuildApp(\"Production\");\n\n        var routes = RoutePatterns(app);\n\n        routes.ShouldContain(\"/health\");\n        routes.ShouldContain(\"/api/files/\");\n        routes.ShouldContain(\"/api/settings/divisor/\");\n    }\n}\n"

  "content": "namespace CashRegister.Api;\n\n/// <summary>\n/// Host composition: everything <c>Program.cs</c> used to decide inline, as extension methods and\n/// small functions that unit tests can call (code review F-001).\n/// </summary>\npublic static class HostSetup\n{\n    /// <summary>The CORS policy that admits the configured UI origins (ADR-005).</summary>\n    public const string SpaCorsPolicy = \"Spa\";\n\n    private const string AllowedOriginsKey = \"Cors:AllowedOrigins\";\n    private const string HealthPath = \"/health\";\n\n    /// <summary>Registers logging, error handling, health, OpenAPI, CORS and the CashRegister module.</summary>\n    public static WebApplicationBuilder AddCashRegisterHost(this WebApplicationBuilder builder)\n    {\n        ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(builder);\n\n        if (!builder.Environment.IsDevelopment())\n        {\n            builder.Logging.AddJsonConsole(); // ADR-008: structured logs outside Development\n        }\n\n        builder.Services.AddProblemDetails();\n        builder.Services.AddExceptionHandler(options => options.StatusCodeSelector = StatusCodeFor);\n        builder.Services.AddHealthChecks();\n        builder.Services.AddOpenApi();\n\n        var allowedOrigins = AllowedOrigins(builder.Configuration);\n        builder.Services.AddCors(options => options.AddPolicy(SpaCorsPolicy, policy =>\n            policy.WithOrigins(allowedOrigins).AllowAnyHeader().AllowAnyMethod()));\n\n        builder.Services.AddCashRegister(builder.Configuration);\n        return builder;\n    }\n\n    /// <summary>Builds the request pipeline and maps health, OpenAPI (Development only) and the module endpoints.</summary>\n    public static WebApplication UseCashRegisterHost(this WebApplication app)\n    {\n        ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(app);\n\n        app.UseExceptionHandler();\n        app.UseStatusCodePages();\n        app.UseCors(SpaCorsPolicy);\n\n        if (app.Environment.IsDevelopment())\n        {\n            app.MapOpenApi();\n        }\n\n        app.MapHealthChecks(HealthPath);\n        app.MapCashRegister();\n        return app;\n    }\n\n    /// <summary>\n    /// Status code for an unhandled exception. Malformed request bodies surface as\n    /// <see cref=\"BadHttpRequestException\"/> (thrown in Development) and keep their own 4xx status;\n    /// anything else is a 500.\n    /// </summary>\n    internal static int StatusCodeFor(Exception exception)\n    {\n        if (exception is BadHttpRequestException badRequest)\n        {\n            return badRequest.StatusCode;\n        }\n\n        return StatusCodes.Status500InternalServerError;\n    }\n\n    /// <summary>Origins allowed to call the API from a browser; none when the section is absent.</summary>\n    internal static string[] AllowedOrigins(IConfiguration configuration) =>\n        configuration.GetSection(AllowedOriginsKey).Get<string[]>() ?? [];\n}\n"
}

## Assistant · 2026-09-21T22:14:10.099Z

F-001 is fixed (task T-018), and the review verdict is now **Approve**.

**What changed**
- **`HostSetup.cs` (new, in the API project):** holds everything `Program.cs` used to decide inline.
  - `AddCashRegisterHost()` registers JSON logging outside Development, ProblemDetails, the error-status selector, health checks, OpenAPI, CORS and the module.
  - `UseCashRegisterHost()` builds the pipeline: error handling, CORS, OpenAPI in Development only, `/health`, and the endpoints.
  - `StatusCodeFor` and `AllowedOrigins` are small functions that tests can call directly.
- **[Program.cs](src/CashRegister.Api/Program.cs)** is now just: create the builder → `AddCashRegisterHost()` → build → `UseCashRegisterHost()` → run. There are no branches or expressions left.
- **`HostSetupTests`**, 10 unit cases:
  - bad-request errors keep their own status (400, 413) and everything else becomes 500;
  - CORS origins come from config, with none when the section is missing;
  - JSON logging applies only outside Development;
  - OpenAPI is mapped only in Development;
  - `/health` and the module routes are registered.
- **`CashRegister.Api.csproj`:** now lets `CashRegister.Tests` see internal members. I added it to T-018's scope before editing it.

**Results:** 189/189 tests pass (159 unit, 30 integration). All the existing host and integration tests pass unchanged, so behaviour is the same. The harness passes overall, and unit coverage is **100% line and 100% branch**. The CORS fallback branch that Gap-003 had marked won't-fix is now covered, so Gap-003 is closed.

**Still open (recommendations only, not blocking):** F-002 to F-007 and the three nits. F-002, the unhelpful "Bad Request" for uploads over 1 MB, is the most user-visible; I can plan it as T-019 if you want.

Commit everything, including the review document. Suggested message:
```
refactor(api): extract host composition from Program.cs into testable HostSetup (T-018, review F-001)
```

## Assistant · 2026-09-21T22:15:08.472Z

Yes, the UI is built. It's a React + TypeScript app in `web/`, done in tasks T-013 to T-015, and it covers the whole flow:
- **Upload transactions:** choose a file and upload it. It shows the result ("Processed input.txt: 3 lines, 1 with errors") or the server's error, e.g. "Too many lines".
- **Uploaded files:** a table of files, newest first, with a **Download** link per file for its change output.
- **Random change rule:** view and change the divisor, with a warning when it's set to 1.

The production bundle exists in `web/dist/`: the harness's last run built it and passed lint, typecheck, 30 tests and coverage.

To see it:
```bash
# terminal 1: API on http://localhost:5080
dotnet run --project src/CashRegister.Api

# terminal 2: UI on http://localhost:5173 (forwards /api to the API)
cd web && npm run dev
```
Then open http://localhost:5173 and upload `samples/input.txt`.

I've tested the components and checked the API live, but I haven't clicked through the UI in a real browser myself. Want me to launch both and take a screenshot of it working?

{
  "file_path": "C:\\dev\\CashRegister\\src\\CashRegister.Api\\Dockerfile",
  "content": "# CashRegister API. Build from the repository root (the build needs global.json and the shared\n# Directory.*.props files):\n#   docker build -f src/CashRegister.Api/Dockerfile -t cashregister-api .\n\nFROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:10.0 AS build\nWORKDIR /repo\n\n# Restore first, from project files only, so the restore layer is cached until dependencies change.\nCOPY global.json Directory.Build.props Directory.Packages.props .editorconfig ./\nCOPY src/CashRegister/CashRegister.csproj src/CashRegister/\nCOPY src/CashRegister.Api/CashRegister.Api.csproj src/CashRegister.Api/\nRUN dotnet restore src/CashRegister.Api/CashRegister.Api.csproj\n\nCOPY src/ src/\nRUN dotnet publish src/CashRegister.Api/CashRegister.Api.csproj -c Release -o /app --no-restore\n\nFROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:10.0 AS runtime\nWORKDIR /app\nCOPY --from=build /app .\n\n# The aspnet image listens on 8080 and ships a non-root \"app\" user.\nENV ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Production\nEXPOSE 8080\nUSER $APP_UID\nENTRYPOINT [\"dotnet\", \"CashRegister.Api.dll\"]\n"
}
```

{
  "file_path": "C:\\dev\\CashRegister\\web\\Dockerfile",
  "content": "# CashRegister UI: builds the Vite app, then serves it with nginx, which also forwards /api and\n# /health to the API container so the browser talks to a single origin.\n#   docker build -t cashregister-web web\n\nFROM node:24-alpine AS build\nWORKDIR /web\n\nCOPY package.json package-lock.json ./\nRUN npm ci\n\nCOPY . .\nRUN npm run build\n\nFROM nginx:1.29-alpine AS runtime\nCOPY nginx.conf /etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf\nCOPY --from=build /web/dist /usr/share/nginx/html\nEXPOSE 80\n"
}

### Tool call: Write · 2026-09-21T22:16:09.516Z

```
{
  "file_path": "C:\\dev\\CashRegister\\web\\nginx.conf",
  "content": "server {\n    listen 80;\n    server_name _;\n\n    root /usr/share/nginx/html;\n    index index.html;\n\n    # A little above the API's own 1 MB upload limit, so oversize uploads get the API's\n    # ProblemDetails response instead of an nginx HTML error page.\n    client_max_body_size 2m;\n\n    location /api/ {\n        proxy_pass http://api:8080;\n        proxy_set_header Host $host;\n        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;\n        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;\n    }\n\n    location = /health {\n        proxy_pass http://api:8080;\n    }\n\n    # Single-page app: unknown paths fall back to index.html.\n    location / {\n        try_files $uri $uri/ /index.html;\n    }\n}\n"
}
```

## Assistant · 2026-09-21T22:21:21.441Z

`docker compose up --build` now builds and runs both projects together. I built and tested it here.

**How to use it**
- **UI:** http://localhost:8080. nginx serves the React app and forwards `/api` and `/health` to the API. Because the browser only talks to one origin, no CORS setup is needed.
- **API:** also reachable directly at http://localhost:5080, e.g. for `curl`.
- **Stop:** `docker compose down`. Uploaded files and the divisor are kept in memory, so they reset when the API container restarts.

**What I checked with the stack running**
- The UI page loads, and deep links fall back to the app.
- `/health` works through nginx and directly.
- Uploading `samples/input.txt` returns 201. The output's first two lines match the README exactly, and the random third line adds up to 167¢.
- A 1.5 MB upload gets the API's own error response rather than an nginx error page, because nginx allows up to 2 MB and leaves the 1 MB limit to the API.
- The API container runs as a non-root user.

**New files**
- `docker-compose.yml`: two services, `api` on host port 5080 and `web` on host port 8080.
- `src/CashRegister.Api/Dockerfile`: builds with the .NET 10 SDK and runs on the smaller ASP.NET runtime image in Production mode. Dependencies are restored in their own layer so rebuilds stay fast.
- `web/Dockerfile` and `web/nginx.conf`: build with Node 24, then serve with nginx, which also forwards the API calls.
- `.dockerignore` and `web/.dockerignore`: keep build output, `node_modules`, tests and specs out of the images.
- **README:** a "With Docker" section under "Running it".

The containers are still running, so you can open http://localhost:8080 now; `docker compose down` stops them.

T-018 isn't committed yet either. I'd commit it first, then the Docker files separately:
```
build: add Dockerfiles and docker-compose to run API and UI together
```

**Optional clean-up** (reviewer minors and nits, none blocking)

- A `.specs/_baseline.json`, so future validation runs can report regressions.

**Planned for v2, not part of "done":** authentication, persistence, other currencies (for example EUR for the France client), OpenTelemetry, and localised output.

If you want the short path: commit, push, `/net-ship`, then open the PR. Shall I start with F-002 or with the PR description?

## User · 2026-09-22T14:53:34.591Z

# /net-ship

**Phase:** 8 — ship (post-commit, pre-deploy hygiene)
**Owning agent:** `.claude/agents/dotnet-code-reviewer.md` (reused; no new persona)
**Skills used:** `shipping-and-launch`, `dotnet-security-baseline`, `efcore-10-data-access`, `dotnet-observability-ops`

## Purpose
After `/net-review` approves the diff and the user commits, produce a structured ship plan that verifies pre-deploy gates, captures rollback + observability + flag posture, plans the staged rollout, and drafts release notes. The agent **never deploys** — it prints the deploy command for the user to run.

## Inputs
- `<feature-id>` (optional; defaults to the most recent feature with an `08-code-review.md` verdict of `Approve` or `Approve with waivers`).
- `--base <ref>` (optional; defaults to `origin/main`) for diff and release-note generation.

## Reads
- `.specs/<feature-id>/01-spec.md` — `## Goal`, AC list, any open `Q-NNN`.
- `.specs/<feature-id>/03-design.md` — EF Core migration plan, security posture, any open `Q-NNN`.
- `.specs/<feature-id>/04-tasks.md` — `files_in_scope` for the diff-scope check.
- `.specs/<feature-id>/07-validation-report.md` — verdict must be `PASS`.
- `.specs/<feature-id>/08-code-review.md` — verdict must be `Approve` or `Approve with waivers`.
- `.specs/_baseline.json` — for the regression check.
- `artifacts/harness-summary.json`, `artifacts/openapi/openapi.json` — gate results and the shipped contract.
- `git diff <base>...HEAD` and `git log <base>..HEAD` — for migration classification, new-endpoint detection, release-note drafting.
- `.claude/skills/shipping-and-launch/SKILL.md` (authoritative behavior).
- `.claude/templates/ship-plan.template.md`.

## Writes
- `.specs/<feature-id>/09-ship-plan.md`

## Process
1. **Resolve feature.** If no `<feature-id>`, pick the most recent feature with `08-code-review.md` verdict `Approve*`. Refuse if none.
2. **Verify pre-ship gates** (per `shipping-and-launch`): validation `PASS`, review `Approve*`, zero unresolved `Q-NNN`, no baseline regression, every changed file in some task's `files_in_scope`. Halt at the first FAIL with the specific recovery command.
3. **Classify migrations.** Walk the EF Core migration classes in the diff (`src/<Module>/**/Migrations/**`). Tag each: forward-only safe / expand / contract / breaking. Generate the idempotent script the operator will apply — `dotnet ef migrations script --idempotent` — and attach it to the plan; migrations are never applied at app startup. Halt on `breaking` without an ADR.
4. **Inventory new surface.** New Minimal API endpoints, message handlers, background services, typed `HttpClient`s. For each, verify the diff registers instrumentation — an OpenTelemetry `ActivitySource` span and a `Meter` counter — and that liveness/readiness HealthChecks still cover any new dependency. Halt on missing instrumentation.
5. **Render the ship plan.** Fill `.claude/templates/ship-plan.template.md` — every section non-empty (`n/a` allowed only with a one-line reason).
6. **Surface human-required inputs as `Q-NNN`.** Flag owner, alert thresholds, rollout cohorts. Halt until the user answers; do not invent.
7. **Draft release notes.** Two sections: external (plain English, ≤ 3 bullets, edited by the user before publishing) and internal (diff summary, AC list, ADR links, migration class, flag name, dashboard).
8. **Print deploy command.** Suggest the team's release-pipeline trigger, or the `dotnet publish -c Release` / container image build-and-push line, plus the `dotnet ef migrations script --idempotent` output to apply first. The agent never executes any of it.

## Refuse if
- `07-validation-report.md` verdict is not `PASS`.
- `08-code-review.md` verdict is not `Approve` or `Approve with waivers`.
- Any `Q-NNN` is unresolved in the spec or design.
- A migration in the diff is `breaking` and there is no covering ADR.
- A new endpoint, handler, or background service has no `ActivitySource` span and `Meter` registration in the diff.
- The diff edits a previously-released EF Core migration (a rename or a changed `Up`/`Down` body for a migration already applied in any environment).
- The OpenAPI contract diff reports a breaking change with no covering ADR and no versioning plan.
- The diff is empty (nothing to ship).

## Done when
`09-ship-plan.md` exists with all seven sections filled, every gate in the pre-ship table is `PASS`, migrations are classified with named rollback steps and an idempotent script, every new endpoint has at least one named metric and one alert (or a documented "no alert" reason), and release notes have both external and internal sections. The agent then prints the suggested deploy command for the user to execute manually — it never deploys.

## User · 2026-09-22T14:57:03.179Z

# /net-validate

**Phase:** 5 — validate (run the harness)
**Owning agent:** `.claude/agents/dotnet-validator.md`
**Skills used:** `harness-report-parsing`, `dotnet-coverage-and-mutation`, `requirements-traceability`, `dotnet-architecture-rules`, `dotnet-build-harness`

## Purpose
Run the full .NET harness, parse the output, and write `07-validation-report.md` with a single `PASS` / `FAIL` verdict.

## Inputs
- `<feature-id>` (optional; if omitted, reports across all changes since `origin/main`).

## Reads
- `./.github/scripts/harness-dotnet.sh`, `./.github/scripts/check-new-code-coverage-dotnet.sh`, `./.github/scripts/traceability-dotnet.sh`
- `artifacts/harness-summary.json`, `artifacts/coverage/cobertura.xml`, `artifacts/new-code-coverage.json`, `artifacts/openapi/openapi.json` (after the run)
- `.specs/_stack.json` (which layers are configured), `.specs/_baseline.json` (brownfield deltas)
- `.specs/<feature-id>/01-spec.md`, `04-tasks.md`, `06-test-plan.md` (for AC mapping)
- `.claude/templates/validation-report.template.md`, `.claude/checklists/validation-gates.md`

## Writes
- `.specs/<feature-id>/07-validation-report.md`
- `.specs/<feature-id>/07a-traceability.md` (regenerated)
- `artifacts/harness-summary.json`, `artifacts/new-code-coverage.json`

## Process
1. Run `./.github/scripts/harness-dotnet.sh --report > artifacts/harness-summary.json`. Layers: format (`dotnet format --verify-no-changes`) → build (`dotnet build -c Release` with Roslyn analyzers + Meziantou.Analyzer, warnings are errors) → unit (`dotnet test --filter "Category!=Integration"`) → integration (`dotnet test --filter "Category=Integration"`) → coverage (Cobertura) → mutation (Stryker.NET, opt-in) → contract (OpenAPI diff) → vulnerable dependencies (`dotnet list package --vulnerable --include-transitive`).
2. Run `./.github/scripts/check-new-code-coverage-dotnet.sh` (env `NEW_CODE_THRESHOLD` default `0.95`, `BASE_REF` default `origin/main`). Must be ≥ 95% on changed lines.
3. Run `./.github/scripts/traceability-dotnet.sh <feature-id>`. Any AC with zero tests = FAIL. An AC whose only test lacks `[Trait("AC", ...)]` reads as uncovered — report it as a missing tag, not as missing behavior.
4. Aggregate the gates — `unit`, `it`, `coverage`, `mutation` — plus new-code coverage and traceability. Coverage floor is 0.90 line and branch overall, 0.95 on new code. Verdict is `PASS` only if every gate is `pass` or `skipped`; a `skipped` mutation gate (no `stryker-config.json`) is expected and is **not** a failure. A `Survived` mutant in changed code fails unless ADR-justified.
5. Diff every metric against `.specs/_baseline.json`. Anything that worsened is a finding, severity per `.claude/checklists/validation-gates.md`.
6. Write `07-validation-report.md` with: verdict, gate table, coverage detail (overall, per-project, new code), mutation detail or the reason the gate is `skipped`, OpenAPI contract diff (breaking / non-breaking) against `artifacts/openapi/openapi.json`, vulnerable-dependency advisories and waivers, baseline diff, top failing items, artifact links, recommended next action.

## Refuse if
- `04-tasks.md` shows any task not `done`.
- The harness was bypassed or a cached result was reused — always re-run.
- A skip or threshold-lowering flag would be needed (`forbid-skip-flags.sh` blocks the underlying `dotnet` invocation; `COVERAGE_FLOOR`, `NEW_CODE_THRESHOLD` and `MUTATION_THRESHOLD` are never lowered).
- A report is missing for a layer `_stack.json` says is configured — that is an `error`, not a `pass`.
- Any `Q-NNN` is unresolved in the spec or design (`block-progress-on-open-questions.sh`).
- A waiver has no covering ADR.

## Done when
- `07-validation-report.md` and `07a-traceability.md` exist with a clear verdict.
- Every gate is accounted for, including the reason for any `skipped` layer.
- If `PASS`, the user is pointed to `/net-review`. If `FAIL`, the report lists the smallest set of `/net-build` or `/net-test` actions needed to recover.

## User · 2026-09-22T15:01:47.682Z

# /net-ship

**Phase:** 8 — ship (post-commit, pre-deploy hygiene)
**Owning agent:** `.claude/agents/dotnet-code-reviewer.md` (reused; no new persona)
**Skills used:** `shipping-and-launch`, `dotnet-security-baseline`, `efcore-10-data-access`, `dotnet-observability-ops`

## Purpose
After `/net-review` approves the diff and the user commits, produce a structured ship plan that verifies pre-deploy gates, captures rollback + observability + flag posture, plans the staged rollout, and drafts release notes. The agent **never deploys** — it prints the deploy command for the user to run.

## Inputs
- `<feature-id>` (optional; defaults to the most recent feature with an `08-code-review.md` verdict of `Approve` or `Approve with waivers`).
- `--base <ref>` (optional; defaults to `origin/main`) for diff and release-note generation.

## Reads
- `.specs/<feature-id>/01-spec.md` — `## Goal`, AC list, any open `Q-NNN`.
- `.specs/<feature-id>/03-design.md` — EF Core migration plan, security posture, any open `Q-NNN`.
- `.specs/<feature-id>/04-tasks.md` — `files_in_scope` for the diff-scope check.
- `.specs/<feature-id>/07-validation-report.md` — verdict must be `PASS`.
- `.specs/<feature-id>/08-code-review.md` — verdict must be `Approve` or `Approve with waivers`.
- `.specs/_baseline.json` — for the regression check.
- `artifacts/harness-summary.json`, `artifacts/openapi/openapi.json` — gate results and the shipped contract.
- `git diff <base>...HEAD` and `git log <base>..HEAD` — for migration classification, new-endpoint detection, release-note drafting.
- `.claude/skills/shipping-and-launch/SKILL.md` (authoritative behavior).
- `.claude/templates/ship-plan.template.md`.

## Writes
- `.specs/<feature-id>/09-ship-plan.md`

## Process
1. **Resolve feature.** If no `<feature-id>`, pick the most recent feature with `08-code-review.md` verdict `Approve*`. Refuse if none.
2. **Verify pre-ship gates** (per `shipping-and-launch`): validation `PASS`, review `Approve*`, zero unresolved `Q-NNN`, no baseline regression, every changed file in some task's `files_in_scope`. Halt at the first FAIL with the specific recovery command.
3. **Classify migrations.** Walk the EF Core migration classes in the diff (`src/<Module>/**/Migrations/**`). Tag each: forward-only safe / expand / contract / breaking. Generate the idempotent script the operator will apply — `dotnet ef migrations script --idempotent` — and attach it to the plan; migrations are never applied at app startup. Halt on `breaking` without an ADR.
4. **Inventory new surface.** New Minimal API endpoints, message handlers, background services, typed `HttpClient`s. For each, verify the diff registers instrumentation — an OpenTelemetry `ActivitySource` span and a `Meter` counter — and that liveness/readiness HealthChecks still cover any new dependency. Halt on missing instrumentation.
5. **Render the ship plan.** Fill `.claude/templates/ship-plan.template.md` — every section non-empty (`n/a` allowed only with a one-line reason).
6. **Surface human-required inputs as `Q-NNN`.** Flag owner, alert thresholds, rollout cohorts. Halt until the user answers; do not invent.
7. **Draft release notes.** Two sections: external (plain English, ≤ 3 bullets, edited by the user before publishing) and internal (diff summary, AC list, ADR links, migration class, flag name, dashboard).
8. **Print deploy command.** Suggest the team's release-pipeline trigger, or the `dotnet publish -c Release` / container image build-and-push line, plus the `dotnet ef migrations script --idempotent` output to apply first. The agent never executes any of it.

## Refuse if
- `07-validation-report.md` verdict is not `PASS`.
- `08-code-review.md` verdict is not `Approve` or `Approve with waivers`.
- Any `Q-NNN` is unresolved in the spec or design.
- A migration in the diff is `breaking` and there is no covering ADR.
- A new endpoint, handler, or background service has no `ActivitySource` span and `Meter` registration in the diff.
- The diff edits a previously-released EF Core migration (a rename or a changed `Up`/`Down` body for a migration already applied in any environment).
- The OpenAPI contract diff reports a breaking change with no covering ADR and no versioning plan.
- The diff is empty (nothing to ship).

## Done when
`09-ship-plan.md` exists with all seven sections filled, every gate in the pre-ship table is `PASS`, migrations are classified with named rollback steps and an idempotent script, every new endpoint has at least one named metric and one alert (or a documented "no alert" reason), and release notes have both external and internal sections. The agent then prints the suggested deploy command for the user to execute manually — it never deploys.

# Ship Plan: <FEATURE-ID>

> Owner: `spring-code-reviewer` · Phase 8 · Skills: `shipping-and-launch`, `spring-security-baseline`, `flyway-or-liquibase-detection`
>
> Pre-deploy hygiene. The agent never deploys; it produces this plan and prints the deploy command for the user.

## Inputs

- Spec: `01-spec.md`
- Design: `03-design.md`, ADRs under `adr/`
- Tasks: `04-tasks.md`
- Validation: `07-validation-report.md` (verdict must be `PASS`)
- Code review: `08-code-review.md` (verdict must be `Approve` or `Approve with waivers`)
- Diff: <git range, e.g. `origin/main...HEAD`>

## 1. Pre-ship gates

| Gate | Source | Result | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Validation | `07-validation-report.md` | PASS / FAIL | <link> |
| Code review | `08-code-review.md` | Approve / Approve-with-waivers / FAIL | <link> |
| Open questions | spec + design `## Open Questions` | 0 / N | <list any> |
| Baseline regression | `.specs/_baseline.json` vs harness | none / N | <list any> |
| Diff scope | `files_in_scope` per task | in-scope / drift | <list any out-of-scope files> |

If any row is FAIL, **stop**. Do not fill the rest of this template.

## 2. Feature-flag posture

- **Flag name:** <name or `none — reason: ...`>
- **Default in production:** off / on
- **Kill-switch:** <env var or remote config key>
- **Owner:** <named human, not "the team">
- **Removal plan:** <date or condition for retiring the flag>

If `none`, justify in one line (e.g. "pure bug fix, additive only, covered by existing alert").

## 3. Migration safety

| Script | Class | Rollback procedure |
|---|---|---|
| `Vxxx__name.sql` | forward-only / expand / contract / breaking | <SQL or contract step> |

Constraints:

- [ ] No previously-released migration script was renamed or edited.
- [ ] Every `breaking` script has a covering ADR.
- [ ] Every `contract` step's matching `expand` has been in production for the agreed period.

## 4. Observability sign-off

For each new endpoint, handler, or scheduled task:

| Surface | Metric (Micrometer) | Structured-log key | Alert | Dashboard |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<METHOD> <path>` | `<metric.name>` (Timer w/ histogram) | `feature_id`, `ac_id` | <alert name + threshold> | <link> |

If a row has no alert, record the explicit reason in the row.

## 5. Rollback plan

1. **Detection.** How do we know it's broken? <alert name + threshold; user-report channel; metric anomaly>
2. **Stop the bleeding (≤ 5 min).** <flag flip; revert; scale-down; circuit breaker>
3. **State recovery.** <revert commit; replay events from offset N; reconcile job; manual SQL>

A `revert the commit` answer to (3) is incomplete when a migration ran — spell out the contract step or SQL.

## 6. Staged rollout

| Step | Cohort | Entry criteria | Abort criteria | Observation window | Watcher |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Canary | ~1% (1 instance) | gates green | error rate > X%, p95 > Y ms | 30 min | <on-call> |
| Step 1 | 10% | canary clean for window | same | 1 hr | <on-call> |
| Step 2 | 50% | step 1 clean | same | 4 hr | <on-call> |
| Full | 100% | step 2 clean | same | steady state | <on-call> |

Or run `docker compose down` to take the service offline.\n3. **State recovery.** Nothing to recover: there is no database, and the in-memory divisor and file list reset on restart (ADR-002). Users re-upload any files processed during the bad window; the divisor goes back to the default 3 and must be set again from the UI if it had been changed.\n\n## 6. Staged rollout\n\nSingle-instance only: the in-memory divisor and file store (ADR-002) make multiple instances inconsistent, so percentage canaries don't apply.\n\n| Step | Cohort | Entry criteria | Abort criteria | Observation window | Watcher |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| Deploy | the one container host (100%) | all gates above PASS; release tagged | `/health` not `Healthy` within 2 min; smoke test fails | — | Harpreet Ghotra |\n| Smoke test | the owner, on the host | containers `Up` | README sample output differs in lines 1–2; the upload doesn't return 201; the divisor can't be changed | 10 min | Harpreet Ghotra |\n| Steady state | all users | smoke test clean | any user-reported wrong change or failed upload | ongoing, manual | Harpreet Ghotra |\n\nSmoke test (on the host):\n\n```bash\ncurl -s http://localhost:8080/health                                   # Healthy\ncurl -s -F \"file=@samples/input.txt\" http://localhost:8080/api/files   # 201 + summary (note the id)\ncurl -s http://localhost:8080/api/files/<id>/output                    # 3 quarters,1 dime,3 pennies / 3 pennies / <random, totals 1.67>\n```\n\n## 7. Release notes\n\n### External (user-facing) — draft; please edit before publishing\n\n- Upload a transaction file (one `owed,paid` pair per line) and download the change to hand back for every line, e.g. `3 quarters,1 dime,3 pennies`.\n- When the amount owed in cents is divisible by the chosen number (3 by default), the change comes in random coins that still add up exactly; you can change that number on the page.\n- Invalid lines get a clear message in the output (e.g. \"amount paid is less than amount owed\") without stopping the rest of the file.\n\n### Internal (engineering)\n\n- **AC covered:** AC-001 to AC-013 and AC-015 to AC-029 (28 active; AC-014 withdrawn → DC-001).\n- **Diff summary:** A .NET 10 Minimal API module (`src/CashRegister`) with Currencies and Change slices: integer-cent money; priority-ordered change rules → strategies (minimal and random); strict line parser with per-line errors; a file processor (1000-line cap); in-memory file store and divisor. A thin host (`src/CashRegister.Api`) composed through `HostSetup` (ProblemDetails everywhere, health, CORS allow-list, OpenAPI in Development). A Vite + React 19 + TypeScript UI for upload, the file list with downloads, and the divisor setting. A quality harness (`.github/scripts/harness-dotnet.sh`), and Docker Compose to run the UI behind nginx next to the API.\n- **ADRs:** [ADR-001](adr/ADR-001-single-module-thin-host.md) · [ADR-002](adr/ADR-002-in-memory-state.md) · [ADR-003](adr/ADR-003-rules-and-strategies.md) · [ADR-004](adr/ADR-004-currency-registry-usd-only.md) · [ADR-005](adr/ADR-005-security-posture-v1.md) · [ADR-006](adr/ADR-006-vite-react-spa.md) · [ADR-007](adr/ADR-007-output-format-and-line-errors.md) · [ADR-008](adr/ADR-008-observability-v1.md) (amended) · [ADR-009](adr/ADR-009-build-harness-deviations.md)\n- **Migration class:** n/a (no database)\n- **Flag name:** `none`\n- **Dashboard:** none (OTel deferred; logs through `docker compose logs api`)\n- **Known limitations (v1):** no authentication; state lost on restart; single instance only; USD only; English output; uploads over 1 MB get a generic 400 (review F-002).\n- **Commits:** `git log 9b945d3..HEAD --oneline` (whole feature) · `git log origin/main..HEAD --oneline` (this push)\n\n## 8. Deploy command (for the user to run)\n\nOn the container host, from a checkout of the release:\n\n```bash\ngit fetch && git checkout <release-tag-or-sha>      # e.g. the merge commit of this branch\ndocker compose up -d --build                         # builds api + web, starts them\ndocker compose ps                                    # both services \"Up\"\ncurl -s http://localhost:8080/health                 # Healthy, then run the smoke test in section 6\n```\n\nBefore that, from your workstation, publish the branch and tag the release so rollback has a target:\n\n```bash\ngit push origin main\ngit tag -a v1.0.0 -m \"Cash register v1\" && git push origin v1.0.0\n```\n\nNo migration script to apply first (no database). The agent does not execute any of this; you run it.\n\n## Sign-off\n\n- [x] All gates PASS (instrumentation waived by ADR-008 amendment).\n- [x] Flag posture (none), alert posture (none, demo) and rollout (single host) confirmed by a human on 2026-09-22.\n- [ ] External release notes edited by a human.\n- [ ] On-call notified: n/a (no on-call); the owner watches the deploy.\n\nDate: 2026-09-22 · Approved-by: Harpreet Ghotra (pending: release-notes edit)\n"
}

## Assistant · 2026-09-22T15:10:25.052Z

Written for: the exercise reviewers at Creative Cash Draw Solutions who will read the pull request.

```markdown
# Cash Register: change calculator (.NET 10 API + React/TypeScript UI)

Upload a flat file of `owed,paid` lines and get back, for each line, the change to hand the customer (for example `3 quarters,1 dime,3 pennies`). Change uses the fewest coins, except when the amount owed in cents is divisible by 3: then the coins are random but still add up exactly.

## Try it

```bash
docker compose up --build
```

- UI: http://localhost:8080 (upload a file, download the result, change the divisor)
- API: http://localhost:5080
- Sample input: [`samples/input.txt`](samples/input.txt). Its output starts `3 quarters,1 dime,3 pennies` / `3 pennies`, and the third line is random but totals 1.67.

Without Docker: `dotnet run --project src/CashRegister.Api`, then `cd web && npm install && npm run dev`. See the README's **Solution** section.

## How it works

- **Money is whole cents** (`long`), never floating point.
- **Special cases are pluggable rules.** Each rule has a priority and says which change method to use; the lowest priority number wins, and minimal change is the fallback. "Divisible by 3 → random" is one rule.
- **Every input line gives exactly one output line.** A bad line (malformed, negative, paid < owed, too many decimals) gets a clear `Error: …` message, and the rest of the file is still processed. Blank lines are skipped; files over 1000 lines are rejected.
- **Structure:** one `CashRegister` module (Currencies and Change slices) behind a thin API host, and a small React app.

## Things to consider — answered

- **Changing the random divisor:** it's a runtime setting, changed from the UI (or `PUT /api/settings/divisor`) with no redeploy. Any whole number ≥ 1 is accepted, and the UI warns that 1 makes every transaction random.
- **Adding another special case:** write one new rule class (and a new change method if it needs one) and register it. No existing code changes; an architecture test keeps rules isolated.
- **A new client in France:** currencies are classes holding their code, decimal separator and denominations. EUR is one new class, one registration and a config value, and the parser already takes the decimal separator from the currency. Localised (French) output and choosing the currency per client are deliberately left for a later version.

## Testing

- 159 unit and 30 integration tests (xUnit v3), plus 30 UI tests (Vitest + React Testing Library).
- Unit coverage is 100% line and branch; the UI is 100% line and 90% branch.
- Also covered: architecture rules, and a performance test showing a 1000-line file processes well under 500 ms.
- One command runs every check (format, build, tests, coverage, API contract, dependency vulnerabilities, UI lint, build and tests): `./.github/scripts/harness-dotnet.sh`.

## Scope and known limitations (v1)

- No login; the divisor and uploaded files are kept in memory, so they reset on restart and only one API instance is supported.
- USD only; English output.
- An upload over 1 MB currently gets a generic "Bad Request" message.

The requirements, design decisions and build log are in [`.specs/2026-09-21-cash-register-change-calculation/`](.specs/2026-09-21-cash-register-change-calculation/). Start with `01-spec.md` and the `adr/` folder.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
```
